### Physical Appearance
Victor's appearance has changed substantially throughout the story as his physiology evolved from a chronically ill Human into a Vampire, Vampire Progenitor, Blood Dragon Primogenitor, Dragon God and eventually an existence possessing an Eldritch True Self. His earlier measurements represented genuine physical changes to his body, but after his Draconic and Divine evolutions Victor gained enough control over his physiology that his height, proportions and even the scale of his Dragon body became variable rather than permanently fixed.

#### Human
Before entering the supernatural world, Victor Walker was a thin and visibly unhealthy young man whose appearance reflected the chronic illness that had affected him throughout his life. He had short black hair, sapphire-blue eyes and unusually pale skin, standing approximately 175 centimeters tall while weighing only around 50 kilograms.[10][247] His extraordinarily rare RH-null blood was accompanied by severe chronic anemia, leaving his body underweight, physically frail and poorly suited for prolonged exertion. Although Victor genuinely enjoyed physical activity and wanted to participate in sports, strenuous exercise could place his health at serious risk and had to be carefully limited throughout his Human life.[229][72]

#### Vampire
Victor's transformation into a Vampire completely reconstructed the frail body he had possessed as a Human. His formerly thin, underweight frame became muscular and proportionally developed, his sickly complexion was replaced by the pale-white skin characteristic of Vampires and the chronic physical weakness produced by his anemia disappeared almost immediately.[247] His body continued maturing after the initial transformation rather than reaching its final state at once: Victor first grew to approximately 180 centimeters and, following months of supernatural development and intensive training, eventually reached approximately 195 centimeters in height.[247][58]
Although Victor normally retained a largely Human appearance, releasing more of his Vampiric nature caused increasingly obvious predatory characteristics to emerge. His ears sharpened, his sclerae turned black, his irises became blood-red, his pupils narrowed vertically and his fangs became considerably longer and more prominent.[65] These alterations first became especially pronounced when Victor stopped psychologically suppressing the instincts and aggression he had restrained throughout his Human life, causing his appearance to shift alongside the increase in power.[65] Continued use of his transformed state eventually left a permanent physical consequence: the sapphire-blue eyes of Victor Walker were replaced by the red eyes associated with his Vampiric existence.
Victor's monstrous Vampiric visage.
Extreme anger and Bloodlust could push this appearance substantially further. Rather than merely displaying sharpened Vampiric features, Victor could assume an almost monstrous visage in which portions of his face appeared swallowed by darkness, leaving intensely glowing red eyes and numerous sharp teeth visible within the obscured features.[248] This appearance became particularly noticeable during periods in which Victor's emotions and predatory instincts overwhelmed his otherwise controlled humanoid presentation.[22]
Victor's appearance continued developing alongside his rapidly evolving body. Following prolonged training, his originally short black hair grew to approximately shoulder length.[249] A considerably more noticeable change occurred after Victor absorbed [[Adonis Snow]]. His hair extended to approximately his waist, his facial features became more refined and his eyes shifted toward the violet coloration that would increasingly characterize his later appearances.[63] These changes did not mean Victor was physically becoming Adonis; the absorption incorporated Adonis' Blood, Soul, memories and other characteristics into Victor while Victor's own identity and appearance remained dominant. As his control over his body improved, the exact length of his hair and similar superficial characteristics also ceased being absolute features, since Victor could deliberately alter them through shapeshifting.[250]
Victor could additionally alter his appearance by emphasizing the different Noble Vampire Bloodlines contained within him. His Snow-associated state displayed the black sclerae, blood-red irises and vertical pupils characteristic of his more predatory transformation, while emphasizing the [[Fulger Bloodline]] could change his eyes toward a brilliant golden-yellow. Manifesting characteristics associated with the [[Scarlett Bloodline]] produced a substantially different coloration, including snow-white hair, unnaturally pale skin and ice-blue eyes. These Count transformations were not independent bodies or separate personalities, but specialized physical expressions of the different Bloodline characteristics incorporated into Victor during his abnormal transformation and subsequent development.
The humanoid appearance of Victor's body also became increasingly misleading as his supernatural constitution evolved. Despite retaining proportions outwardly comparable to an exceptionally muscular Human, his physical density eventually became enormous. During the period in which he existed as a Host to Roxanne and the power of a World Tree, Victor's humanoid body was described as weighing approximately 6,000–8,000 kilograms.[73] The extreme mass was contained within an otherwise Human-sized frame, reflecting how radically the composition of his muscles, bones and supernatural body had diverged from ordinary biological standards long before his later Draconic evolutions.

#### Demon King
Victor's appearance during his conquest and subsequent rule of Hell developed several characteristics directly associated with the enormous quantity of Miasma and Negative Energy circulating through his body. These changes did not represent a transformation into the Demon Race; when Hell accepted him as its ruler, Victor was still fundamentally the Second Vampire Progenitor, albeit one whose physiology and Soul had already been altered by years of consuming Demons, interacting with Hell's energies and hosting Roxanne. During the final stages of his conquest, his skin was described as becoming extremely pale, almost as though he were dead, while his eyes shone an intense blood-red.[61] His already long black hair was surrounded by a dense mass of Miasma, and his Greatsword was similarly enveloped in Pure Miasma as he led the conquered Demon Legions toward Hell's lower levels.[61]
The influence of Miasma became increasingly integrated into Victor's appearance rather than remaining merely an aura around him. When he entered the castle of the previous Demon King, his long black hair was visibly covered by constantly moving Pure Miasma.[23] After Hell acknowledged Victor as its legitimate sovereign, the enormous throne altered itself to accommodate him and changed into a black-and-red throne; [[Junketsu]] floated beside it while Victor sat upon it and inherited the knowledge and responsibilities associated with the Ruler of Hell.[23] This throne, the surrounding Miasma and Victor's increasingly unnatural complexion became recurring elements of his presentation as Hell's King.
Victor's mature Demon King of Tyranny appearance developed this theme even further. By this period, his hair was explicitly described as long hair composed of Pure Miasma rather than ordinary black hair merely surrounded by Demonic Energy. When Victor summoned his Royal Armor, his body became encased in armor while the Miasma forming his hair floated continuously around him. A black cloak also manifested over his shoulders, but unlike an ordinary piece of clothing, this cloak was formed entirely from Pure, Unaltered Miasma; physical contact with it was itself dangerous because of the nature of the Energy composing it.[168]
Consequently, Victor's Demon King appearance is best understood as the increasingly infernal presentation of his existing body rather than a separate Demonic species transformation: corpse-like pale skin, intense blood-red eyes, long or Miasma-formed black hair, Royal Armor and an ever-present mantle of darkness and Miasma surrounding both himself and his weapons. His appearance would continue evolving after his later Draconic transformations, but those subsequent changes belong to his Blood Dragon and Divine forms rather than the original state in which he conquered Hell.

#### Dragon Rider
Victor's Dragon Rider state began after he formed a complete spiritual bond with [[Zaladrac Zeovnur Elderblood]]. The bond initially allowed the two to share their senses, but as their connection deepened it began producing genuine physical changes in both of them.[91] Victor did not obtain his violet eye color from Zaladrac—the color had already become part of his appearance before their bond. Instead, his eyes acquired increasingly Draconic characteristics: his pupils became noticeably thinner and more reptilian, while his vision developed the perception naturally possessed by Dragons.[251][85] Zaladrac changed in the opposite direction, with her original coloration shifting toward Victor's own; her scales became dark violet and her eyes similarly developed a deep violet coloration as their bond strengthened.[251]
The clearest physical manifestation of the bond was Victor's ability to cover his body in a second skin of Draconic scales. These dark-violet scales formed over his existing Vampire body like natural armor rather than replacing his flesh, dramatically increasing the durability of areas they covered.[251] This distinction is important to Victor's later evolution: during the Dragon Rider stage, the Dragon scales were something his body manifested over itself. During the battle at [[Olympus]], his constant regeneration and adaptation eventually progressed to the point where newly formed flesh was itself composed of Dragon scales, marking the beginning of the permanent fusion between his Vampiric and Draconic physiology.[162]
Other aspects of Victor's body also became progressively more Draconic even when no scales were visible. His lungs, heart, instincts and sensory organs were altered through the connection with Zaladrac, allowing him to reproduce abilities such as a Dragon's enhanced vision and Draconic Breath.[252][223] By this period even powerful Divine observers could perceive something distinctly Dragon-like in Victor's gaze, with his violet eyes giving the impression of an enraged Dragon when he focused upon someone.[85] These characteristics remained layered onto the body of the Vampire Progenitor rather than constituting an independent Dragon body.
The Dragon Rider state therefore represents the transitional stage between Victor's existence as the Second Vampire Progenitor and his later Blood Dragon physiology. He possessed a Vampire body increasingly modified by a genuine Dragon connection—reptilian violet eyes, summonable dark-violet scales, altered organs and Draconic senses—but the two racial systems had not yet completely merged. That distinction disappeared during the Olympus conflict, when repeated destruction and regeneration caused Victor's Vampire Progenitor and Dragon traits to fuse permanently into a single new existence.[194][5]

#### Blood Dragon Primogenitor
Victor's transformation into the Blood Dragon Primogenitor occurred during the battle surrounding [[Olympus]], after his body was repeatedly destroyed by the combined pressure of [[Erebus]]' gravity and attacks from [[Nocturnus]]. His regeneration continuously rebuilt him to endure the damage, but the regenerated body was no longer identical to the one being destroyed. Whereas the scales obtained through his earlier Dragon Rider state had functioned as a layer covering his Vampiric body, the newly regenerated tissue became fundamentally Draconic—Victor's own skin had become Dragon scales. His [[Dragon Heart]], the adaptive characteristics remaining from his Human origin, Roxanne's Negative Energy and the Draconic existence developing within him collectively drove the transformation until his Vampire Progenitor and Dragon characteristics began permanently merging.[162]
The change became externally visible as Victor's Progenitor and Draconic features fused into a single humanoid body. His coloration took on a dark-red hue mixed with violet, horns emerged from his head and two enormous Dragon wings grew from his back. His scales became predominantly violet with smaller crimson tones, while his Draconic eyes retained their violet coloration but increasingly displayed crimson within their glow.[162] His long black hair remained composed of or enveloped by Miasma, continuing the characteristic he had developed as the Demon King.[5] Victor's humanoid height stabilized at approximately 200 centimeters, but almost every part of this seemingly Human-sized body had become a natural weapon due to the permanent integration of Draconic physiology.[162]
The physical transformation reflected an equally fundamental change within Victor's Soul. As his two racial natures merged, a gigantic Dragon manifestation formed within his Inner World, possessing scales compared to the starry night of a galaxy. Roxanne initially distinguished this presence from Zaladrac and realized that it was Victor's own Soul evolving toward a genuine Draconic existence rather than merely borrowing characteristics from his wife.[162] The process was completed after Victor consumed [[Tartarus (Realm)|Tartarus]], causing an eruption of red and violet Energy and fully fusing the Draconic and Vampiric characteristics of his Progenitor Form.[5] His long Miasma-like black hair, violet pupils carrying crimson tones and enormous wings remained visible when the completed transformation emerged.[5]
The resulting Being was no longer classified as the Second Vampire Progenitor who happened to possess Dragon characteristics. The Primordial authorities recognized Victor as the Primogenitor of the Draconic Vampires, described as a Progenitor standing above the existing Dragon and Vampire subspecies and as the First, Beginning and origin of a completely new lineage.[5][6] This distinction is physically important: from this point onward, Victor's horns, scales, wings, Dragon organs and other Draconic characteristics were not transformations temporarily superimposed over a Vampire body. They were components of his natural physiology.
Immediately afterward, Victor continued using this primarily humanoid Draconic form. When issuing his orders for the fall of Olympus, his wings were described as spreading to a diameter of more than 50 meters, dwarfing his approximately two-meter body, while violet Energy containing shades of red surrounded him.[253] He could retract those wings when necessary and otherwise maintain a compact humanoid appearance despite possessing the physiology of the newly born Primogenitor.
The 500-meter Dragon body sometimes associated with Victor should not be treated as the original size of this Blood Dragon transformation. Victor's canonically described 500-meter True Dragon form was established later during his ascension to Godhood, when his Dragon body initially attempted to expand beyond planetary dimensions before he deliberately compressed it to 500 meters for greater density and control.[186] Much later, Victor demonstrated that he could reduce that body to approximately 100 meters as a convenient minimum size or enlarge it far beyond 500 meters through shapeshifting.[13] Those later sizes therefore belong to Victor's mature True Dragon and Divine development rather than the initial Blood Dragon Primogenitor appearance born during the Olympus conflict.

#### God
Victor's ascension into Godhood did not discard the Blood Dragon body he had acquired during the destruction of [[Olympus]]. Instead, his existing Draconic physiology, [[Dragon Heart]], Soul and newly awakened Divinities evolved together. As Victor crossed the threshold into a Higher Existence, the accumulated paths that had defined him—Vampire Progenitor, Dragon, Demon King, martial artist and ruler—began manifesting as Divine Concepts, ultimately producing fifteen Divinities and establishing the existence identified as the Dragon God of [[Chaos]].[186][12]
The most significant physical development of this ascension was Victor's complete access to his True Dragon body. When it first manifested, the form continued expanding until its size exceeded that of a planet. Victor considered such dimensions unnecessarily inconvenient and deliberately compressed the body to approximately 500 meters, increasing the concentration and density of his power while retaining the same fundamental Draconic existence.[186] This 500-meter state was not another independent transformation or a fixed maximum size; it was the scale Victor deliberately chose for his newly awakened True Dragon body. The form was recognized within his own Soul as one of his natural appearances, although Victor initially lacked sufficient experience controlling such an enormous anatomy and commonly returned to a humanoid manifestation when the full body was unnecessary.[186]
Victor's Divine Dragon appearance retained the Western Draconic structure originating from his Blood Dragon evolution but became considerably more abnormal. His body carried the dark coloration and violet influence associated with his established Draconic physiology, while the form possessed multiple eyes rather than conforming completely to the anatomy of an ordinary Dragon.[12] The enormous quantity of Energy contained inside the form was itself extraordinary; his existence had become sufficiently saturated with supernatural power that even remaining inactive for prolonged periods could influence the surrounding environment on astronomical scales. [[The Universal Tree]] consequently identified him as a Chaos Dragon God, reflecting that Victor's newly Divine Draconic existence contained powers connected to both Positivity and Negativity rather than belonging exclusively to one side of the cosmic Balance.[186][12]
Godhood also made the separation between Victor's familiar physical body and the much stranger existence beneath it increasingly visible. His ascension produced moments in which his appearance ceased conforming completely to recognizable Human or Dragon anatomy, with the emergence of multiple eyes and other unnatural characteristics hinting at something far more alien than an ordinary Divine Dragon.[12] This should not be confused with the later fully revealed Eldritch manifestation itself. Victor did not consciously understand that deeper existence during the initial ascension; only afterward, within the deepest regions of his Soul, did he encounter the incomprehensible Being he would eventually recognize as his own True Self.[237][71]
Unlike the comparatively stable measurements associated with Victor's earlier Human and Vampire bodies, his post-Godhood humanoid height is no longer fixed. His developed Shapeshifting and Draconic physiology allow him to alter the dimensions of the body through which he interacts with others. This becomes especially clear in the later Imperial era: during the investigation of [[Nikolai Francis Nichev]], Victor appeared before War and the Heralds in a humanoid body approximately 5.50 meters tall.[46] That height was a form chosen for the meeting, not a new fixed measurement of his body.
Later appearances demonstrate the same variability in the opposite direction. When Victor deliberately approached [[Tyche]] without the overwhelming presentation associated with the Emperor, he reduced himself to approximately 190 centimeters, appearing much closer to the Vampire body he had used earlier in his life, with short black hair and violet eyes.[64] His enormous Imperial manifestations and smaller humanoid appearances should consequently not be treated as separate permanent heights. By this stage, physical scale had become another characteristic Victor could adjust according to circumstance, ranging from Human-sized manifestations to Divine humanoid bodies several meters tall and ultimately to a True Dragon body whose later development would reach astronomical proportions.

#### True Dragon
Victor's True Dragon Form is his genuine Draconic body and, unlike his humanoid manifestations, its natural scale has repeatedly increased as Victor himself has grown stronger. The different measurements shown throughout the story therefore do not represent separate Dragon transformations. They are successive stages in the development of the same body, with Victor retaining enough Shapeshifting control to compress it whenever its unrestricted size would be inconvenient.
The first complete manifestation of this body occurred during Victor's ascension to Godhood. His Dragon body initially expanded from hundreds to thousands of meters and continued growing until it exceeded the size of an entire planet. Victor deliberately reversed that expansion and compressed himself to approximately 500 meters, reasoning that concentrating the same existence into a smaller body would give it greater density and make it considerably easier to control.[186] The resulting 500-meter Dragon was described as Victor's true appearance registered within his Soul and the form in which his Draconic existence naturally felt most comfortable, although his complete lack of experience controlling such an enormous body caused him to return to humanoid form shortly afterward.[186]
As Victor became accustomed to his new physiology, even the 500-meter body became something he could resize freely rather than an absolute measurement. During a later transformation he remained at approximately 100 meters because of the restricted space around him; the narration explicitly identified this as his practical minimum at the time and noted that his normal full size remained approximately 500 meters.[13] Victor could already become substantially larger through shapeshifting—including planetary dimensions if he wished—but during this stage the 500-meter configuration represented the compact form in which he concentrated his Draconic power rather than allowing his body to expand without purpose.[13]
That scale changed drastically as Victor's Divinities and overall existence matured. When he deliberately tested how large his body could naturally become, Victor first grew to several times the size of [[Jupiter]], continued expanding until he was larger than the entire Solar System and finally stopped at a scale where the Solar System could effectively be held within one of his hands.[67] At that point he manifested as an enormous black Dragon with violet hues. His physical presence was already massive enough to disturb the surrounding balance of Space, forcing Victor to compensate for the distortions produced simply by existing at that scale.[67] This demonstrated that the original 500-meter limit had ceased to represent the natural extent of his Dragon body; his increasing power was being reflected directly in the size that body could sustain.
An even greater transformation followed after Victor understood Attributeless Energy and reorganized his powers around a single fundamental Energy rather than maintaining numerous different Energy systems simultaneously. The change affected not only the efficiency of his abilities but the development of his body itself. Victor's True Dragon had become much larger than entire galaxies, to the point that the narration stated he could swallow galaxies if he desired.[68] His mature appearance remained that of an immense Black Western Dragon carrying pronounced violet hues, with eyes glowing crimson-violet.[68] His body possessed such tremendous natural weight within the fabric of Space that stars, planets and black holes began being drawn toward him merely through his presence; Victor had to alter Reality around himself to prevent those celestial bodies from being displaced.[68]
Victor continued demonstrating this Galactic scale during the preparations for the coming Upper-Sector conflict. When he stopped restraining his growth while organizing the [[Elderblood Empire]] across the Sector, his Dragon body passed the size of an entire Solar System and continued expanding until it was larger than a galaxy.[74] This was no longer portrayed as an exceptional one-time enlargement. The scale had become compatible with Victor's ordinary cosmic operations: while occupying that form he simultaneously perceived [[World Trees]] throughout the Sector, reorganized Galactic infrastructure and manipulated astronomical structures without the Dragon body itself becoming an obstacle.[74]
The nearly 200,000 years of accelerated Imperial development widened the difference even further. Near the end of that era, Victor described scales removed from his primary body as originating from a True Dragon whose unrestricted dimensions now surpassed several galaxies.[135] The scales themselves retained the properties of that immense main body despite appearing as small objects after Victor reduced them for his daughters, illustrating that his smaller manifestations did not represent regression in his actual physical development.[135]
The clearest late-era description appears during Victor's confrontation with the System. Victor entered what the narration explicitly calls his fully developed Dragon form, a body larger than entire galaxies.[69] Its physical scale had become so extreme that each of Victor's individual Dragon eyes was described as being approximately the size of an entire Solar System.[69] His body's natural gravity was likewise powerful enough that neighboring galaxies would be thrown into chaos simply by his unrestricted presence if Victor did not continuously control its effects.[69] He later manifested the same galaxy-surpassing Dragon body while extending his influence over the smaller Sectors surrounding his domain.[244]
That body was not only present for the merger. Once Arcane, [[Nightingale]] and Samar were inside the Mid-Level Sector, Victor kept the Dragon and used it to rebuild the Galactic layout. The form dwarfed ordinary galaxies, closed around entire spiral galaxies, and moved them — billions of stars, with the Solar Systems and the orbits inside them left as they were.[254] The populations of the three worlds could already see that Dragon across the sky while the Sectors were being drawn in.[244]
He used it again when he answered War in person. After War refused to be handed to any of the patrons, Victor appeared as that giant Dragon holding an entire galaxy. Light, Darkness and the Emperor-aligned patron all turned toward the body. Darkness had found Negativity.[246] Nothing in that appearance places him past the multi-galactic size already reached. It is the same True Dragon, brought into the open against the Upper-Sector factions, with no new color, eye or limb measurement.
Victor's Draconic growth can therefore be followed directly through the novel: his True Dragon initially expanded beyond planetary size before being compressed to 500 meters;[186] he later used approximately 100–500 meter configurations while learning to control the form;[13] his matured body then grew from Jupiter-scale to beyond an entire Solar System;[67] eventually surpassed galaxies after his adoption of Attributeless Energy;[68] and, following the enormous Imperial time-acceleration era, developed into a body exceeding multiple galaxies with Solar-System-sized eyes.[135][69] He has since moved intact galaxies in that form,[254] and appeared holding one galaxy when he entered the fight beyond the barrier.[246] These are not distinct transformations, but chronological stages in the physical maturation of the same True Dragon body as Victor's power, Energy capacity and level of existence continued increasing.

#### Outer God
Victor's Eldritch appearance cannot be accurately represented by conventional humanoid or Draconic anatomy. When Victor perceived the entity existing within the deepest part of himself, he instinctively understood that it was not a parasite, possession or independent creature, but another manifestation of his own existence—his True Self.[71] The [[Heavenly Father]] later put the same distinction in plainer terms. On the outside, Victor is a Blood Dragon. Internally, he is a Cosmic Horror.[224]
The dream in which he met that self did give it a depiction. It was drawn in violet, crimson and black, with enormous numbers of eyes, vast mouths and tentacle-like structures, and no stable conventional anatomy. Individual eyes were described on scales exceeding galaxies, and its movement and voice interacted with or erased surrounding Galactic structures.[71][70] That depiction is what the dream could show. It is not a finished body, and it is not the only way the form has been met.
Hela did not see that anatomy. When she tried to use Time on him, she was pulled into a dark space filled with galaxy-sized spheres and met an Eldritch Victor who had no form. That presence was guarding his past and the past of his wives. It spoke of the [[Akashic Records]] and of outsiders from other realities.[99] The two meetings are not a contradiction the novel resolves into one shape. One witness gets eyes, mouths and tentacles. The other gets no body at all.
The Nightmare Form is not a single copy of him either. It exists in two versions. One is inside the Akashic Records and is his present self. The other is outside them, and that one safeguards his past and the past of his wives.[217] He has also used the Nightmare Form as a working state rather than only as something seen in a dream: when [[Yog-Sothoth]] was born, that form is what he used to hold her influence on Reality.[255] His clones later draw on the same name as a power, alongside Creation, Dream and Reality, when they make minions. That use is not a second description of the body.[256]
A cosmic horror shown to someone else is not the same thing as this form being fully present. When [[Odin]] provoked him, Victor answered with murderous intent and a cosmic horror vision.[37] The vision is what Odin was made to see. It is not a measurement of the True Self, and it does not add eyes, limbs or a size the other scenes did not already give.
Showing the Eldritch Form is also worse than merely looking at Victor. An ordinary Mortal who perceives him without restraint can die from the weight of the information, and exposing the Eldritch Form makes that worse.[105] Even his wives needed protective Runes when the memories in front of them carried his unrestricted Eldritch existence.[140] This form still has no fixed height, length or volume. The galaxy-sized spheres Hela entered are the space around the formless presence, not a length of the body.

#### Regular Appearance
In ordinary family, social and diplomatic situations, Victor generally prefers to interact through a humanoid body rather than manifesting his enormous True Dragon body or his deeper Eldritch existence. By the late Imperial era, however, this humanoid appearance no longer possesses a single biologically fixed height, hairstyle or exact configuration. Victor's advanced Shapeshifting allows him to alter superficial characteristics and the scale of his body according to circumstance without the change representing a new transformation.[257]
Despite that freedom, Victor normally remains immediately recognizable. Black is still his preferred hair color, while his eyes are generally violet or crimson-violet depending upon how strongly his Draconic and supernatural characteristics are being expressed. When he personally appeared before Kali and [[Shiva]] during the incident involving his Human ancestor, Victor manifested with long hair composed of Pure Miasma and eyes glowing crimson-violet, retaining visual characteristics originating from both his Demon King and later Draconic development.[14] In less imposing circumstances he can suppress those traits almost completely. While spending private time with [[Tyche]], Victor deliberately appeared much closer to his former Vampire self, wearing a black-and-white suit with short black hair and violet eyes.[64]
His clothing has remained similarly consistent even as his body has changed. Victor continues to strongly favor black and white rather than colorful clothing. During a family gathering he entered wearing black trousers, black sneakers with white details and a white long-sleeved shirt, with the narration explicitly noting that his preference for black and white had remained unchanged throughout his life.[108] His Imperial clothing and armor can be substantially more elaborate when the situation demands it, but his casual appearance remains comparatively simple.
Victor's humanoid height is now just as variable as his hairstyle. During the same family gathering, he deliberately maintained a height of approximately three meters. Several of his daughters had themselves grown to or beyond ordinary Human heights, with some exceeding two meters, and Victor enlarged himself specifically so that he would not be physically buried when they all rushed to embrace him.[108] The size was therefore a conscious convenience rather than a new permanent height.
The opposite is demonstrated during his courtship with Tyche. Victor reduced his humanoid body to approximately 190 centimeters, only slightly taller than her, while presenting himself in the smaller Vampire-like appearance he considered appropriate for their private interaction.[64] In other circumstances he has manifested humanoid or anthropomorphic bodies several meters tall, demonstrating that measurements such as 190 centimeters, three meters or the larger Imperial manifestations are selected scales rather than successive permanent growth stages.
Victor's regular appearance should therefore be understood as his preferred social manifestation rather than a separate biological form. He normally presents himself as a recognizable humanoid man with black hair and violet eyes, frequently dressed in black and white, but the length and supernatural nature of his hair, the crimson influence in his eyes and even his total height can be changed according to his intentions.[14][108][64] His humanoid body, enlarged Imperial manifestations and galaxy-surpassing True Dragon body are consequently not contradictory physical descriptions; by the current era, Victor can deliberately choose the scale and presentation through which others perceive him.

### Personality
Victor is best understood not as someone whose personality was repeatedly replaced by his transformations, but as an intensely self-directed individual whose supernatural evolution progressively removed the limitations that once restrained him. Pride, possessiveness, competitiveness, curiosity, vindictiveness, affection, ambition and a powerful desire for personal freedom were already present while he was Human; becoming a Vampire amplified those traits and finally gave him the physical and social freedom to express them openly. What changes most throughout the story is therefore not who Victor is, but how much control, experience and responsibility he develops over characteristics that were present from the beginning.[229][65][258]
As a Human, Victor was far more restrained than his later reputation would suggest. His illness left him physically incapable of acting upon many of his impulses and ambitions, something he deeply resented. He was stubborn enough to refuse help with personal grievances even when people close to him could have intervened, regarding problems such as [[Luan Davis]]' bullying as matters he needed to resolve himself.[229] His resentment could last for years, and once Vampirism gave him the strength he had previously lacked, he deliberately humiliated Luan rather than simply forgetting the past.[259] At the same time, Victor's pride did not erase his gratitude toward those he loved. He remained deeply conscious of what [[Leon Walker]] and Anna Walker had sacrificed while raising a chronically ill child and rejected the idea that newfound supernatural independence gave him the right to become ungrateful toward his parents.[109]
Vampirism did not create an entirely new personality so much as remove many of the social and physical restraints surrounding the old one. During his confrontation with [[Corneliu Funar]], Victor recognized that part of his comparatively ordinary Human behavior had functioned as a mask developed to coexist peacefully despite his frustrations and limitations.[65] Once he possessed a body capable of surviving the consequences of his actions, he became far more willing to express his pride, aggression, possessiveness and desires directly. Victor eventually summarized his own attitude without attempting to portray himself as conventionally selfless: he considered himself a selfish and greedy Vampire who pursued what he wanted.[258] This does not mean that Victor is incapable of restraint or morality; rather, he prefers a personal code built around his own [[Will Solace|Will]], relationships and responsibilities instead of automatically accepting whatever morality, law, hierarchy or tradition another society places before him.
This extreme emphasis on personal Will is one of Victor's most consistent characteristics. He strongly dislikes allowing status, tradition or the expectations of others to decide what he is permitted to desire. This appears very early in his relationships, when he refuses to discard Sasha simply because accepting her as another wife would be socially complicated, and repeatedly encourages the people around him to acknowledge what they themselves actually want instead of passively living according to expectations imposed upon them.[163][260] His encouragement can be aggressive, and Victor frequently pushes people toward choices he believes will make them stronger or freer, but he gradually learns that protecting someone does not give him the right to make every deeply personal decision for them.
This distinction becomes particularly important with Sasha and [[Maria Elderblood]]. Victor eventually recognized that his earlier instinct had been to solve Sasha's pain through his own preferred form of retaliation. When Maria's fate became uncertain, however, Victor acknowledged that deciding whether Maria should die, be forgiven, punished or remain beside Sasha ultimately belonged to Sasha herself. He could protect his wife and destroy anyone attempting to force a decision upon her, but he did not want his own power to turn him into a tyrant toward the very people he claimed to protect.[261] This is one of the clearest developments in Victor's possessiveness: he never stops regarding his loved ones as his, but he becomes increasingly capable of distinguishing between protecting their freedom and replacing their freedom with his own decisions.
The same principle appears in his treatment of people such as [[Bruna Elderblood]] and [[Eve Elderblood]]. Victor is fully capable of extreme violence against those who abuse the powerless, yet he does not simply reduce the victims he rescues into passive objects requiring his decisions. Bruna was given the opportunity to decide whether she wanted revenge against those who had abused and sold her, while Eve was offered a path away from the life in which she had been treated as less than Human.[262][263][264] Victor's empathy is therefore highly personal rather than universally gentle. He can respond compassionately to someone he considers a victim while, in the same situation, showing almost no sympathy toward the person he identifies as the abuser.
Victor's relationship with strength is equally central to his personality. His first meeting with [[Scathach]] established a pattern that persists throughout the novel: his instincts correctly recognized her as an overwhelmingly superior predator and initially reacted with fear, yet that fear rapidly transformed into excitement because Victor had discovered someone capable of showing him how much stronger he could become.[16] He genuinely enjoys battle, especially against opponents who reveal unfamiliar techniques, superior mastery or a level of strength he has not yet reached. Scathach's training reinforces this trait while simultaneously teaching him that Bloodlust and instinct are tools to control rather than masters that should dictate his actions.[214]
His battle obsession should consequently not be confused with simple reliance upon overwhelming power. Victor is extraordinarily confident, but one of the reasons that confidence does not normally become complete complacency is his willingness to identify his own deficiencies. When training against several members of Clan Scarlett, he recognized shortcomings in his ability to manage multiple coordinated opponents and responded by expanding his weapon training rather than dismissing the weaknesses because he had greater raw power.[60][265][266] The pattern continues much later. After his body fundamentally changed through his evolution as a Blood Dragon, Victor deliberately returned to basic movement and combat training because centuries of mastery with a humanoid Vampire body did not automatically make him equally skilled with wings, claws, a tail and an altered center of balance.[267] Victor is proud of his talent, but he repeatedly treats talent without continuous refinement as wasted potential.
This contributes to his intolerance for complacency. Victor respects people who continue trying to improve even when they begin from comparatively weak positions and becomes frustrated when highly gifted individuals waste opportunities available to them. He applies this standard to himself, his soldiers, friends, wives and eventually his children. His methods can be severe because he considers weakness created through deliberate laziness more objectionable than weakness created through circumstances beyond someone's control. Even in the late Imperial era he supports Scathach's notoriously harsh training because his daughters were born with overwhelming natural advantages and still needed the discipline required to control their power, survive independently and protect one another.[108][268]
The emotional center of Victor's personality is nevertheless his family. His definition of family is based more upon accepted bonds than biology alone. Wives, parents, children, maids, adopted relatives and other individuals he has consciously accepted can all enter the circle he treats as an extension of himself. Once someone occupies that position, Victor's attachment becomes intensely possessive. When Scathach challenged him with the possibility that political authority could allow someone to take Sasha away from him, Victor's answer was effectively that he would become powerful enough to destroy whoever attempted it.[240] The scale of this mentality expands throughout the story, but the underlying principle changes very little: external authority loses legitimacy in Victor's eyes the moment it requires him to willingly abandon someone he considers his own.
Victor's possessiveness is reciprocal rather than purely acquisitive. Calling someone his also means that Victor regards their safety, development and well-being as his responsibility. This is why a maid such as Kaguya ceases to be a disposable servant once Victor accepts her personally; sacrificing her simply because it would benefit another member of the household becomes unacceptable because Kaguya herself has become part of that household.[230] The same mentality eventually extends beyond the immediate family toward soldiers, servants and citizens under his authority, although family consistently remains the innermost and most important layer of that hierarchy.
His affection toward people inside that circle can be strikingly gentle when compared with his behavior toward enemies. Victor listens to the emotional problems of his wives, reassures them physically and verbally, enjoys ordinary domestic interaction and later becomes an extraordinarily indulgent father. Around his daughters, the Emperor capable of terrifying Pantheons readily allows himself to be climbed on, surrounded and monopolized for attention.[101][108] His wives repeatedly accuse him of spoiling the girls, and the accusation is largely justified; nevertheless, Victor still intervenes when their behavior crosses from harmless competition into genuine hostility, explicitly teaching them that members of the family are expected to protect one another rather than seriously attack each other.[108]
The opposite side of this attachment is Victor's capacity for extraordinary vindictiveness. His moral framework is heavily based upon reciprocity: kindness is remembered, loyalty is rewarded, betrayal is difficult to forgive and deliberate hostility—especially toward his family—is often answered far beyond the original scale of the offense. Victor eventually summarizes the principle as "An eye for an eye. A tooth for a tooth. Blood for blood", adding that kindness shown to them will not be forgotten while hostility will be returned a hundredfold.[182] This philosophy explains why the same person can be exceptionally generous toward a loyal subordinate and deliberately cruel toward someone who has betrayed his trust.
Victor is therefore capable of sadism and punitive violence without considering those qualities incompatible with affection or leadership. He has tortured enemies, publicly displayed punishments as warnings and participated in exterminations when he concluded that a hostile group represented an unacceptable danger.[269] He does not generally portray himself as a conventional hero and rarely pretends that revenge is motivated by abstract justice when the real reason is personal. At the same time, this cruelty is not indiscriminately directed at everyone outside his family. Victor can respect enemies, spare opponents he considers worthy and recruit former adversaries when their conduct gives him a reason to do so. War, for example, earned enough respect during their battle that Victor allowed him to survive rather than consuming his Soul after victory.[270][271]
His experiences in Hell further erode the importance he assigns to racial stereotypes. Victor eventually stops treating the question of whether Demons are "naturally evil" as particularly meaningful. A Demon who behaves loyally or possesses qualities Victor respects can be accepted, while a Human, Vampire or God who acts monstrously receives no moral protection merely because their Race has a better reputation.[232][272][273][274] This practical judgment of individuals by conduct, loyalty and usefulness later contributes to the formation of a civilization containing races that historically regarded one another as enemies.
Victor's development as a ruler follows a similar transition from instinct to controlled application. His earliest solution to most dangerous problems is personal confrontation: find the threat, overpower it and eliminate it. The absorption of [[Adonis Snow]] changes this considerably because Victor inherits approximately seventeen centuries of memories belonging to a man who survived primarily through information, politics, manipulation and careful preparation rather than physical supremacy.[62][63] When Clan Snow falls into crisis, Victor uses that experience not only to identify and execute conspirators but also to reorganize intelligence, administration and inefficient internal structures after the killing ends.[269][275][276] The event marks an important change: Victor begins learning that winning a battle and successfully governing what remains afterward are fundamentally different problems.
Centuries of warfare and rule in Hell accelerate that maturation. Instead of spending the entire period merely slaughtering Demons, Victor recruits useful enemies, organizes conquered Legions and eventually develops an actual power structure beneath himself.[232][192][179] His later government continues this tendency. Victor prefers capable specialists to perform tasks in which they possess greater expertise rather than forcing every decision through himself; Velnorah, for example, is allowed considerable freedom in technological and civilizational development precisely because Victor recognizes that her knowledge in those fields exceeds his own.[76][277][278] Becoming Emperor therefore does not make Victor less dominant, but it does make him considerably more willing to delegate.
He also becomes increasingly conscious that loyalty is not produced solely through fear. Victor can be brutally unforgiving toward betrayal while still thanking subordinates for competent service, recognizing accomplishments and treating servants as living people rather than disposable machines. This remains visible even after his rise to an almost incomprehensible level of authority; when his Heralds successfully completed an assignment during his investigation of [[Nikolai Francis Nichev]], Victor personally thanked them, a habit he had retained despite possessing absolute authority over them.[46] His rule consequently combines overwhelming personal sovereignty with a strong emphasis on usefulness, competence, loyalty and recognition.
Despite becoming increasingly politically sophisticated, Victor never becomes emotionally detached in the manner often associated with ancient rulers. His ascension into Godhood makes this particularly explicit: several of the Divinities awakened from his own life correspond directly to characteristics that had already defined him, including Revenge, Martial Honor, [[Rex Invictus|Home]], Family and even Yandere.[186] Rather than Godhood replacing Victor's personality with an abstract Divine mentality, his personality itself becomes part of the conceptual foundation of his Divinity.
Victor displays the same acceptance toward the increasingly inhuman aspects of his existence. Alter was ultimately accepted as a missing portion of himself rather than an evil personality that needed to be destroyed; their final integration caused Victor to describe himself as complete.[168] Later, when Victor consciously encounters the incomprehensible Eldritch Being residing within the deepest region of his Soul, his reaction is similar. He recognizes the entity not as a parasite or invader but as another version of himself—his True Self—and accepts that identity rather than attempting to deny it because it no longer resembles the Human Victor Walker.[71] A recurring element of Victor's development is therefore integration: when confronted with a new part of himself, his instinct is usually to understand it, master it and incorporate it into his identity.
This does not mean Victor lacks internal contradictions. He values freedom while ruling an Empire beneath his absolute sovereignty; he is possessive while increasingly learning to respect the agency of those he loves; he enjoys violence while spending enormous effort creating a safe civilization for his family; he can be extraordinarily indulgent yet demands continuous self-improvement; and he describes himself as selfish while repeatedly assuming responsibilities that force him to consider the lives of people far beyond his immediate household. These apparent contradictions are not separate personalities. They reflect the hierarchy through which Victor interprets the world: his Will and family come first, followed by those he has accepted under his protection, while enemies and outsiders are judged according to their actions toward those circles.
His later caution is one of the clearest examples of how experience modifies that hierarchy without fundamentally changing it. The younger Victor was willing to personally enter dangerous situations simply because they interested him or promised a worthwhile fight. The Emperor eventually reaches a point where such behavior would risk not merely his own life but the Souls, connections, [[World Trees]], dimensions and countless people tied to his existence. Before investigating civilizations beyond his Sector, Victor therefore creates an independent Energy clone modeled deliberately upon a younger, more reckless version of himself, preserving the old Victor's aggression and appetite for battle while keeping the original and his family protected from unknown forms of retaliation.[141] The existence of the clone demonstrates that Victor himself understands the difference: the recklessness remains part of his personality, but the ruler he has become can no longer afford to indulge it without calculation.
Fatherhood reinforces this change more strongly than political authority alone. Victor is almost incapable of emotional detachment where his children are concerned and is significantly more indulgent than many of his wives consider healthy.[101][108] Yet his protectiveness does not completely eliminate his belief in growth through difficulty. He supports training that teaches his daughters discipline and self-defense, even while frequently moderating Scathach when her definition of "training" becomes excessive.[108][268] The resulting parenting style reflects Victor's broader personality: he wants his children safe, loved and free to develop individual lives, but he also wants them strong enough that their safety does not depend entirely upon him.
The priority Victor places upon family remains absolute even after he becomes responsible for an entire civilization. This reaches its clearest expression when the System proposes that [[Moira Eutychia Elderblood]] assume a cosmic role connected to Destiny. Victor believes accepting the role could eventually reduce his daughter into a mechanism serving the Universe rather than allowing her to remain an individual. When the System asks whether he would truly risk trillions of lives and Reality itself rather than sacrifice one person, Victor answers yes.[69] Importantly, he immediately rejects the assumption that protecting Moira requires abandoning everyone else: Victor argues that his Soul and Personal Universe could shelter enormous populations during a genuine cosmic catastrophe and begins considering alternatives rather than accepting the forced choice presented to him.[69] The scene summarizes the hierarchy governing Victor better than almost any other: he accepts the responsibilities of an Emperor, but no political office, cosmic mechanism or utilitarian calculation is permitted to demand that he willingly surrender his family.
Despite the enormous amount of time, power and experience accumulated throughout the story, Victor's central identity therefore remains remarkably stable. The sick young Human who hated helplessness, refused to let other people settle his personal grudges and wanted the freedom to live according to his own choices does not disappear. The scale surrounding those traits changes. Pride becomes sovereign confidence; possessiveness expands into responsibility for an enormous family and civilization; his hunger for battle becomes a disciplined pursuit of mastery; selfishness becomes intertwined with obligations voluntarily accepted toward everyone he calls his; and vindictiveness develops into an explicit principle of reciprocity toward both kindness and hostility. Victor matures considerably, but he never becomes a fundamentally different person. His growth is the process of learning how to carry more power, more people and more consequences without surrendering the Will that defined him before any of that power existed.

### Alter Victor
Alter Victor, also referred to as Victor's inner self, was the temporary personification of the portion of Victor's Vampire Progenitor existence that his developing body and Soul had not yet completely assimilated. Although Alter possessed a distinct voice, could converse with Victor and Roxanne, and appeared to think independently, he was never a separate Soul, possessing entity or conventional alternate personality. Alter repeatedly identified himself as Victor, describing himself as the projection of Victor's Progenitor powers and as a part of Victor's own Soul that remained separated only because Victor's body was still developing the capacity to contain everything he had awakened.[279][280][281]
The phenomenon originated alongside Victor's abnormal development as the Second Vampire Progenitor. His Blood Count Transformation combined Blood with the elemental characteristics inherited from the Snow, Scarlett and Fulger Bloodlines, producing considerably greater output than an ordinary Count transformation. Victor's body initially lacked the control and durability necessary to safely sustain that power; an early use left him unconscious for approximately a month and damaged even his Soul through recoil.[25] [[Scathach Elderblood Scarlett|Scathach Scarlett]] consequently gave him magically enhanced gloves that restrained and helped regulate his power. The gloves should not be interpreted as a prison specifically designed to contain Alter: their primary purpose was to prevent Victor from releasing more power than his body and Soul could safely support.[25]
Alter Victor's initial appearance.
Alter's earliest appearance was considerably less Human than his later manifestations. He appeared as an amorphous or distorted shadow-like Being without a clearly defined body, distinguished primarily by prominent blood-red eyes and a mouth filled with sharp teeth. His temperament nevertheless made his identity obvious. Alter displayed Victor's pride, possessiveness, aggression, sadism toward enemies and protectiveness toward the people Victor regarded as his own. He habitually spoke in terms such as "we", "us" and "ours", treating Victor's wives, powers, secrets and interests as equally belonging to both of them rather than behaving like an unrelated consciousness occupying Victor's Soul.[279]
This shared identity was more than a personality similarity. Alter possessed access to portions of the inherited information contained within Victor's Progenitor nature before Victor could consciously retrieve all of it himself. The Blood of the Night King carried inherited knowledge in a manner compared to the racial memories naturally transmitted among Dragons. Victor technically possessed that information, but much of it initially remained inaccessible to his conscious mind; Alter could therefore explain things Victor already possessed somewhere within himself but had not yet learned how to retrieve directly.[280] Alter was consequently able to discuss Victor's Blood, Progenitor physiology, Soul and inherited supernatural knowledge without being an external teacher. His knowledge fundamentally came from the same existence as Victor's own.[280][282]
Alter also understood that his apparent separation was temporary. He explained that as Victor awakened more completely as the Blood of the Night King, mastered his powers and developed a body capable of sustaining the full output of his Progenitor nature, the distinction between them would disappear. Victor would eventually possess Alter's knowledge and power directly rather than requiring an internal manifestation to mediate access to them.[280]
Alter demonstrated that he could react independently to threats directed at Victor's Soul. When [[Aphrodite]] covertly used her [[Divine Sense]] to inspect Victor, Alter detected the intrusion before Victor consciously understood what she had done. He blocked Aphrodite from seeing deeper into Victor's Soul, limiting what she perceived primarily to the thousands of Souls already stored inside him, and immediately warned Victor not to reveal the existence of Roxanne or the World Tree hidden within him.[283] The incident demonstrated that Alter was not merely a passive visual representation; while the separation existed, he could actively defend the internal regions of their shared Soul.
A far clearer explanation of Alter's nature occurred when Victor deliberately entered his Inner World to deal with the enormous quantities of Souls, Miasma, Bloodlust and accumulated supernatural material inside himself. By then Alter's appearance had changed completely. Instead of the indistinct dark creature Victor had known previously, he possessed a humanoid body resembling Victor himself, but his entire body was completely white while only his violet eyes retained distinct coloration.[281] Alter explicitly explained the change by stating that he was the projection of Victor's Progenitor powers and a portion of Victor's Soul with which Victor was gradually becoming compatible as he grew stronger. Even the restoration of parts of Alter's previously incomplete body reflected the strengthening of Victor's Progenitor side.[281]
The state of Victor's Inner World explained why this assimilation was initially so difficult. Victor had accumulated thousands of foreign Souls within a living body, something Alter described as fundamentally contrary to the normal order of existence. Functions involving such enormous concentrations of Souls ordinarily belonged to spiritual dimensions such as Heavens and Hells rather than to the body of a living mortal. Vampire Progenitors were exceptional because their Race naturally interacted with Souls, but Victor had pushed even that abnormal characteristic far beyond ordinary conditions.[281]
Alter compared Victor's condition to a system operating continuously at its maximum capacity. Victor's enormous Progenitor Soul could contain the burden, but doing so placed constant pressure upon his existence.[281] The presence of Roxanne radically changed the situation. Because a World Tree normally supports the world in which it grows, Roxanne existing directly inside Victor's Soul caused her natural function to support Victor himself. As she consumed and refined the Souls accumulated within him, her own growth simultaneously refined Victor's body and Soul, creating a symbiotic process in which both Victor and Roxanne continuously developed together.[281][282]
Alter further explained an important distinction concerning Progenitor Souls. A Progenitor possessed a Soul of extraordinary size, even exceeding those of Gods in that respect, but its spiritual quality remained below a genuine Divine Soul because a Progenitor was still fundamentally classified as a mortal existence wielding God-level power. Roxanne's presence provided a method of continuously improving that quality rather than merely increasing the amount of power stored inside Victor.[282] The combination of Victor's enormous Progenitor Soul, Roxanne's World Tree function and the vast number of Souls being refined inside them was therefore producing an abnormal elevation of Victor's overall existence; by this stage Alter and Victor recognized that the process was even beginning to generate the first traces of Divinity.[281][282]
Alter's role during these internal developments extended beyond explaining them. He could perceive the condition of Victor's Soul, interact with the internal Sea of Blood and recognize metaphysical structures Victor had not yet learned to interpret. Following Victor's [[Soul Marriage]] with Aphrodite, for example, Alter helped explain the Soul-level connection and the internal manifestation associated with the portion of Aphrodite's Soul Core anchored within Victor.[282] His function was therefore closely tied to the parts of Victor's spiritual existence that were already present but not yet fully understood by Victor's conscious mind.
The visual development of Alter eventually reversed as Victor began successfully assimilating what Alter represented. During Victor's conquest of Hell, Roxanne noticed portions of Alter's white humanoid body disappearing back into darkness. Alter explained that this was not deterioration. Roxanne's continuous refinement of the Souls Victor consumed strengthened Victor's body, allowing him to directly access a larger fraction of the Progenitor power that had previously required Alter's separate manifestation.[284] Alter predicted that as the process continued he would progressively return to his former black ghost appearance before finally returning to the place within Victor where he belonged.[284]
The rate of integration increased dramatically as Victor fought and consumed Higher-Order Demons. By the confrontation with War, approximately half of Alter's body had become complete darkness. Roxanne initially believed the large number of Demonic Souls Victor had taken into himself must be burdening his Soul, but Alter corrected her: Victor's repeated exercise of his powers as a genuine Progenitor, combined with the consumption of increasingly powerful Beings and Roxanne's refinement, was instead accelerating the maturation of his existence.[270] Alter was visibly satisfied by the change because the disappearance of his independent form meant Victor was finally becoming capable of directly containing what had always belonged to him.[270]
Victor's centuries of training and warfare in Hell eventually completed almost the entire process. By the time he returned, approximately 99% of the Progenitor power represented through Alter had already fused with Victor; only the remaining 1% continued maintaining Alter as an independently visible presence.[168] The final obstacle was not insufficient physical strength. Victor had spent centuries separated from his wives and remained filled with worry, longing and unresolved emotion concerning his family. That internal unrest prevented him from achieving the state necessary for the final portion to settle completely into place.[168]
Once Victor returned to his family and those emotions were resolved, the separation finally ended. Within the red-skied Inner World, Alter appeared as a faint humanoid shadow whose form had almost completely disappeared. Victor initially interpreted their final conversation as a farewell, but Alter rejected that description. He was not dying and would not cease to exist; he was merely returning to where he should never have left.[168] Alter also clarified that Victor should not expect an entirely new set of powers from the fusion. Victor already possessed the Progenitor's abilities and inherited memories. What remained missing was the final state of spiritual integration—the sensation of being genuinely complete.[168]
Before returning, Alter asked Victor to continue taking care of everyone important to them, addressing him as another version of himself rather than as a separate person. The two acknowledged one another before Alter's remaining shadow entered Victor and the final division vanished.[168] Victor immediately experienced a profound sensation of fulfillment and familiarity, which he compared to the feeling of returning home after being away for an extremely long time. The integration also gave him a new clue concerning the path toward the Grandmaster level of [[Martial Arts]], another consequence of finally restoring the missing internal unity of his existence.[168]
The conclusion of the fusion revealed what Alter had fundamentally represented from the beginning. After the humanoid shadow reintegrated, the Inner World became turbulent and a colossal Being composed of pure darkness mixed with crimson shades rose within it, possessing blood-red eyes.[168] Roxanne immediately recognized the Being as the representation of Victor's Soul. She finally understood why she had never been able to locate a separate spiritual representation corresponding to Victor despite living inside his Soul: the manifestation she had been searching for had always been Alter himself. Once the incomplete separation ended, that aspect resumed its proper position within Victor's existence and stood over his Inner World as the Guardian of Victor's Soul.[168]
Alter Victor therefore should not be treated as an evil personality that Victor defeated, a second Victor who permanently lived inside him or an independent entity that died during their fusion. He was the visible consequence of Victor possessing more Progenitor power and spiritual potential than his immature body could initially assimilate. As Victor's body, Soul and Progenitor nature matured, the need for that separation progressively vanished. Chapter 749 completed the process: Alter's conversational individuality disappeared because there was no longer a meaningful division between Victor and the part of himself Alter represented, while the underlying Soul manifestation remained as the Guardian of Victor's Inner World.[281][284][270][168]
