##### The Three Wives, the Greedy Witch and Ruby's Return
Chapters 40–50
Violet eventually reached [[Nightingale]] while Ruby and Sasha remained temporarily in the Human World. Back at the Walker residence, Leon became more familiar with his two additional daughters-in-law and questioned how the arrangement between the three women could possibly function without constant violence. Ruby and Sasha admitted that jealousy existed but emphasized that they had known and cared about one another since childhood. From their perspective, Victor had effectively entered an already existing bond between the three rather than completely separating them into unrelated relationships.[40]
The supernatural investigation on Earth simultaneously continued through June. The Greedy Witch returned with information concerning Lucy, Karen and the larger political situation surrounding Clan Fulger. Karen was revealed to possess connections to Clan Horseman, the family that had obtained the Vampire Count title formerly held by Sasha's family. The sacred object stolen from the Church had also become part of Lucy's attempt to pursue his own ambitions, while Natalia used June's professional rules and greed to push her into investigating Clan Horseman more deeply on Sasha's behalf.[41]
Sasha's hatred toward the captured Maria remained intense because Maria had participated in Julia's murder. Maria showed little remorse, explaining that she and Carlos had grown up as poor orphans and had entered the Inquisition because killing supernatural beings was simply the profession through which they survived. Sasha refused to accept emotional detachment as an excuse. She asked Maria to imagine someone murdering the person she valued above everyone else and then expecting forgiveness simply because the killer considered it "work." Maria admitted that she would feel hatred, loss and emptiness and would never forgive such a person. Sasha's response was simple: Maria finally understood her.[42]
Violet's arrival in Nightingale reunited her with Victor after [[Scathach]]'s kidnapping. Their reunion immediately returned to the intensely possessive affection characteristic of their relationship, although Victor briefly reacted when he smelled another man's scent on her. Violet explained that it belonged to her father, [[Adonis Snow]], whom Victor had not yet met. Once satisfied, Victor resumed training rather than abandoning his routine simply because his wife had arrived, something Violet began to recognize as another fundamental part of his personality.[43]
Victor's connection with his wives was also becoming more complex. Through the marriage bond he could increasingly sense significant changes in Sasha's emotional condition even when she was elsewhere. When Sasha became troubled by discussions surrounding her family, Victor instinctively sent reassurance through their connection before she later joined him in Nightingale. Sasha's conflict with [[Siena Scarlett Elderblood]] over Clan politics further demonstrated how deeply the loss of the Fulger Count title and Julia's death still affected her, even when she attempted to behave normally around Victor.[44]
Training with Lacus gave Victor a more practical understanding of how deeply a Noble Vampire's abilities could influence their user. Fire naturally resonated with forceful emotions and aggression, ice encouraged emotional coldness and detachment, and lightning pushed the body toward extreme activity. Victor experimented with maintaining different powers across different portions of his body, at one point emphasizing lightning through most of himself while using fire and ice through his arms. The exercise demonstrated that his powers were not simply attacks he activated externally; they were increasingly becoming integrated into his physical state and fighting style.[45]
Victor, Violet and Sasha later received a rare period of peace together beneath Nightingale's night sky. Away from the Inquisition, political disputes and Scathach's training, the three exchanged blood and spoke more openly about their emotions. Victor reassured Sasha that she did not need to hide her grief or instability from him and made clear that he would listen whenever she wished to speak. The evening became one of the earliest occasions in which their unusual marriage functioned as an actual shared relationship rather than a crisis created by a ritual gone wrong.[46]
Ruby, meanwhile, remained in the Human World long enough to eliminate loose ends surrounding Victor's household. She investigated the university, learned that Corneliu had fled to Nightingale and examined the prisoners kept beneath the Walker residence. Thomas and Jimmy had become so accustomed to captivity that Ruby found them playing cards rather than attempting escape. Instead of killing two relatively inexperienced hunters who might remain useful, she considered magical contracts and other means of controlling the information they possessed.[46][47]
Ruby also evaluated Maria's transformation in greater detail. Because Sasha had converted Maria improperly and under extreme emotional circumstances, Maria had not become an ordinary Plebeian Vampire. She had instead become a form of Ghoul, with the characteristics of a Ghoul King allowing her to retain intelligence while carrying the dangerous traits of creatures historically treated as biological weapons. Ghouls could spread their condition through bites and wounds and were associated with physical degradation and a hunger for Human flesh, making Maria potentially catastrophic if left uncontrolled.[48]
Before returning to Victor, Ruby finally confronted her relationship with Scathach. Despite admiring her mother, Ruby had spent much of her life frustrated by Scathach's emotional distance and her inability to understand what the ancient Countess was thinking. Scathach unexpectedly responded by embracing and comforting her daughter, explaining that living for thousands of years inevitably made someone difficult for younger people to read. When Ruby asked whether anyone truly understood her, Victor briefly entered Scathach's thoughts before she dismissed the possibility. Even so, Scathach privately recognized that she had laughed and enjoyed herself considerably more since meeting her son-in-law.[49]
Ruby finally reunited properly with Victor in Nightingale. Victor immediately teased his normally composed wife and even recorded one of her reactions, joking that the material could someday be shown to their children. Beneath the teasing, however, he gave Ruby the same direct affection he had already given Violet and Sasha. Their exchange of blood restored the balance among his three wives and reinforced that Ruby was not merely Scathach's daughter or the quiet third participant in the ritual, but one of Victor's partners in her own right.[50]
Victor hugged Ruby tightly in the forest after her emotional outburst. They kissed passionately until a saliva bridge formed. He offered his neck; she bit it while pressing her soft breasts against his chest. He held her ass, feeling her body like a seductive Succubus, and bit her collarbone. Ruby moaned loudly, her legs weakened, and a clear liquid leaked from her secret place, soaking her pants. She wrapped her legs around his waist and felt his thick erection against her intimate place. After mutual feeding, she looked at his reaction with happiness. He teased her by pulling her hard nipples, making her cover her breasts and turn red, then blew in her ear. He later carried her princess-style and squeezed her ass. Lacus and Pepper watched from a tree with red faces.[50]

##### The Horseman Wager and Scathach's Training Begins
Chapters 51–57
[[Scathach]] eventually gathered Victor, his wives and her daughters for a discussion about the political conflict involving Clan Fulger. During the meeting, Victor again displayed how little he cared for traditional vampire etiquette, particularly whenever Siena attempted to lecture him about the proper way to address her mother. He also became visibly disgusted when Scathach prepared to drink stored blood. Victor considered stale blood vastly inferior to feeding directly and instead cut his own wrist and filled her cup with his blood, giving Scathach her first deliberate taste of the blood that had already transformed the lives of Violet, Ruby and Sasha.[51][52]
The conversation turned to [[Victoria Fulger Elderblood|Victoria Rider]], Sasha's aunt. Victoria had formally challenged Clan Horseman in an attempt to obtain the Vampire Count title previously lost by Clan Fulger. She had wagered essentially her entire economic empire—assets valued at more than three trillion dollars—against the title. The enormous disparity between the material stake and the apparently symbolic title gave Victor his first indication that becoming a Vampire Count carried hidden privileges and responsibilities that ordinary Clan members were not permitted to know.[53]
Scathach then asked what Victor intended to do about Sasha's family. Victor separated the political title from Sasha herself. If a wager had somehow made Sasha the property of another Clan, he declared that he would train for as long as necessary and then slaughter everyone attempting to claim his wife. If Sasha was personally safe and had merely lost a family title, however, he had no intention of interfering unless Sasha wanted his help. Victor's concern was not prestige for its own sake but the wishes and safety of his wife.[53]
When Siena continued interrupting, Victor looked at her with glowing red eyes and ordered her to be quiet. Siena's body immediately obeyed. She became unable to move normally and answered him in a flat, obedient manner despite never agreeing to follow his command. Scathach, Kaguya and the others recognized the similarity to previous incidents in which Victor's words had imposed themselves upon other vampires. Victor himself remained largely unaware of the significance of what he had done, providing another early manifestation of the supernatural authority later associated with his bloodline.[53]
Scathach finally revealed why the original Fulger-Horseman wager had occurred. Clan Horseman had possessed something extraordinary enough to attract Annasthashia's curiosity: a living hybrid born from a Noble Vampire and a Werewolf. Annasthashia had wagered the Fulger Count title for the opportunity connected to the creature and lost, allowing Clan Horseman to replace Clan Fulger as one of [[Nightingale]]'s Count families.[53]
Victor initially expected vampire-werewolf hybrids to combine the strengths of both races, but his wives quickly corrected that assumption. Vampires and [[Werewolves]] were fundamentally incompatible species, and their rare offspring were normally afflicted with serious genetic abnormalities, short lifespans and sterility. Some could develop diseases dangerous to both parent species, which was one reason vampires and Werewolves traditionally exterminated discovered hybrids. The fact that Clan Horseman had kept one alive therefore implied that someone powerful was protecting the family from intervention.[54]
Suspicion naturally fell upon the Royal Family because Nightingale's royal authorities would normally have prevented such a dangerous experiment. The political implications interested Victor far less than the practical fact that the Clan game would occur in approximately six months. When the possibility of hiding or sealing Victor's three inherited Clan abilities to avoid political trouble was suggested, Victor and Scathach rejected the idea almost simultaneously. Neither believed power should be concealed simply because its existence might provoke others. Their nearly identical responses made the similarities between master and future disciple increasingly impossible for the people around them to ignore.[54]
Scathach chose that moment to announce that Victor's real training would begin immediately. She moved against him without warning, breaking his foot and striking hard enough to nearly make him lose consciousness. Victor responded by biting his tongue to remain awake, counterattacking and then smiling through the blood in his mouth. He told his wives not to interfere and assured Scathach that she did not need to force him to accompany her; if training meant being pushed against someone overwhelmingly stronger, he would follow willingly.[55]
Before leaving, an important change occurred between Violet, Kaguya and Victor. Violet formally released Kaguya from her position as Violet's personal maid, allowing Kaguya to serve Victor directly instead. The decision acknowledged what had already happened emotionally: Kaguya's loyalty to Victor was no longer simply an extension of her hereditary obligation to Clan Snow. For the first time, she had personally chosen the master she wished to serve.[55]
Scathach's first lessons were deliberately brutal. Instead of beginning with elegant martial techniques, she tested Victor's pain tolerance and regeneration. She stabbed vital areas, inflicted injuries that would have instantly killed a Human and observed how quickly his body repaired itself. Victor regenerated at a rate that surprised even Scathach, recovering from severe wounds within seconds despite being only a newborn. His regenerative ability gave him an enormous advantage, but Scathach warned that regeneration was useless if pain caused him to freeze or if an opponent destroyed his brain, heart or other vital structures faster than he could recover.[56]
She therefore began by teaching Victor how to remain functional while injured. Scathach disemboweled, impaled and repeatedly struck him, forcing him to learn to continue observing the battlefield regardless of what happened to his body. Victor accepted the suffering enthusiastically because every injury showed him another weakness that could be corrected. Once Scathach had established his physical limits, she began rebuilding his fundamentals: movement, distance, control of strength, efficient use of Energy and proper weapon handling.[56][57]
Victor gravitated toward the greatsword while also showing interest in the spear. Scathach had no intention of allowing him to remain dependent on a single weapon and planned to expose him eventually to many different forms of combat. Her objective was not simply to make Victor stronger. She intended to remove the wasteful habits of a newborn who possessed enormous power without technique and replace them with the foundations necessary for Victor to eventually develop a style of his own.[57]

##### The White Wolf, Bloodlust and the First Weeks of Training
Chapters 58–64
While Victor trained under [[Scathach]], Ruby and Sasha began training together. Sasha had always relied heavily upon the overwhelming speed provided by Fulger lightning, whereas Ruby possessed more formal martial instruction from her mother. Lacus helped bridge the differences between them, allowing Sasha to begin learning the basic principles Scathach had taught her daughters while Ruby focused on improving her own ability usage and understanding the Vampire Count transformation.[58]
Violet temporarily separated from them and returned to Snow territory to train beneath Hilda. Her years of monitoring Victor and concentrating obsessively upon him had caused her to neglect portions of her own development. Hilda consequently forced Violet to confront the fundamentals she had left incomplete rather than allowing her to rely entirely upon natural Snow power and raw emotion.[58][59]
Events in the Human World simultaneously introduced another supernatural figure connected to Victor's old life. [[Johnny Lykos]], known as the White Wolf and Leona's older half-brother, returned to the Lost Club while working as a supernatural mercenary. One of the jobs reaching him involved Lucy, whose attempts to complete an artificial ritual for Noble Vampire status required dangerous ingredients and had already drawn considerable attention from the Inquisition.[58][60]
Johnny also learned that his younger sister had developed feelings for a newborn vampire named Victor Walker. His immediate response was the overprotective suspicion expected from Leona's older brother, causing him to investigate Victor personally. The information he obtained described Victor as honest with people he cared about but vindictive, prideful and unwilling to forget personal grievances. Traits that Humans might have regarded as worrying did not sound especially strange to a Werewolf accustomed to territoriality and direct retaliation, although Johnny remained interested in the vampire who had become important to Leona.[60][61]
Victor's training continued while the Lucy, Horseman and White Wolf plots developed outside Scathach's territory. Scathach repeatedly pushed Victor close to death while correcting his movements and teaching him to stop wasting strength. Instead of simply releasing as much power as possible, Victor began learning to concentrate force where it was necessary, conserve Energy and observe how an opponent moved before responding.[61][62]
Kaguya adapted to her new status as Victor's personal maid during the same period. For most of her life, service had been an inherited obligation tied to Clan Blank and Clan Snow. Serving Victor felt fundamentally different because she had been given the opportunity to choose him. Her duties consequently became a source of genuine personal satisfaction rather than merely something expected by her lineage.[62]
After approximately two weeks of training, Victor had already exceeded many of Scathach's expectations. His handling of the greatsword had become far more natural, his battle instincts sharpened continuously through repeated combat with Scathach and his elemental powers increasingly behaved like extensions of his body rather than borrowed abilities. Meanwhile, Ruby explained Scathach's martial principles to Sasha. Scathach had divided four central foundations among her daughters according to their individual talents: Strength through Pepper, Speed through Lacus, Resistance through Ruby and Power through Siena. Scathach herself had mastered all four while specializing historically in Sojutsu, or spearmanship.[63]
The training also exposed a problem far more dangerous than Victor's lack of technique: his bloodlust. Unlike Noble Vampires who had lived with their instincts since birth, Victor had been Human only weeks earlier. The predatory urges created by his transformation were unusually powerful and were becoming harder to suppress as his training repeatedly pushed his body and emotions to their limits. Ruby and Sasha could feel the disturbance through their bonds and realized that Victor's bloodlust was more intense than theirs.[63]
Victor eventually lost control. His body entered a far more monstrous state than his ordinary vampiric appearance, with his blood, skin and physical features changing while a wing-like structure manifested from his body and surrounding blood reacted to his presence. Scathach did not respond with panic. The transformation confirmed what she had suspected: Victor's instincts and bloodline possessed far more depth than he consciously understood. Her task was therefore not to suppress those instincts forever but to teach him how to command them without being consumed by them.[63]
The loss of control was physical. Victor fell holding his throat and said the thirst hurt. Bones cracked. A bone wing came out of his back. His pale skin turned dark purple and his ears sharpened. He then stopped moving and looked dead. Blood gathered around him, was drawn into his body, and floated. Scathach said what an ordinary loss of control did: the vampire entered a berserker state until the thirst was satisfied, and if it was not satisfied, or if the vampire held himself for a month, a protection spell would drop him into a coma. She had underestimated him. When his eyes opened, the whole eyeball was blood-red, not only the iris. He screamed. Her face flushed. She shouted that she had known she was correct, and told him to eat.[63]
The incident became another component of Victor's training. Scathach taught him that strength obtained at the cost of reason could become a liability, while Victor slowly learned to recognize the approach of uncontrolled bloodlust before it overwhelmed him. Outside the training grounds, Lucy and Karen continued pursuing the ritual intended to elevate them artificially, while the involvement of Clan Horseman and Johnny ensured that the supernatural conflicts Victor had left behind on Earth were continuing to develop during his absence.[59][64]
Karen poured noble blood into the circle under a blood-filled coffin. The circle went crimson. She stripped, lay in the blood, and closed the lid. The light blinded the room. [[Einer Horseman]] and [[Zwei Horseman]] were already there. Einer had messy black hair, pale skin, red eyes and an unhinged smile. Zwei had straight black hair to the shoulders, pale skin, bright blood-red eyes, and a dry noble manner. Karen came out unchanged in body and swung at Einer. Zwei stopped the fist and said she had gotten stronger. Einer told them the rebirth had failed because the real ingredient was missing. Common vampires, in his explanation, were a lesser subspecies, closer to weapons such as Ghouls than to Noble Vampires. A tall man opened a case on a vial he called the blood of the King, the Progenitor, not of his descendants or wives. Lucy and Karen wanted it. Einer shut the case and laughed.[64]

##### Six Months Later and Eleonor Adrasteia
Chapters 65–69
Approximately six months after Victor's serious training began, the difference between the newborn who had been nearly killed by Mizuki and [[Scathach]]'s current disciple had become enormous. Victor's physical ability, control and combat instincts had all advanced, while his presence alone had become oppressive enough that weaker vampires could be overwhelmed by his killing intent. Scathach had also begun using specially prepared clothing and restraints to help Victor regulate the power that now escaped from him too easily.[65]
Victor was not the only person visibly changed by the six-month period. Repeated exchanges of blood between Victor and Scathach had stabilized much of the ancient Countess's persistent bloodlust. Her eyes, once habitually blood-red from constant hunger, had changed noticeably as the condition eased. The exchange also reinforced the increasingly unusual bond developing between master and disciple: Scathach had given Victor training no ordinary student could have survived, while Victor's blood had affected Scathach in ways thousands of years of ordinary feeding had failed to accomplish.[65]
Victor's personal household expanded again when Yuki was assigned to his service. Kaguya immediately regarded another maid positioned close to Victor with suspicion, while Yuki had to adapt to a master whose behavior bore little resemblance to the conventional Noble Vampires she understood. Victor's reunion with his wives after the training period also demonstrated how much all of them had changed, with Ruby, Sasha and Violet having trained separately instead of remaining stagnant while waiting for him.[65][66][67]
Shortly before the Clan game, another major Vampire Count arrived in Scathach's territory. Eleonor Adrasteia appeared accompanied by black-armored forces and supernatural horses associated with her territory. Victor immediately became more interested in the animals than in formal politics and approached one of them, Chloe, who accepted him with unusual ease despite the difficulty normally involved in bonding with such creatures.[68]
The column with her was an army of black-armored vampire knights carrying black lances larger than the knights, red eyes behind the helmets. The horses had blood-red eyes. Chloe was female, and Eleonor said Chloe did not let strangers touch her. Sasha's look recorded Eleonor at 190 centimetres, long flowing white hair, pale skin, bright golden eyes, a red coat, black gloves, a white shirt open on H-cup breasts, and black jeans. Violet called her the bitch from the west and a giraffe. Victor was already spinning Eleonor's completely black greatsword, larger than his own body. The gusts tore trees down. She demanded the sword and the horse. Chloe came to him and asked, in her way, to leave with him. He told the horse he would save her from the insensitive woman. Her eyes watered. Violet accused Eleonor of making him cry. Eleonor lent the sword for one hour. He hugged her, told Violet he loved her, kissed his wife, and ran into the forest to keep swinging.[68]
Eleonor herself was another former disciple of Scathach and wielded an enormous greatsword whose weight made it impractical for ordinary vampires. Victor surprised those present by handling the weapon despite his age. Scathach also used the meeting to demonstrate how far Victor's training had progressed. By this point he had begun integrating the major fundamentals she taught into a fifth principle: Control. Raw Strength, Speed, Resistance and Power became far more dangerous when every movement and release of Energy could be regulated precisely.[68][69]
Scathach said she had taught him the basics in six months and still needed time to cut the diamond. Those basics were all five techniques, not the four her daughters had been given. They had not been ready for the last one. The fifth was Control, and its prerequisite was already knowing the other four. Pepper recognized her own force-control in the swings. When Scathach called him back, he threw the greatsword. Eleonor stopped Violet from catching it, took the hilt on her shoulder, and the impact cracked the ground under her in a cobweb.[68]
Victor's enthusiasm occasionally outpaced that control. During a demonstration he released an attack far beyond what was necessary and devastated a large portion of the surrounding forest, earning an immediate reprimand from Scathach. The incident showed both sides of his progress: the newborn who once possessed tremendous power without knowing how to fight had become a highly capable combatant, yet he still required experience to use that power proportionally in every situation.[69]
With the Clan game approaching, Victor traveled toward the Royal Capital alongside Scathach's group and Eleonor's forces. He rode Chloe during the journey, marking the end of the secluded training phase of his life. Victor had spent roughly half a year hidden within Scathach's territory; he was now about to enter [[Nightingale]]'s political center and reveal the result of that training before vampire society.[69]

##### The Royal Capital, Ophis Tepes and Victor's Philosophy
Chapters 70–77
The journey to the Royal Capital took Victor beyond the relatively isolated territories in which he had spent most of his time in [[Nightingale]]. The Capital was the center of royal power and contained far larger concentrations of vampires, Noble families and supernatural presences. Victor reacted to many of those presences not with caution but with excitement, instinctively searching for powerful individuals who might eventually become worthy opponents.[70][71]
Victor's casual way of addressing [[Scathach]] also generated immediate attention. Ordinary vampires treated the Countess with extreme deference, while Victor openly called her by name and interacted with her with the familiarity of a close master rather than a distant political superior. Rumors consequently began spreading even before Victor publicly fought anyone, with observers wondering what sort of young vampire could behave so freely around the infamous [[Scathach Elderblood Scarlett|Scathach Scarlett]].[70]
While exploring the Capital, Victor encountered a quiet black-haired girl with violet eyes. The child, Ophis, took Victor's hand with almost no hesitation and rapidly began calling him "Father." Victor knew nothing about her identity and did not particularly care; he saw a lonely child and responded naturally by taking care of her.[72]
Victor brought Ophis shopping, bought her clothing and treated the experience like an ordinary outing with a young daughter. His servants displayed substantially more awareness of propriety than he did, assisting Ophis where necessary while Victor remained largely oblivious to the political consequences of becoming attached to an unknown child in the Royal Capital. The situation changed when Elizabeth appeared and revealed that Ophis was one of the daughters of [[Vlad III Tepes|Vlad Tepes]], the King of Vampires.[72][73]
Learning Ophis' status did not alter Victor's behavior. He continued carrying her, caring for her and allowing her to call him Father. Royal blood meant nothing to him compared with the relationship that had already formed. Ophis, who normally had difficulty connecting with others, became increasingly attached to Victor because he treated her according to his own feelings rather than as a princess whose every interaction carried political significance.[73][74]
The situation naturally alarmed Victor's wives and the people responsible for understanding Nightingale's politics. Victor was questioned about why he continually involved himself in situations that could generate enormous complications. His answer summarized the philosophy guiding most of his actions: he did what he wanted. That freedom did not mean ignoring consequences. If his decisions caused problems, he would accept those problems, learn from mistakes and rely upon the people he trusted when he lacked knowledge.[75]
Scathach strongly approved. Victor's answer reflected the same mentality through which she had lived for thousands of years: social expectations should not become chains preventing someone from living according to their own nature. The exchange made their similarities explicit enough that the people around them increasingly treated Victor as a younger male counterpart to Scathach rather than merely her latest disciple.[75]
Kaguya meanwhile continued developing into Victor's shadow in a literal and figurative sense. Her ability allowed her to remain hidden within his shadow for extended periods, hearing conversations and gathering information people often assumed was private. Victor trusted her with access few others possessed, and Kaguya increasingly functioned as his personal intelligence network, bodyguard, confidante and maid simultaneously.[76]
Victor's relationship with Scathach deepened further when the two exchanged blood again. Victor behaved toward her with physical familiarity almost nobody else would dare display, including comforting and touching the ancient Countess without fear. Scathach, rather than punishing him, increasingly accepted and even welcomed behavior that would have resulted in the death of another vampire. The relationship remained formally one of master and disciple, but its emotional boundaries were already becoming far less simple.[77]

##### The Rider–Horseman Game and Victor's Public Debut
Chapters 78–90
The long-awaited game between [[Victoria Fulger Elderblood|Victoria Rider]] and Clan Horseman transformed the Royal Capital into a major public event. Noble Vampires and ordinary citizens gathered to watch because the stakes affected the political structure of [[Nightingale]] itself. Victoria sought the Count title, while Clan Horseman intended to retain the position and obtain the enormous wealth she had wagered against it.[78][79]
Victor attended with his family and [[Scathach]] while Ophis once again attached herself to him, at one point comfortably occupying his lap during the proceedings. His increasingly visible relationship with the King's daughter added another layer of rumor around the unknown young vampire already associated with three major Clans and Scathach.[78][80]
The political tensions surrounding Ophis also brought Victor into more direct contact with Elizabeth. Victor understood that his actions could generate consequences but refused to distance himself from Ophis merely to make royal politics easier. Discussions with his wives reinforced another important difference between Victor and the traditional Noble society around him: status alone did not determine how he treated someone. A king, princess, maid or ordinary child would receive respect according to Victor's own judgment rather than according to rank.[80]
Behind the public spectacle, both competing Clans were concealing substantial secrets. Victoria's representative was Tatsuya, a highly skilled swordsman secretly connected to Victoria far more closely than most observers understood. Clan Horseman's representative was [[Einer Horseman]], whose abilities and relationship with the Clan's hybrid research made him equally important to the family's plans.[81][82]
Tatsuya, as Victoria dressed him for the arena, was 185 centimetres, pale, with long dark-blond hair and dark eyes, in a black yukata with gold accents. She told him not to use lightning and to rely on his father's talent. The witch [[Hecate]], in a modern purple dress with white accents, could not explain how Horseman had learned he existed. Niklaus sent Einer, age 105, and warned him not to repeat a failure involving an alpha wolf. Zwei reported that the captive hybrid was sick and dying. The announced rules were one duel, one round, no time limit, lost by destruction of the heart or by surrender, with permanent death forbidden. Clan Horseman bet the Vampire Count title. Clan Rider bet the Rider Conglomerate.[82]
Tatsuya and Einer entered the arena and immediately demonstrated abilities worthy of the political stakes. Tatsuya relied upon swordsmanship, lightning and sophisticated illusions capable of deceiving the senses of numerous vampires in the audience. Einer possessed unusual dark abilities associated with Clan Horseman and could alter his combat state dramatically. Victor quickly became less interested in who politically won the wager than in the two warriors themselves.[83][84][85]
Einer opened on a created black rapier, black slime and blackthorn, and pierced his own heart to force the power. Tatsuya answered with katana footwork while keeping the lightning down. Einer later took a Count form that decayed the ground, broke techniques by force, grew black-thorned wings and tried to coffin Tatsuya in thorns. Tatsuya drew and released Hakai no Sora, a colossal oriental dragon of golden scales, blue eyes and lightning, and destroyed the cocoon. Einer dropped the transformation to save stamina and went to the blade.[83][85]
After six months of being beaten almost exclusively by Scathach, Victor desperately wanted a realistic measurement of his improvement. Fighting Scathach could not provide that because the gap between them remained too vast. Tatsuya and Einer were powerful enough to challenge him while still existing within a range where Victor could judge his own progress. His mounting excitement became so obvious that Scathach immediately understood what her disciple wanted.[86]
Scathach had already decided to turn the situation into another lesson. She formally inserted Clan Scarlett into the wager, temporarily suspending the original match. Her proposal was extraordinary: if either Tatsuya or Einer defeated Victor, Scathach would give the winner's faction her complete support for one year, even for objectives as extreme as war or political upheaval. If Victor defeated both heirs, he would gain permission to visit their Clans, use the two men as future training partners and learn any techniques or knowledge that were not protected Clan secrets.[86]
Her wording in the administration room was this. She wanted her disciple to fight both heirs. Whoever defeated him received her support for one hundred percent of whatever goal that side had, for one year. If he won, he could enter their houses at any time to use the heirs as training and could learn anything that was not a Clan secret. The image on the screen named him Victor Walker/Snow, Fulger, Scarlett, age twenty-one.[86]
The offer was too valuable for either faction to reject. When Victor's information appeared before the audience, Nightingale finally learned the identity of Scathach's mysterious new disciple: Victor Walker/Snow, Fulger, Scarlett, age twenty-one. His age alone shocked the crowd. To vampire society, Victor was effectively an infant being inserted into a fight against exceptional Noble Vampires several times his age.[86]
He rose from the ice throne with Ophis held like a princess, set his glasses down, and passed a gloved hand through the glass. The magic symbols on the white gloves glowed blood-red. His whole body went through. He floated, landed between the two heirs, and the arena floor turned to ice under his feet. Einer made a rapier and thrust it at his face. Victor coated his fingers in ice and stopped the rapier on one finger, then punched the air. The blast threw Einer into the wall. Einer coughed blood, and the cold left on the hit started freezing his body. Victor snapped his fingers, formed a greatsword of pure ice, set it on his shoulder, and told Tatsuya to come. Tatsuya did not. Lightning covered Victor. He vanished in a trail of golden light, and Tatsuya was blasted into the sky. Victor grew a fire sphere on one finger until it was a miniature sun and sent it with the word "Burn." The blast cleared the clouds over the capital. Tatsuya's eyes flashed gold, lightning wrapped him, and he left the sky. Victoria's chair cracked in her hand. Scathach laughed.[87]
Einer and Tatsuya were forced to reveal increasingly greater portions of their abilities. Einer entered his transformed state while Tatsuya used more of his lightning and swordsmanship. Victor suffered serious injuries during the exchange, including being pierced through the abdomen, but regenerated within seconds and continued fighting as though the damage were simply another part of the training exercise.[88]
In that exchange Einer's Count form darkened his skin, enlarged him and gave him black wings. Thorns punched through Victor's stomach and lifted him. The wound closed in under seven seconds, clothes included. Tatsuya's Ryujin, Hakai no Sora, a lightning-covered oriental dragon with golden scales and blue eyes, was frozen solid by the magic circle on Victor's glove and then shattered. Victor took Tatsuya by the neck with an ice-covered arm that ignored the katana and threw him into Einer. He lifted the melted ice into the sky and brought it down as an ice-thorn shower crossed with lightning rain. Impacts ignited. A single giant ice spike formed over the arena. He was still in his ordinary state.[88]
As the confrontation escalated, Victor constructed an enormous mass of ice and layered lightning and fire into the attack. Tatsuya and Einer realized that neither could handle him independently and began cooperating despite entering the original game as enemies. Einer reinforced Tatsuya with his dark Energy while Tatsuya became the primary offensive weapon of their temporary partnership.[89]
Their teamwork pleased Victor rather than irritating him. He wanted opponents who could adapt, cooperate and force him to improve, not easy victories. After confirming that both men possessed the qualities he wanted from future training partners, Victor finally ended the battle by incapacitating them and was declared the winner.[90]
He turned falling ice debris into water and then into harmless hail with a snap, teased a referee who said he was 1,794 years old, and told the two he liked them as warriors. They insisted on continuing while exhausted. He ended it by flicking both foreheads. The burst knocked them unconscious into the wall. The referee declared him the winner. Female vampires in the stands reacted loudly enough that killing intent answered from the VIP room, including Ophis declaring that Victor was hers. Five killing intents came out of that box.[90]
The result did not settle the original political dispute between Victoria and Clan Horseman. Scathach's intervention had constituted a separate wager designed around Victor's development, and the Rider-Horseman conflict remained its own issue. Scathach openly identified Victor as both her disciple and son-in-law, while Victor's public performance ensured that the twenty-one-year-old newborn could never again remain an obscure figure within Nightingale. Victoria and Niklaus closed their own bet as a tie because the conditions had been broken. Word went to the King. He was angry, and the working assumption in the arena was that the anger concerned his daughters.[90]

##### Fame, Tatsuya and Nightingale's Wilds
Chapters 91–101
By the following day, Victor's name had spread throughout vampire society. Recordings and discussions of the arena battle circulated widely, with particular attention given to his age, [[Scathach]]'s public recognition of him and his use of powers associated with three different Count bloodlines. Victor had entered the Capital as an almost unknown newborn and emerged as one of [[Nightingale]]'s most discussed young vampires.[91]
Victor was less interested in fame than in the people he had fought. He went looking for Tatsuya almost immediately, entering Victoria's residence with little concern for normal boundaries. Victor regarded Tatsuya as valuable precisely because the swordsman had been capable of challenging him. Tatsuya initially struggled with Victor's aggressive approach to friendship, but Victor eventually made his intentions simple: they had fought, respected one another's ability and should therefore become friends and fight again in the future.[91][92]
Tatsuya soon gave Victor an opportunity to demonstrate his post-training control outside the arena. Victoria's residence contained infiltrators and hostile observers. Rather than destroy the entire area, Victor spread his perception and used highly controlled ice and rainfall to neutralize enemies throughout the estate while keeping them alive for interrogation. The precision contrasted sharply with the enormous, uncontrolled attacks of his early training.[92]
Victor and Tatsuya subsequently sparred and discussed combat more directly. Victor had begun internalizing Scathach's teaching philosophy and criticized Tatsuya whenever his technique became too rigid or dependent upon a particular ability. Their relationship gradually shifted from former opponents to genuine friends who could improve one another through repeated combat.[93]
Ophis remained another continuing connection from the Capital. She had become reluctant to leave Victor, but he gently told her to return with her family and reassured her that she could visit again. Ophis obeyed him with unusual ease, surprising those who normally struggled to manage the quiet princess. Victor's influence over her increasingly resembled that of a parent despite the lack of any biological connection.[94]
Victor's wives were becoming increasingly conscious of how frequently powerful or unusual women entered his orbit. Their discussion ranged from royal princesses to [[Vampire Counts]] and eventually Scathach herself. Despite their jealousy, they recognized that Victor had never actually betrayed their trust. More troublingly, they realized that Victor's stated preference for extremely possessive women meant that their own obsessive personalities were exactly what attracted him in the first place.[95]
Victor later explored the eastern wilderness and discovered that Nightingale's natural environment contained far more than vampire civilization. He entered a dangerous forest and encountered an enormous armored gorilla as well as a predatory tree whose fruit contained blood-like liquid edible by vampires. The remains surrounding the tree demonstrated that it had evolved by consuming living beings, yet Victor approached the bizarre creature with curiosity rather than immediate hostility.[96]
The giant gorilla responded differently. Victor and the creature fought for hours, only temporarily cooperating when other beasts interfered with their duel. Once those creatures were eliminated, the two resumed fighting until both were exhausted. Victor left the encounter considering the gorilla a future friend and training partner, while the blood-producing tree became another of the strange entities he intended to revisit.[97]
Eleonor soon invited Victor and his family to her own territory. Her lands constantly suffered attacks from demonic beasts, making the region both strategically important and extremely dangerous. The possibility of months spent fighting strong monsters naturally appealed to Victor, but he chose not to leave immediately. He had spent six months almost completely consumed by Scathach's training and wanted time with his wives, parents, Human friends and even Zack before throwing himself into another prolonged campaign.[98]
Victor also learned more about Nightingale's Count system during this period. The great Count families were not simply wealthy aristocrats; each governed a major territory and fulfilled functions that supported the Vampire King and the kingdom as a whole. Their power was enormous, but the title also bound them into a political structure under royal authority. The different Clans had evolved around distinct territories, economic roles, military obligations and inherited abilities.[99][100]
The political discussion became immediately relevant when several members of Victor's extended family arrived to meet him. Agnes Snow, [[Adonis Snow]], [[Annasthashia Elderblood Fulger]] and William Fulger all entered the situation for their own reasons, bringing Victor's increasingly complicated relationship with his wives' parents directly into Scathach's territory.[99][100]
Before confronting that gathering, Victor spent time with Kaguya. The maid had become one of the few people who knew nearly every embarrassing or politically dangerous detail surrounding him. During their conversation Victor reflected upon the simplicity and brutality of the previous six months: train, fight, be nearly killed, regenerate, understand one more mistake and repeat. Kaguya also realized how frequently Victor and Scathach had exchanged blood during that period, helping explain the changes both had undergone.[101]

##### A Date with Violet and the In-Laws Arrive
Chapters 102–109
After months dominated by combat, Victor finally began fulfilling his promise to spend individual time with each of his wives. Violet was the first. Ruby helped her prepare, and Violet deliberately chose clothing that evoked one of the important early periods of her relationship with Victor. The choice reflected how strongly she valued the years in which she had secretly watched over him before he ever knew vampires existed.[102]
Natalia, recently returned from her own extended absence, provided transportation and magical assistance. With a portal, Victor and Violet traveled to [[Paris]]. Victor admitted that he possessed little conventional dating experience, but his approach remained characteristic: the location mattered less than spending time alone with his wife.[103]
Their date gave Violet something she rarely possessed after the abnormal marriage ritual—Victor entirely to herself. They explored Paris, ate, shopped and behaved like a young married couple rather than members of several ancient vampire families. When Violet's attention began drifting toward other wives or supernatural problems, Victor reminded her that this time belonged specifically to her.[103][104]
Victor also reflected upon the strange speed with which his life had changed. Only months earlier he had been a chronically ill Human whose future appeared physically limited. He was now a vampire trained by [[Scathach]], married to three women and capable of fighting Noble Vampires more than a century old. Despite the chaos, Victor told Violet how fortunate he considered himself to have met her, reinforcing the emotional foundation that existed beneath their possessiveness and blood bond. Their date eventually became one of the most intimate periods of their relationship since his transformation.[104]
While Victor and Violet were away, the atmosphere at Scathach's mansion became considerably less peaceful. Agnes and Adonis had arrived from Clan Snow, while William and Annasthashia represented the Fulger side of Victor's extended family. Sasha was particularly uncomfortable because the arrival of her biological parents reopened everything Victor had learned about her childhood.[105]
The problem worsened when Annasthashia learned about Julia's death and reacted with an indifference that deeply hurt Sasha. Julia had effectively raised Sasha and occupied the emotional position Annasthashia herself had failed to fill. Treating Julia as merely a replaceable servant reinforced everything Victor already despised about the way Sasha had been raised.[105]
Victor's time with Violet also caused him to experience another memory transfer through their blood bond. He witnessed moments from Violet's past and gained a clearer understanding of how long she had been attached to him. A younger Violet had feared how Victor might react to her vampiric traits, only for the young Human Victor to respond with fascination rather than rejection. Memories such as these explained why Violet's attachment had developed long before the ritual formally made him her husband.[106]
When Victor and Violet returned to [[Nightingale]], Victor handled the consequences of their Paris trip with the increasingly powerful Charm he had begun using more consciously, manipulating the memories of ordinary Humans who had been exposed to circumstances that could reveal too much. The ability that had first appeared unconsciously against Scathach and Siena was rapidly becoming another practical tool in Victor's arsenal.[107]
Victor then properly met his in-laws. His behavior toward Agnes and Adonis remained confident but relatively cordial, and Victor became especially interested in Adonis because his instincts recognized that something unusual was happening within the man's body. Adonis' abilities and condition clearly carried a heavy cost, although Victor did not yet understand every detail of his father-in-law's circumstances.[107][108]
The meeting deteriorated when Victor turned toward Sasha's parents. Everything Sasha had told him about her childhood returned immediately. He could accept harsh training when the purpose was genuinely to prepare someone to survive—Scathach had spent six months inflicting horrific injuries upon Victor for precisely that reason—but what Sasha described went beyond necessary discipline. Victor viewed much of William and Annasthashia's treatment of their daughter as neglect and cruelty rather than education.[108][109]
Victor consequently made no attempt to behave like a respectful son-in-law. His anger spread through the marriage bond strongly enough that Violet, Ruby and Sasha could feel it, and he openly confronted William and Annasthashia over what they had done to Sasha. The confrontation escalated until Victor chose the most direct method available to him: he challenged both of Sasha's parents to battle.[109]

##### The Fulger Parents, William's Death and Natashia
Chapters 110–118
News that Victor had attacked two former [[Vampire Counts]] rapidly reached [[Scathach]]. Rather than rush to rescue him, she laughed. Sasha was terrified that Victor would die because of her family, but Scathach ordered her to trust her husband and stand proudly. She would interfere if Victor's life truly became unsalvageable, but until then the battle belonged to her disciple. Scathach's confidence reflected how much her opinion of Victor had changed during their six months together.[110]
Victor did not fight alone. Kaguya acted from his shadow and combined her abilities with his own, allowing master and maid to alternate between direct attacks, deception and sudden shifts in positioning. Against opponents with centuries of experience, Victor relied upon unpredictability rather than attempting to overpower them straightforwardly. Ice transformed the terrain, fire pressured regeneration, lightning altered his speed and Kaguya's shadows created attack angles his opponents had to constantly monitor.[111]
The battle quickly became vicious. Kaguya cut William's throat while Victor attacked Annasthashia's vital organs and spine. Annasthashia retaliated by tearing out Victor's heart and even drinking his blood, an act that unexpectedly intensified her interest in him rather than simply weakening him. Victor's abnormal regeneration restored injuries that should have ended the battle, allowing him to continue adapting while his opponents gradually realized that treating him as an inexperienced child was a serious mistake.[111]
The order of the blows in that chapter: she blocked a shadow dagger. William punched the ground and the explosion blew the fog apart. Victor came out of the shadow behind her, drove a hand into her guts and pulled, then reached back in for her spine. She turned and broke that hand, then swung at his head. He set his own body on fire. She screamed in the burn. A golden lightning bolt came down on her and vaporized his hands. He kicked at William's head with ice on his feet. Kaguya came out of his shadow and opened William's neck, a shallow cut. Victor bit into that neck and tore out a piece of meat, taking the vocal cords with it. She shoved her hand into his chest, pulled the heart out, burst it, and drank the blood. He dissolved into shadow and was whole again in seconds. He formed an ice greatsword and brought it down vertically. The cut split the mountain. He jumped into the gap and kept cutting until the ice broke apart. Kaguya covered the mountain in shadow, and an ice sword wrapped in fire, sent through her, pierced William's brain. That chapter ends on the injury. It does not itself record the death.[111]
Victor eventually created an opening against William through a combination of terrain manipulation, shadow techniques and misdirection, while Annasthashia was forced to rescue William from attacks capable of destroying his head before his regeneration could save him. Once she accepted Victor as a real threat, Annasthashia stopped restraining herself and subjected him to increasingly brutal injuries.[112]
Victor was dismembered, impaled and repeatedly damaged at the level of his organs, yet instead of surrendering he laughed and continued provoking her. Kaguya's safety remained one of his priorities because her shadow-based fighting style possessed limitations against the type of overwhelming attacks being used. When Scathach finally reached the battlefield, Victor became confident that Kaguya would survive even if he lost control of what he was about to do.[112]
Victor then released the transformation Scathach had forbidden him from using casually. His body and blood changed into a darker, more monstrous state as a pillar of crimson power erupted around him. His blood behaved almost like a living extension of himself, responding defensively and offensively without requiring the same conscious manipulation as ordinary techniques. To the observers, the newborn increasingly resembled a monster that had been given power far beyond what someone of his age should possess.[112][113]
Scathach explained that Victor's transformation was related to the heightened states available to powerful Noble Vampires but that his version remained dangerously unstable. The increase in strength was enormous, yet the transformation damaged more than his physical body. His Soul and overall existence suffered under power he had not yet learned to regulate. His gloves and other restraints existed partly to prevent such states from overwhelming his control, and Scathach had prohibited him from relying upon the transformation until he could properly master all of his primary abilities.[113]
Victor nevertheless continued because the battle had become personal. He rejected William and Annasthashia's claim to automatic respect merely because they had biologically created Sasha. From Victor's perspective, Julia had performed the role of Sasha's mother far more completely than either of them had performed the role of parent. He treated William increasingly as an enemy who had harmed his wife rather than as a father-in-law whose title deserved reverence.[114]
William ultimately died during the confrontation. Victor did not attempt to disguise his responsibility or pretend the outcome had been accidental. His willingness to kill Sasha's father created consequences he understood he would eventually have to face with Sasha herself, but in the moment he considered William responsible for enough of her suffering that he did not regret the decision.[114]
Annasthashia's reaction became stranger than simple grief or rage. The battle, Victor's blood and the emotional pressure surrounding Sasha destabilized the personality Victor had been fighting. Another identity emerged: Natashia, the original personality who had existed before the cold Annasthashia persona came to dominate her behavior.[115]
Natashia was almost the opposite of the woman Sasha remembered. She was energetic, affectionate, shameless and immediately interested in Victor to an absurd degree. Scathach recognized the personality and confirmed that Sasha's mother effectively possessed two distinct selves. Natashia's emergence did not cause Victor to simply forgive everything done under Annasthashia, however. He considered both personalities parts of the same person and continued holding Sasha's mother responsible for repairing the damage.[115][116]
Sasha was overwhelmed when the woman who had always behaved coldly toward her suddenly began showering her with affection. Victor directly instructed Natashia to become a better mother, protect Sasha properly, train her without pointless cruelty and take responsibility for the Clan she had allowed to deteriorate. Natashia, unlike Annasthashia, accepted the criticism and genuinely apologized to her daughter before turning her attention toward rebuilding Fulger influence.[116]
The most difficult consequence remained William's death. Victor chose to tell Sasha himself rather than allow her to discover it indirectly. He had been raised by Anna to believe that painful truth was preferable to comforting deception, and everyone around Sasha deliberately allowed Victor to have the conversation personally.[117]
Sasha's reaction was complicated rather than simple condemnation. William had failed her in many ways, but he was still her father, and his death produced emotions she could not reduce to either hatred or grief. Victor admitted that if Sasha had been unable to accept his decision, he could have chosen another method—crippling or imprisoning William instead—but he did not lie about the fact that he had killed him because William harmed someone Victor considered more important than himself.[117][118]
Their conversation eventually moved beyond William. Sasha confessed the extremity of her attachment to Victor, including possessive impulses she normally feared would make her seem abnormal. Victor did not reject them. Extreme attachment did not frighten a man who had already admitted that possessive women were precisely the type he loved. He asked only that Sasha never allow those impulses to truly harm the family they were building together. The exchange strengthened their relationship by allowing Sasha to stop hiding the darker portions of her personality from the person most capable of accepting them.[118]

##### The Vampire King and the Birth of Clan Alucard
Chapters 119–130
Victor's increasingly disruptive presence eventually brought him before the highest authority in vampire society: [[Vlad Dracula Tepes]], the Vampire Progenitor and King of [[Nightingale]]. The Royal Family gathered around the situation, including Vlad's sons and daughters, while [[Alexios Alioth]], Vlad's trusted subordinate and Natalia's father, remained close to the throne.[119]
The encounter also exposed more of Ophis' family circumstances. Despite being the King's daughter, Ophis was emotionally distant from Vlad and feared him far more than she trusted him. Her willingness to call Victor Father therefore carried greater significance than Victor had initially understood. Ophis had spontaneously formed a parental attachment to a vampire only months old while remaining uncomfortable around her actual father.[119]
Vlad immediately imposed pressure upon Victor to evaluate how he would react before the Vampire King. The difference in power was so extreme that Victor's body understood he could not win, yet the experience reproduced the same reaction [[Scathach]] had provoked months earlier. Victor refused to simply submit because his opponent was stronger. Vlad then demonstrated supernatural control over his appearance and body, adopting different forms while observing the newborn's reactions.[120]
When Vlad ordered Victor to approach and tested him directly, Victor responded by attacking. He entered his unstable transformed state and formed a blood weapon, launching himself at the King despite knowing the attack had almost no chance of succeeding. Vlad stopped Victor's greatsword with a single finger.[121]
The overwhelming defeat pleased Victor more than it discouraged him. Vlad represented another visible summit, proof that even after six months under Scathach he remained nowhere near the highest level available to his race. Victor briefly lamented not having been born thousands of years earlier, since the additional time would have allowed him to approach such monsters sooner, but he also recognized that changing his birth would mean never meeting the wives and family he currently possessed.[121]
Vlad had originally summoned Victor partly because one young vampire marrying the heiresses of Snow, Scarlett and Fulger created an obvious political danger. A single man potentially connecting three of the greatest Noble bloodlines could eventually become the center of a faction capable of challenging the throne. Victor's behavior during the test instead interested Vlad enough for the King to make an unexpected proposal: Victor could be elevated into the Noble hierarchy himself.[121]
Victor was initially unimpressed by ordinary Noble status because titles implied administration and obligations that could interfere with training. His response reminded Vlad strongly of Scathach, who had displayed similarly little interest in conventional status. The King therefore escalated the offer and proposed making Victor a Vampire Count.[122]
Elsewhere, Natashia had begun acting decisively after her reemergence. She purged disloyal or undesirable elements from her own household, abandoned relationships she no longer valued and began preparing to restore the Fulger family's position. Victor's blood had also affected her lightning and body in noticeable ways, continuing the pattern in which people who repeatedly consumed his blood underwent changes rather than Victor alone benefiting from theirs.[122]
Victor's discussion with Vlad finally revealed more of what being a Count meant. Counts were not ornamental aristocrats but Pillars supporting Nightingale's political and territorial structure. Their territories, armies and unique functions existed under the King, and the position carried hidden privileges known only to those bound by the Count contract. Victor's lack of political ambition did not eliminate the usefulness of such a position: becoming a Pillar would give him resources, territory, freedom and opportunities suited to his desire to explore and grow.[123][124]
The discussion also clarified why Eleonor's territory was so militarized. Nightingale had contained dangerous supernatural creatures long before vampires established their present civilization, and Count families such as Adrasteia served as barriers against threats along vulnerable regions. The Pillars therefore represented functional components of the kingdom rather than simply four rich families collecting titles.[124]
Vlad then revealed the most important connection between himself and Victor. Victor's RH-null blood was not merely an unusual Human blood type. Within vampire history it was known as [[Sanguis Noctis Regis]], the Blood of the Night King, and Vlad possessed the same fundamental blood.[125]
The revelation provided a framework for several of Victor's abnormalities. Victor had entered the vampire race carrying blood naturally associated with its highest hierarchy and had then been transformed through a ritual involving three Noble heiresses. Vlad believed the interaction between Sanguis Noctis Regis, the ritual and Victor's wives helped explain why Victor inherited three separate Clan characteristics instead of becoming an ordinary Plebeian Vampire. His abnormal Charm, extraordinary learning speed and rapid adaptation likewise fit the larger pattern of a vampire whose basic nature was fundamentally different from that of an ordinary transformed Human.[125]
Vlad nevertheless warned Victor against abusing his unstable transformation. Victor still needed to master the major powers inside him—fire, ice, water, lightning and blood—because the transformed state changed far more than his muscles and could damage his Soul when his control failed. The consequences had already become partially permanent: Victor's eyes, once naturally blue as a Human, had settled permanently into the blood-red appearance associated with his vampiric evolution.[125]
The King also offered Victor advice concerning the three women bound to him. Violet, Ruby and Sasha were not merely political assets or sources of inherited powers. Their relationship with Victor was central to his stability and development, and Vlad warned him not to repeat mistakes born from distrust. Victor's own philosophy was simpler: if he could not trust the women he had chosen as wives, there would be little point in maintaining the relationship at all.[125]
Victor ultimately accepted the Count position. Alexios produced the same type of black Witch contract used by Nightingale's existing Counts. In exchange for the title, authority and hidden privileges associated with the position, Victor was bound to secrecy concerning information restricted to the Pillars.[126]
Before signing, however, Victor had to establish a formal Clan name. "Walker" was his Human family name, and Vlad's tradition required a Count to adopt a distinct supernatural surname when acting in that capacity. Victor asked Vlad for his complete name and learned—or deliberately confirmed—that the King was Vlad Dracula Tepes.[126]
Victor decided that although he possessed blood resembling Vlad's, he intended to become the King's opposite in one important respect. He did not want to build his relationships around suspicion toward the people closest to him. Victor therefore reversed "Dracula" and chose Alucard as his new Count name.[126]
To Victor, the choice represented a personal statement about the type of man he intended to become. To Scathach, Alexios and vampire politics, it looked considerably more provocative. Taking Dracula's name backwards implied that Victor regarded himself not as an inferior subordinate but as someone who intended eventually to stand on the King's level. Vlad understood the interpretation immediately and responded with delighted laughter rather than anger.[126]
After Victor signed the contract, Vlad's voice echoed throughout Nightingale as he announced the first new Vampire Count in thousands of years. Clan Alucard was formally recognized as the Fifth Pillar of vampire society, with responsibility centered upon exploration and the discovery of new lands. At only twenty-one years old, Victor became the youngest vampire ever elevated to the position.[126]
The announcement produced consequences across Nightingale. [[Adonis Snow]] received visions connected to Victor's possible future, including images suggesting Victor's eventual ascension surrounded by trusted individuals and another future involving Violet and catastrophic destruction. Adonis' prophetic ability continued exacting a severe toll upon him because the supernatural natures within his body were poorly compatible, making every significant vision dangerous.[127]
Natashia reacted to the changing political environment by reuniting with her sister Victoria and recruiting her, Tatsuya and others into the effort to rebuild their family's position. Her openly declaring Victor to be the husband she now desired naturally bewildered the people around her, but beneath the absurdity she had become dramatically more motivated than the cold Annasthashia who had allowed many family relationships to deteriorate.[128]
Victor's actions also forced Vlad to reconsider his own children. He gathered the princes and princesses and explained that Victor's suicidal-looking attack against him had contained a lesson they had failed to understand. Victor knew Vlad was overwhelmingly stronger yet still attacked because he wanted to test himself, learn the difference between them and refuse to let fear decide his actions. Vlad believed many of his own children had become mentally weak because royal status had protected them from the ambition and danger that once drove him.[129]
The reprimand affected the royal heirs differently. Some reacted with resentment toward Victor, regarding the newborn as the cause of their humiliation, while others recognized that their father rarely delivered such criticism without purpose. The existence of a twenty-one-year-old Fifth Count also altered the political balance of Nightingale immediately, giving ambitious members of the Royal Family and the Noble Clans a completely new faction to consider.[129][130]
By the end of Vampire Society, Victor was no longer simply Violet Snow's transformed Human husband. In roughly six months he had survived Scathach's personal training, learned to fight as a true Noble Vampire, developed the inherited abilities of Snow, Fulger and Scarlett, gained control over increasingly abnormal bloodline powers, befriended Tatsuya, attracted Ophis' filial attachment, publicly defeated the heirs of two major Clans, killed William Fulger, helped force Natashia's original personality back to the surface, confronted the Vampire King without submission and discovered that his Human blood belonged to the same supernatural lineage as Vlad's. His signing of the Count contract transformed those personal developments into political reality: Victor Alucard now stood as the leader of a newly created Count Clan and the Fifth Pillar of Nightingale, ensuring that every major power in vampire society would have to account for him from that point forward.[130]

#### Volume 3: A New Pillar
Chapters 131–249

##### The Fifth Pillar and the First Retaliation
Chapters 131–137
Shortly before Victor returned from his meeting with [[Vlad III Tepes|Vlad Tepes]], the people waiting at [[Scathach Elderblood Scarlett|Scathach Scarlett]]'s mansion heard the Vampire King's voice broadcast throughout [[Nightingale]]. Vlad formally announced the creation of a Fifth Pillar of Vampire Society, placing the newly founded Clan Alucard under Victor and assigning it responsibility for exploring and discovering new lands. The announcement stunned virtually everyone present. Victor had been a vampire for only approximately six months, yet had been granted a position that normally required an ancient and established Clan possessing generations of military, political and economic power. Siena considered founding an entirely new Count Clan even more extraordinary than defeating an existing Count and taking their title, while Maria, from her previous experience as an Inquisition hunter, understood how difficult even hunting a normal Vampire Count was expected to be.[131]
Vlad also publicly announced that Victor had abandoned the Walker surname for his Count identity and would henceforth be known as Victor Alucard. The name immediately carried a provocative implication because "Alucard" was "Dracula" written backwards. Victor had deliberately chosen it after learning Vlad's complete name, turning the identity of his new Clan into an implicit statement that he did not intend to live beneath Dracula forever.[131]
Victor soon returned carrying [[Scathach]] and reunited with Violet, Ruby and Sasha. His wives immediately noticed that something about him had changed again. Victor's lightning had become significantly stronger after drinking Natashia's blood, while Scathach observed that he had unconsciously begun combining Fulger lightning with movement principles he had learned during her training. Victor's abilities therefore continued evolving through blood exchange even after he had already inherited the basic characteristics of his wives' Clans.[132]
Victor also began treating the responsibilities surrounding his own household more seriously. He arranged proper payment for the people serving him, including Maria, whom Sasha had effectively acquired without ever considering the mundane matter of salary. His increasingly natural behavior as the head of a household contrasted with the absurd speed at which that household had been created; only months earlier Victor had possessed no servants, Clan or political authority at all.[132]
The women around Victor simultaneously began acknowledging something more personal. Ruby, Violet and Sasha openly discussed Scathach's increasingly obvious feelings toward their husband. Ruby believed her mother had not yet consciously recognized those feelings for what they were. The wives remembered Scathach's own declaration that she would only accept a husband capable of defeating or surpassing her and concluded that directly forcing the issue could encourage their battle-obsessed husband to recklessly challenge Scathach long before he was ready. They therefore chose to leave the matter alone for the time being.[133]
Outside Nightingale, the announcement of the Fifth Count spread rapidly throughout supernatural society. Victor's age, his unknown origin and his choice of the Alucard name attracted immediate attention. Witches were particularly interested in the new Pillar's assigned purpose because exploration and territorial expansion naturally implied the discovery of resources, magical materials and new opportunities. Werewolf authorities also began paying attention, with Anderson eventually being sent to investigate the young vampire whose rise had disrupted the established balance so quickly.[134]
The Vatican likewise reviewed information on Victor. Existing recordings showed that he possessed the powers associated with three major Noble Vampire bloodlines, although the Church did not yet consider him equivalent to a fully developed ancient Count. What concerned experienced observers was not his current strength alone but his rate of growth. A vampire who had reached Victor's present level in only six months represented a problem very different from an old enemy whose limits were already understood.[134]
The first direct consequence of Victor's new fame arrived almost immediately when assassins infiltrated Scathach's territory. Victor detected them and captured the group rather than allowing the assassination to proceed. Using his increasingly developed Vampiric Charm, he compelled their leader to answer his questions and learned that the attackers belonged to Clan [[Amon]], a Noble Vampire Clan specializing in assassination.[135]
Victor immediately went after Clan Amon rather than requesting a royal investigation. He annihilated the Clan with Snow fire, demonstrating significantly more precision than during his earlier battles. Rather than unleashing uncontrolled flames across the surrounding territory, Victor confined the destruction to the people and structures he had deliberately chosen to burn. His improved fire control reflected the months spent correcting the wasteful use of power Scathach had identified during his training.[135]
Clan Amon's mansion was already inside a cocoon of flame. Vampires who tried to cross it died. The clan leader screamed and asked what the monster was. Victor's eyes were blood-red and his body was on fire. He said that he normally liked a good fight, and that they were not worthy. He pointed his palm and said, "Turn to Ashes." A barrage left his hand. He then took a breath, pictured the place as the inside of a sun, and said, "...All creation turns to ashes." The wave reduced what he had chosen to ash. He dispelled the fire. The ground was black and burnt, and he was satisfied that he had controlled an attack of that size for the first time. His eyes went blood-red again and lightning covered him. He crossed the distance faster than a blink and caught the black owl by the head. He told whoever was watching that he did not care who they were, and that the moment he found them he would devour them. The skin of his face disappeared into a black outline, red eyes, sharp teeth and a distorted smile. His mouth grew out of proportion and he swallowed the owl whole. He said it tasted like bread and cheese.[135]
During the extermination Victor detected a black magical owl being used to observe him remotely. Instead of ignoring the surveillance, he addressed whoever was watching and destroyed the construct, deliberately transforming the destruction of Clan Amon into a warning. The surviving assassins captured earlier were not immediately killed; Victor later concluded that they could instead be used as practical opponents for his wives, who needed experience of their own rather than allowing Victor to personally fight every enemy who approached the family.[135][136]
Scathach separately followed the information trail to Clan Astharoth, an information-brokering Noble Clan involved in supplying intelligence connected to the assassination. She froze and destroyed the organization before discovering another of the same observation constructs. The conspiracy ultimately led toward [[Theo Tepes]] and Radu Tepes, who had wanted to observe the new Count and determine how he would react to being targeted.[136]
Niklaus understood the result better than Theo. In his assessment, Victor possessed the same dangerous mentality that had made Scathach nearly impossible to control throughout vampire history. Victor was younger, rapidly improving and personally attached to Scathach, meaning antagonizing him risked creating another enemy who could eventually become even more troublesome than his master.[136]
With the immediate threat eliminated, Victor prepared to return to the Human World. The prospect unexpectedly made him nervous. His body had grown again during the six months in Nightingale, reaching approximately 195 centimetres, while the repeated use of his transformed states had left his eyes permanently red. The line said to him was exact: he was 195 cm tall now, and his eyes were blood red. Clan Astharoth did not get a battle. Scathach's gesture turned the leader into an ice sculpture, and the rest of the clan with him. [[Niklaus Horseman]] was the one watching both screens, Victor's and Scathach's. The killing intent still reached him from thousands of kilometres away. The implausible "late puberty" explanation previously given to his parents could no longer conceal what had happened.[136][137]
Victor briefly acknowledged that Charm could make the problem disappear, but immediately rejected using it on Leon or Anna. Manipulating enemies or strangers was acceptable to him; rewriting the thoughts of the parents who had loved and raised him despite his lifelong illness was not. Victor therefore decided to finally tell them the truth about becoming a vampire and about the supernatural world surrounding their family.[137]
