VOLUME 08

#### Volume 8: God Emperor Victor Elderblood
Chapters 986–1134

##### A New Generation in a Changing World
Chapters 986–1004
Two years had passed in the outside world since the fall of [[Asgard]], and Earth was almost unrecognizable compared to the planet Victor had once known. Working with the World Tree, his faction had driven pollution out of the seas and the ground until the planet looked closer to an age before industry. The influence of Victor Elderblood, the [[Dragons Nest Pantheon]] and the [[Blood God Religion]] had spread on a global scale. The relative peace did not erase the ambitions of the older Pantheons. A God of the [[Indian Pantheon|Hindu Pantheon]], recorded as [[Ganesha]], tried to take credit for the cleaning. [[Kaguya Elderblood Blank]] took his head in black fire, a mix of Darkness and Fire, and reduced it to atoms. War then stood before [[Shiva]]: about two and a half meters of plate, twelve wings of darkness, a face of endless dark and hundreds of thousands of eyes, and the silhouette of a great cat behind him. He delivered Victor's warning in the Emperor's own voice. Out of respect for Shiva, this one would pass. There would be no second chance. The shock let Shiva finish taking the Pantheon away from [[Indra]]. Belief in Victor's religion rose with it.[1038]
The greatest transformation, however, had occurred within Victor's own family. Although only two years had passed externally, Victor and many of those closest to him had experienced roughly two thousand years inside his Inner World. True Dragon children took about a thousand years to gestate, and stronger mothers took longer: about 1670 years for the daughters of [[Scathach Elderblood Scarlett]] and [[Otsuki Elderblood Haruna]], about 1900 for the daughters of [[Aphrodite]], [[Persephone]], [[Metis]], Nyx, [[Gaia]] and [[Hestia]], about 1950 for Velnorah's daughter, and about 1990 for the daughters of Anna and Jeanne. Only a few wives had children because of that wait. A body finished childhood around two thousand years, the teens around five thousand, and adulthood around ten thousand, while the mind was pushed faster by teaching. Victor sealed the daughters' powers so the household would not come apart. His own count stood at seventeen Divinities. Five were major: War, Destruction and Blood, all mastered; Negativity, still a beginner; Beginning, intermediate. Twelve were minor and mastered: Assassination, Strength, Beauty, Revenge, Martial Honor, [[Rex Invictus|Home]], Family, Nature, his obsessive Divinity, Creation, Dream and Madness. Among the children who could already be named, [[Valentina Victoria Elderblood]] was Violet's daughter, and Siren was [[Scathach]]'s. His wives had matured further as Goddesses, Progenitors and Dragons, and the household had produced an enormous second generation, including [[Rosemary Lavina Elderblood]], [[Silvia Elderblood]], [[Gina Elderblood]], [[Angelina Elderblood]], [[Nikolina Nia Nefela Elderblood]], [[Evelyn Elderblood]] and many others.[1039][1040][1041]
Victor's new status as God Emperor did little to restrain him as a father. He became intensely affectionate, indulgent and protective toward his daughters, while the girls themselves competed shamelessly for his attention. Their personalities also demonstrated that Victor had transmitted more than his power: several possessed his confidence, recklessness, possessiveness and refusal to accept limitations. [[Stella Elderblood]], the daughter of Victor and [[Anna Elderblood]], became a particularly troublesome example due to her extraordinary ability to interfere with Reality; despite that power, the threat of Scathach reporting her misbehavior to Victor remained enough to make her immediately behave. Victor nevertheless refused to view his children simply as future weapons. He spent time observing their individual personalities, aspirations and abilities, while the older members of the family slowly adjusted to the realization that the next Elderblood generation could eventually become a faction of exceptional beings in its own right.[1041][1042][1043]
The changes within the family also forced [[Leon Walker]] to confront how thoroughly his old life had ended. After discovering Stella and seeing Anna's new family firsthand, Leon spoke privately with Victor and Anna about the years that had passed. Anna acknowledged that whatever remained of their former marriage could no longer be treated as an active relationship, while Leon accepted that both of them had moved onto completely different lives. Victor nevertheless continued treating Leon as family because of their shared history, although Anna made clear that this privileged position did not give him freedom to behave disrespectfully toward Victor's wives or children. Rather than reducing Anna to her former identity as Leon's wife, these conversations emphasized how much she herself had changed: she was now one of Victor's wives, a Dragon Goddess and an Empress whose responsibilities and worldview had expanded far beyond her old human life.[1044][1045][1046][1047]
Life inside the Elderblood household continued to reveal the almost absurd scale of Victor's family. Daughters from different mothers gathered around one another as sisters, Victor was repeatedly overwhelmed by their demands for affection, and even his wives maintained their own private communication network in order to coordinate an increasingly complicated household. [[Azathoth Elderblood]], despite remaining physically separated from Victor, managed to intrude into that network through an avatar, further demonstrating how close her connection to Victor had become. The family was no longer simply a collection of Victor's lovers and allies; after thousands of subjective years, it had begun functioning as its own enormous civilization-scale dynasty.[1048][1049][1050][1051][1052][1053]
That same principle extended into government. Victor did not intend to personally control every insignificant decision made within his territory, and he deliberately allowed his wives, daughters and trusted subordinates to act independently. Nevertheless, everyone understood that the Emperor's [[Will Solace|Will]] stood above every lesser institution when matters capable of affecting the Empire as a whole were involved. Kaguya and the other women around him could therefore issue commands carrying Imperial authority without waiting for Victor to personally supervise every action. Victor was capable of observing far more than he normally chose to, but deliberately preferred trust, responsibility and competence over turning his family into puppets monitored every second of their lives.[1054][1055]
The technological expression of Victor's new civilization appeared through Velnorah and her daughter, [[Velina Velnorah Elderblood Thaloria III]]. Over about two weeks they had built a prototype infinite battery. Victor drove dark-violet slime from his fingers into it, laid Draconic runes over it, and set a piece of his Soul inside so it would hold. The sphere became a living icosahedron about ten meters across. Output began at the prototype's full rate and climbed through ten thousand percent and past it, as pure Energy that could be given any property afterward. It was tied to him and was not a part of his body: destroying it would not wound him, and it was close to indestructible. Any sentient thing made with that Energy stayed inside his domain, and he could end it with a thought. Velina's later idea, an intelligence that would be his daughter rather than a tool, pointed straight at Akasha. What began as a battery became the [[Dragon Heart]], the core the Empire would build on.[1056]

##### Lessons in Divinity
Chapters 1005–1019
With the younger generation established, Victor began paying particular attention to [[Nero Elderblood]] and [[Ophis Tepes Elderblood]]. Both possessed extraordinary inherited potential, but Victor considered power without self-understanding dangerous and incomplete. [[Jeanne Elderblood]] therefore taught them about Gods, Divinities and the relationship between an individual's nature and the Concept they embody. A true Divinity could not be reduced to receiving a convenient ability; the God needed to understand what the Concept represented and how that Concept related to the self.[1057][1058]
Victor transformed those lessons into practical trials. Using his authorities over Dreams and other aspects of Reality, he constructed artificial circumstances in which [[Nero]] and Ophis could experience lives radically different from their normal existence as Victor's overwhelmingly protected daughters. Their normal advantages were stripped away or altered, forcing both girls to confront fear, helplessness, attachment and their own identities rather than simply overwhelming every obstacle with inherited strength. Nero's scenario repeatedly resisted her attempts to break free, but the pressure instead began awakening something even Victor had not completely anticipated. The Energy responding to Nero was connected not merely to ordinary native Divinity, but to the Eldritch side of Victor's existence.[1059][1060][1061]
Ophis' trial became much more personal. The artificial reality allowed her to encounter her deceased birth mother, [[Otsuki Hana]], placing Ophis in front of the woman whose loss had shaped much of her earliest life. Hana's extreme maternal instincts resurfaced immediately; she attempted to protect and isolate Ophis from everyone she perceived as a threat, while Ophis emotionally regressed around the mother she had lost. Yet the child Hana remembered no longer existed. The power developing within Ophis had become so immense that even powerful beings around her could instinctively perceive danger from the girl Hana still wanted to protect.[1062][1063][1061][1064]
Ophis' developing Divinity was connected to Infinity, placing her on a path radically beyond the ordinary Vampire she had once been. The experience nevertheless mattered for more than power. Victor's recreation allowed Ophis to confront emotions surrounding Hana that had never been properly resolved. [[Otsuki Elderblood Haruna]] was also forced to confront her own grief and the possibility of seeing her sister again. Victor promised them that the artificial encounter was not intended to replace Hana forever; once the danger involving Azathoth and the greater problems surrounding their existence had been resolved, he intended to pursue Hana's genuine restoration.[1064][1065][1066]
The trials produced an even greater revelation through Nero. Victor's daughters had inherited more than his Dragon physiology or Divine potential. Because Victor himself had become something foreign to the ordinary structure of the Cosmos, that foreign nature could also be passed to his descendants. Nero's emerging Divinity developed Eldritch characteristics and ultimately manifested around the idea of Apocalypse—large-scale calamity, catastrophe and the conditions that produce an ending. Unlike an ordinary native Divinity that existed entirely within the established hierarchy of the Cosmos, Nero's developing authority was rooted through Victor and therefore did not interact with the Rules of Existence in exactly the same manner as conventional Gods.[1061][1067][1068][1069][1070]
[[Azathoth Elderblood]] consequently explained more clearly what Victor was becoming. He was an outer god of this Creation as well as a high god inside it, an Eldritch [[Chaos]] that could feed on Divinities the way he already fed on remnants such as Positivity and Negativity. That kind of being can eat Creation and keep growing until the Reality that made him no longer holds him. Eldritch Gods distort Rules and cannot be removed the way a native God can, because Chaos is part of the foundation. Another Chaos can answer them. Primordials administer a universe. They do not erase that foundation. Victor was still immature by the standard of a finished Eldritch Chaos. Turning a mature native Goddess into the same kind of outsider was harder than letting a daughter grow into it from the start.[1067][1068]
The implications did not escape Kali. For an immense portion of her existence, she had pursued deeper mastery over Destruction and the possibility of reaching the level of a genuine Primordial Entity. Watching Victor and his daughters revealed an alternative path—one that did not necessarily require following every limitation established by the native cosmological system. Kali's interest in Victor therefore became increasingly tied not only to his strength, but to his ability to perceive possibilities that beings far older than him had accepted as impossible.[1071]

##### Faith, Rewards and the Shape of an Empire
Chapters 1020–1032
Victor's treatment of [[Valeria Alekerth]] demonstrated another side of his rule. Valeria had served the [[Blood God Religion]] with exceptional loyalty while never demanding repayment for the loss of her daughter, [[Vanessa Alekerth]]. Victor had not forgotten. Through his authority over Souls, the information preserved within the Akashic system and negotiations involving [[The Judges of The Abyss]], Victor acquired what was necessary to reconstruct Vanessa's existence. The process included obtaining the positive and negative aspects required for her Soul in exchange for one thousand supernatural Souls, after which the Records of her previous existence could be used to restore the identity that had been lost.[1072][1073]
The resurrection embodied one of the most consistent principles of Victor's character as Emperor: he remembered kindness as obsessively as he remembered hostility. Valeria had given him loyalty without demanding a reward, so Victor gave her something she had believed permanently impossible. At the same time, the Blood God Religion was becoming much larger than a conventional cult. It possessed military personnel, bases, ranks, artifacts and followers who genuinely believed that service to Victor could alter their destiny. Their faith was strengthened further when the overwhelming scale of their God ceased being an abstract idea and became something they could physically witness.[1072][1073][1074]
A suspicious artifact recovered by Valeria exposed activity connected to the Celts and other Gods. Rather than carelessly touching it, she followed the procedures established for potentially cursed Divine objects, allowing [[Violet Elderblood Snow]] to examine it. Violet confirmed the presence of a curse and provided the religion with a version of the Empire's [[City Core]] technology, allowing territory to be monitored while deliberately keeping the base vulnerable enough to attract enemy spies rather than frightening every observer away. Shortly afterward, Victor's enormous Dragon form became visible across the horizon. To his followers, the sight became direct proof that the God they worshipped truly watched over them; to independent supernatural powers, it became a terrifying demonstration of how insignificant conventional Divine strength had become beside him. [[Shiva]] used the display to finally force [[Indra]] to understand the political reality: Victor could no longer be treated as simply another God-King competing for influence on Earth.[1074][1075]
Victor then personally brought Vanessa into the Paradise prepared for his faithful and reunited mother and daughter. Valeria was allowed to abandon her responsibilities temporarily and remain with Vanessa for several days, while Victor himself dealt with portions of the enormous institution she usually administered. The experience reinforced both how important Valeria had become to the day-to-day function of the religion and how dramatically Victor's worship had developed from the small group of followers it had once been.[1076][1077][1078]
His attention subsequently moved from spiritual salvation to biological development. Rena, a Werewolf descended from the Lykos lineage, became an example of Victor's refusal to accept inherited racial weaknesses simply because they had existed for thousands of years. Examining her body, bloodline and potential, Victor used his authorities to reconstruct her into a superior form of Werewolf capable of functioning far beyond the limits traditionally associated with the species. Her development included a superior Alpha state, greatly improved adaptation and a form no longer dependent upon the normal circumstances required by ordinary [[Werewolves]]. Victor was beginning to treat entire racial systems the same way he treated techniques or technology: something that could be understood, corrected and improved.[1079][1080][1081]
The increasingly organized Blood God Religion reflected the same philosophy. Becoming an Archbishop required more than possessing intense Faith. Victor expected capability, discipline, loyalty and the ability to actually shoulder authority. Faith could open opportunities, but incompetence was not transformed into merit simply because someone worshipped him sincerely.[1082] [[Kaguya Elderblood Blank]] continued embodying this standard among Victor's closest followers, combining her duties as wife, chief maid and executor of the Emperor's [[Will Solace|Will]] with power that had grown far beyond what she possessed during Victor's earliest years.[1083]
Even the [[World Trees]] connected to Victor were developing increasingly individual emotions. [[Amara Elderblood]] occasionally displayed jealousy toward [[Roxanne Elderblood]], revealing how their immense cosmic nature did not prevent them from acquiring distinctly personal attachments to Victor. The situation was representative of the increasingly strange family around him: beings who once represented planets, Divinities, ancient races or cosmic systems were gradually becoming people whose loyalties and emotions revolved around the same household.[1084]

##### Training Beyond Old Limits
Chapters 1033–1040
Kali eventually demanded that Victor stop treating her advancement as a purely theoretical problem and fight her seriously enough to expose what she still lacked. Her existence had already begun approaching an unusual border between Goddess and Primordial-like being: her body and Power were increasingly identified with Destruction itself, yet she had not crossed the threshold into becoming the impersonal cosmic mechanism represented by a true Primordial Entity. Victor saw this not as proof that she had reached an unavoidable ceiling, but as another problem whose structure needed to be understood.[1085][1086]
Their confrontation displayed how absurd the difference between Victor's raw capability and conventional Divine combat had become. Kali opened at about half her strength, fist wrapped in Destruction, and Victor caught it without stepping off his mark. She then ran a full martial sequence—animal shapes, Kalari, Chinese forms, pressure points driven into his stomach—and he did not use his left hand or leave the spot. He turned her blows aside with elbow and palm. When she wrapped herself in a pillar of crimson light and fired a concentrated beam, he punched the air, bent the space in front of the beam, and sent it back into her. He never called Destruction, Creation, Beginning or Positivity. In that human-like shape his pressure points were not where a human body keeps them, because the body underneath was a Dragon shapeshifter. Kali learned she was being read, not fought.[1086][1087]
The result was the formal development of the [[Seven Arts of the Blood Dragon Primogenitor]]. These were not copies of [[Scathach Elderblood Scarlett]]'s martial teachings. They only sit on a body that already distorts Reality, so ordinary races cannot use them without tearing themselves apart. The first art makes a solid surface out of distorted space, so the user can stand on air. The second is close combat that bends Reality on a small scale without a spoken word, so a blow of that strength does not throw a shockwave. The third takes those skills and drives them harder, until a punch or a kick opens a small hole in Reality. The fourth runs Energy in a loop like an Ouroboros, spending almost nothing and letting a controlled leak move the body before conscious thought. The fifth closes the leaks until the loop is complete. The sixth feeds that loop into the Soul and binds loose Soul-fragments into it. The seventh seats those hardened Soul-aspects in the body, and in a weapon, so the Soul is not naked in a clash. Only [[Junketsu]] was said to survive the pressure of that last step. Victor meant to add a level zero later, for bare movement, because the arts kill a student who enters them unready. Anna, [[Scathach]], Rose and Victor locked the system at the highest secrecy. A daughter learns it only with the Emperor, the Grandmasters and two Empresses in agreement, and only under a Grandmaster or under Victor. A daughter who teaches it without leave is distanced from him. A stranger is exiled or has the memory taken.[1088]
Creating the Seven Arts did not solve Victor's own stagnation. Despite training for immense subjective periods, he had failed to progress beyond his existing Grandmaster state. Sparring and training with warriors such as Scathach, Rose, Haruna and Morgana finally allowed him to perceive the obstacle more clearly. In his internal perception, progress appeared as enormous damaged gates standing in his path. Versions of Victor representing different stages and aspects of his existence—including his Vampire self and the Eldritch monstrosity within him—reached the same conclusion: a limitation simply existing was not sufficient reason to accept it.[1089][1090][1091]
Yet destroying the obstacle was not merely a matter of forcing more Power into it. Victor recognized that he had spent so much time accumulating advanced abilities that the foundations supporting them required equal refinement. Like a structure attempting to rise without sufficiently strong pillars, further advancement demanded returning to the fundamentals that had created his martial path in the first place. He therefore revisited the simplest movements, stances and principles behind his swordsmanship and combat instead of chasing another exotic ability. The realization became one of the most important features of Victor's martial development: reaching higher stages did not make the basics obsolete; it made perfect understanding of those basics even more necessary.[1091][1092]

##### Heaven, Old Wounds and a New Protector
Chapters 1041–1050
Events then shifted toward Heaven. The Angels were no longer as simple as the perfectly obedient servants many outsiders imagined them to be. Exposure to other people and experiences had encouraged increasing individuality, emotion and personal judgment among them. Ariel, despite being one of the [[Heavenly Father]]'s greatest Angels, found interacting with Victor's family far more intimidating than fighting ordinary enemies. Surrounded by Dragon Goddesses whose possessiveness toward Victor could become genuinely dangerous, Ariel was forced to confront a household governed by completely different social rules from Heaven.[1093][1094]
The meeting also exposed important differences among Victor's wives. Some responded to Heaven and the Angels with predatory or aggressively pragmatic suggestions, while others—including Sasha and Anna—rejected harming innocent beings merely because Victor possessed the strength to do so. Anna emphasized that Victor respected the Heavenly Father and would not attack Heaven without an actual reason. The discussion illustrated an important reality of the Elderblood family: Victor's wives were not a uniform collective sharing one morality. They disagreed, argued and possessed radically different instincts, but ultimately understood that major actions affecting other civilizations remained subject to Victor's judgment and the principles governing their family. In the same period the wives clarified the structure of their household to Ariel. It was a harem, not polyamory. The women regarded one another as sisters and family, not as lovers. Intimacy occurred exclusively with Victor. Rare group sessions happened only when he was especially frustrated after long absences or training, and only with him present. Variety with him was accepted to avoid monotony across millennia, but individual attention remained the norm for most.[1094][1095][1096]
Victor himself interacted directly with the Heavenly Father within the higher levels of Heaven, discussing the increasingly complicated relationship among the surviving Pantheons and the beings under his protection. Around the same period, [[Mizuki Elderblood]] returned to Victor's immediate life. The woman who had once nearly killed him as an Inquisition General now stood on the opposite side of their former relationship, ultimately being welcomed into the family she once would have considered composed of monsters.[1097][1098]
Mizuki's history explained why that change was so significant. Her hatred toward Vampires and supernatural monsters had not originated from abstract prejudice. As a child she had experienced captivity, violence and the destruction of the safety that should have surrounded her family, forcing her to understand at an early age that supernatural predators could treat ordinary Humans as possessions. Her later discipline, hatred and willingness to become a monster hunter were built upon the conviction that she would never again remain the helpless child who could do nothing while monsters controlled her life.[1099][1100]
Victor did not attempt to rewrite that history simply because he had become a Vampire and she had become part of his family. His own morality had never required believing that Vampires were inherently good. A Vampire, Human, Demon, Angel or God who became an enemy of his people could still be treated as an enemy. Mizuki's acceptance therefore represented a much greater change than abandoning one species for another; she had learned to distinguish the individual from the race she once hated collectively.[1100][1101]
The problem of protecting an Empire that was becoming too vast for any single administrator then produced another major development. Victor and Velnorah were increasingly exposed to the scale of civilizations and infrastructure that existed beyond ordinary planetary societies, making it clear that Dragons Nest required a guardian capable of operating throughout the entire Imperial System rather than merely another conventional artificial intelligence.[1101][1102]
Victor consequently created [[Akasha Elderblood]]. She was not programmed software given a face. He made her from his Essence as an Eldritch daughter of his [[Primordial Chaos|Primal Chaos]], and he put the memories of [[Primordial Gods]] and his own memories into her at birth. She had no native Divine Concept, because she was not seated inside this Creation. Her domain was Control, and standing near her made other people lose their grip on themselves. The Heart of her Father fed her Energy and opened the Imperial systems. Her processing at the start was a vanishing fraction of what the network could hold. She could watch through screens, propose databases kept in other dimensions, store memories and Souls for later revival, and approach System only with caution. For the first years she was to obey her Mother, and her own well-being came before the job. Victor did not need her reports. He still wanted them, because they were time with her father. She was Overseer of the Empire, and she was his daughter before she was its machine.[1102][1103]
Akasha became the System's guardian and an Eldritch Goddess associated with Control. Her existence blurred the distinction between daughter, Goddess, artificial intelligence and living Imperial infrastructure. Where the [[Dragon Heart]] supplied the enormous Energy required by Victor's civilization, Akasha would increasingly become the intelligence capable of coordinating that civilization.[1103]

##### War Games and the Dark Beyond
Chapters 1051–1062
Victor next turned his attention toward a problem created by his daughters' privileged birth. Being born as [[Blood Dragons]] surrounded by some of the strongest beings in the Sector made it dangerously easy for them to depend upon overwhelming natural ability rather than adaptability. He put them into war games under rooms sealed with protective Runes the girls could not rewrite. [[Akasha Elderblood]] played by his orders to the letter and functioned as a check on the ones who treated the exercise as a game. [[Priscillia Penny Elderblood]], daughter of Victor and Pepper, went in with her mother's command and his own cruelty. Rosalyn and Amaya, miniature forms of Amara and Roxanne and therefore [[World Trees]] with almost no freedom of their own, were kept out. The rest were assigned races and roles they did not live in—[[Stella Elderblood]] as a Demi-Goddess, [[Rosemary Lavina Elderblood]] as a Fairy Queen, [[Gina Elderblood]] as a Dryad, [[Yuno Elderblood]] as a Necromancer—so that bloodline alone could not win the room.[1104][1105][1106]
The exercise was intended to teach strategy, cooperation and the ability to exploit limited resources. Predictably, the Elderblood daughters converted it into an intensely competitive family conflict. Their mothers observed, interfered and reacted to the girls' decisions while Victor allowed the scenario to evolve rather than guaranteeing that everything followed his original plan. The purpose was precisely to make them deal with situations where possessing the best bloodline in the room was not an automatic solution.[1106][1107]
Victor then extended the exercise through shared Dreams, allowing several family members to experience environments and training conditions together without requiring the same passage of physical time. What began as another carefully controlled method of education nevertheless produced events outside the original expectations of the observers, pushing the family toward regions and phenomena that had previously received little attention.[1108][1109][1110][1111]
The resulting discoveries drew Victor toward the regions associated with true cosmic death. Hela explained the waste left when galaxies died: regions around supermassive black holes where Life, Time, Space and even the ordinary Void had stopped meaning anything. Only darkness remained, and things that could live in it. Most civilizations called those places worthless. Victor did not. He walked through a portal into the Domain of Primordial Death and went to bargain with what lived there.[1112]
Victor entered territory associated with [[True Death]] and encountered entities whose existence more closely resembled the abnormal creatures of the Abyss than ordinary Gods or species. The one he chose was called the little one by the standards of that place: a mass of eyes and darkness, among the oldest there and still the smallest and weakest. Its power soaked a target in a corruptive negative effect. Weaker beings died of the exhaustion of the mind. He did not bind it with a written pact in that meeting. He picked it as a companion for a daughter and left.[1113]
These events also returned attention to Victor's Soul. What had begun long ago as an internal mental world had expanded together with him until ordinary descriptions of a Soul were increasingly inadequate. His internal existence could contain separate spaces, systems and manifestations of himself while supporting contradictory forms of power that would destroy conventional beings. Hela and others were forced to recognize that looking at Victor only through his physical body gave an incomplete picture of what the Emperor had become.[1114][1115]

##### Soldiers for a Larger Future
Chapters 1063–1079
The political order of Earth continued collapsing into Victor's sphere of influence. [[Indra]], whose choices had repeatedly placed the [[Indian Pantheon|Hindu Pantheon]] in increasingly untenable positions, finally relinquished leadership and [[Shiva]] assumed the role of God-King. The change represented more than an internal succession: even one of Earth's oldest Pantheons now had to organize itself around a world in which Victor's power had become the dominant political fact.[1116]
Victor's view of Divinity likewise continued becoming more pragmatic. He rejected the assumption that becoming a God inherently made an individual wiser, kinder or more worthy. Gods possessed greater lifespan, authority and opportunity, but they remained capable of pettiness, stupidity, ambition and cruelty. Mortals and Gods differed enormously in capability, yet power did not automatically correct character.[1117] [[Kaguya Elderblood Blank]] continued serving as one of the clearest examples of what Victor actually valued: competence, loyalty and the ability to execute his [[Will Solace|Will]] without requiring constant supervision.[1118]
The same standards influenced the construction of Victor's future military. He could not stamp copies of himself. His Soul, blood and flesh were poison to anyone who was not already bound to him, and a stranger who tried to take them died badly. The commanders were built instead as a mix: a Dragonoid frame about four meters tall, Human adaptability so a Soul could sit in it, Angelic obedience, a Faery tie to Nature and to him, and a fraction of his Soul so small it was written as 0.0000001 percent. Demonic cruelty was left out because it made them hard to command. Souls were edited before they were grown. Only people he authorized could copy their pattern. The first of them was John, codename [[John-000]], who was given no family name. [[Clare Bloodhunter]] was logged as C-000. With them came [[Laura Bloodhunter]], [[Kiana Bloodhunter]], Conan, [[Kaleb Hunter]] and [[Caelus Hunter]]. They were elite commanders, not a mob of disposable bodies, and they belonged to the Empire rather than to any one wife's private army.[1119]
They were built as commanders who could lead the clone armies, and they belonged to the Empire rather than to any one wife's private force.[1120][1121][1122]
Domestic developments continued beside these military projects, with the Snow family and Victor's other wives ensuring that the Emperor's household remained almost as unpredictable as his conquests.[1123] Victor also discussed Humanity with [[Poseidon]], returning to one of the ideas repeatedly reinforced throughout his life: power did not necessarily corrupt someone into a completely different person. Very often it simply gave a person the ability to act upon desires that weakness, fear or law had previously forced them to suppress. Humans were therefore fully capable of becoming as monstrous as the supernatural creatures they feared if given sufficient power and opportunity.[1124][1125]
After the remaining matter involving Poseidon was dealt with, Victor turned toward the World of Water. He did not alter an old sea. Creation was the material and Beginning was the boost. He spoke them into a dimension of water that sat apart from his planet and inside his Soul: from the water they were born, and with water they brought life and destruction. What came out were leviathans of the depths, proud in the way Dragons are proud and not Dragons. They carried the will of the Blood Dragon Progenitor and sat under a sub-concept of Beginning, the one that makes monsters. They were tied to [[Chaos]] and were not given Souls that would enter reincarnation, because the Judges of the Abyss would not take that extra load. The Primordial of Life gave permission. The Primordial of Soul gave it unwillingly. The Judges called Hand, Eye and Mouth were present. Time in that dimension stopped for everyone except administrators, and Victor still moved. [[Roxanne Elderblood]] and [[Amara Elderblood]] carried the Energy cost, which was already pressing toward a Primordial scale. The people of his world, apart from those in the Nightmare Tower or in his dream, heard the proclamation and were brought across. [[Amaterasu]], [[Gaia]] and Nyx watched from outside.[1126]
His unusual status also affected his dealings with the cosmic powers surrounding death and the Abyss. Victor understood that the mere possibility of involving [[Azathoth Elderblood]] could frighten entities that would normally have little reason to care about the threats of native Gods.[1127] Azathoth subsequently provided him with further context concerning the larger cosmological structure. Separate Creations could possess their own laws, Primordials and Chaos, and the beings who embodied the fundamental functions of a Cosmos could not be treated exactly like ordinary Gods.[1128][1129]
Removing a true Primordial such as Life, Death or another fundamental principle without replacing the function it embodied could cripple the Cosmos dependent upon it. Victor therefore began thinking beyond the simplistic objective of "killing" a Regulator. If the consciousness occupying a cosmic office could be separated from the function necessary for Creation, then replacing or controlling that administrator became theoretically more useful than destroying the principle itself. This distinction would become increasingly important as Victor's ambitions grew beyond fighting individual Gods.[1128][1129]
His Eldritch characteristics simultaneously allowed him to violate assumptions that constrained beings entirely produced by the native system, reinforcing his growing conviction that the Rules of Existence were mechanisms rather than sacred absolutes.[1130] The following developments also revisited Humanity and the existence of exceptional humans whose potential did not fit the limitations associated with weakened modern mankind, reminding Victor that "Human" described an origin rather than a universally low ceiling.[1131][1132]

##### A World Moving Under One Banner
Chapters 1080–1087
Victor's Empire finally began eliminating the fragmented political order that had defined supernatural Earth for millennia. The growth was not only conquest of borders. He marked chosen Dragons with violet beams and laid incomplete copies of Divinities he had already eaten onto them, including a derivative of a God of Fear, as support and as a reason to keep growing. Humans who had been given to that God were thrown through a gate into Hell. This was not merely another war between Pantheons. Victor intended to end the system in which dozens of Divine factions possessed overlapping claims over the same planet while constantly dragging mortals into their rivalries.[1133][1134][1135][1136][1137]
The [[Indian Pantheon|Hindu Pantheon]] represented the largest remaining question. Victor entered its territory without suppressing his presence to the level normally expected during negotiations, forcing its Gods to experience directly how enormous the difference between them had become. When the possibility of maintaining a simple alliance was raised, Victor rejected the idea that two powers separated by such an extreme difference could meaningfully call themselves equal partners. He offered a far simpler choice: surrender sovereignty and become part of his Empire, or resist and be destroyed, after which the power and Divinities of the defeated Gods would become resources for those under him.[1138]
[[Shiva]] understood that resistance would accomplish little beyond killing his people. The Hindu Pantheon therefore submitted rather than forcing Victor to demonstrate his superiority through annihilation. With the major supernatural territories of Earth either absorbed, subordinated or aligned beneath his order, Victor formally established the [[Elderblood Empire]] as the governing power of the planet. Earth itself was renamed [[Yggdrasil]], and the old calendar was replaced by the [[Imperial Calendar]], beginning from Year One of the new civilization.[1138][1139]
The new order was not intended to be a Vampire Empire with other species tolerated beneath it. Victor established Imperial identity above racial identity. Vampires, [[Werewolves]], Demons, Angels, Witches and other races who belonged to the Empire were citizens first, and racial discrimination capable of destabilizing that unity was treated as a serious crime. The state simultaneously developed a military structure around enhanced soldiers and Dragonoid forces designed for wars far beyond planetary battlefields.[1140]
Victor's Hell was also incorporated into this legal philosophy. Crimes were judged through the standards of his Empire rather than the traditions of any single species or Pantheon, with acts such as treason against the Emperor, abuse of children, sexual violence, experimentation upon citizens and severe racial persecution placed among the crimes deserving the harshest consequences. Victor's civilization was authoritarian in the most literal sense—his [[Will Solace|Will]] remained the final law—but that law was increasingly being transformed into an institutional system rather than depending upon Victor personally appearing every time someone committed a crime.[1140]
The greater System consequently recognized the scale of what had occurred. Victor was no longer simply the strongest God or Emperor on Yggdrasil; he had established himself as the effective Overlord of his Sector. His responsibilities and enemies would therefore no longer be measured on the scale of a single planet. The civilization that had begun with a newly awakened Vampire in [[Nightingale]] was preparing to compete across an entire cosmic region.[1139][1140]

##### The Empire's Race Against Time
Chapters 1088–1093
Becoming Overlord exposed a fundamental problem. Victor's civilization had become powerful with extraordinary speed, but the wider Universe contained civilizations that had been developing for periods almost impossible for ordinary Humans to comprehend. Victor could personally become monstrously powerful in a comparatively short time, yet an Empire required scientists, soldiers, populations, infrastructure, education, culture, industry and countless specialists. Those things could not all be replaced by the Emperor simply becoming stronger.[1141]
Victor also reflected upon Time itself as one of the greatest forces driving change. Immortal Gods could spend tens or hundreds of thousands of years repeating the same behavior precisely because the passage of time no longer pressured them as it did mortals. Many ancient beings stagnated not because they lacked potential, but because eternity gave them little incentive to transform. Victor's own faction had changed rapidly because its members were repeatedly exposed to new worlds, enemies, relationships and crises that forced adaptation.[1141]
The solution was characteristically excessive. Victor and his family began preparing an enormous project capable of altering the rate at which Time flowed throughout major portions of their civilization. Using the [[Dragon Heart]], Divine authorities, [[World Trees]], Runes, advanced technology and enormous quantities of Energy, the Empire could potentially experience centuries, millennia or more of internal development while much less Time passed outside the affected territory.[1142][1143]
[[Violet Elderblood Snow]] examined the political consequences of the coming expansion. Ordinary Empires frequently secured stability through arranged marriages among ruling families, but Victor categorically refused to turn his daughters into political currency. No alliance was valuable enough for him to marry one of his children to a stranger for convenience. Violet therefore had to design the Empire's diplomatic future around strength, technological advantage, mutually useful agreements and overwhelming internal unity rather than one of the most common tools used by hereditary civilizations.[1142][1143]
Victor's daughters were themselves becoming part of the solution. The girls who had previously existed primarily inside the protected Elderblood household increasingly wanted responsibilities of their own, creating tension between Victor's instinct to shelter them and the reality that many were already powerful enough to affect the Empire directly.[1144]
Construction planning escalated rapidly. Entire planetary systems, World Trees, Divine craftsmen, Imperial researchers and the Dragon Heart's energy output were incorporated into calculations for the Time project. The structures necessary to affect such an enormous region could not simply be produced by a single spell; the Empire was engineering a civilization-scale mechanism intended to give its population the one resource even Victor could not normally create through conquest—time to mature.[1145][1146]

##### Family, Foundations and a New Understanding
Chapters 1094–1105
The Empire's preparations did not prevent the Elderblood family from continuing to expand. The Snow lineage produced another set of daughters, while several of Victor's children began insisting upon participating in Imperial affairs rather than remaining permanently protected by their parents. Violet in particular had to balance her own protectiveness with the knowledge that the younger generation would eventually need experience governing the civilization they were expected to inherit and defend.[1147]
Victor also used this comparatively peaceful period to resolve personal matters that had remained unfinished for years. Several women were forced to examine whether they regretted the paths that had brought them into Victor's family or the identities and relationships they had abandoned along the way. The resulting discussions emphasized that entering Victor's life did not magically erase the past. Choices had consequences and some relationships could not be restored to what they once were, but Victor had no interest in forcing people to mourn lives they genuinely no longer wished to live.[1148][1149][1150]
His interactions with Ariel similarly explored the distinction between attraction and love. Victor did not consider desire, physical compatibility or fascination with someone's power sufficient to constitute genuine love. To him, love required knowing another person beyond the traits that were easy to admire—trusting them, enduring their flaws, accepting their unpleasant qualities and continuing to care about the person rather than an idealized image of them.[1151][1152]
Attention then returned to Imperial development. The Empire's scientific structure was becoming increasingly formalized, with specialized departments devoted to subjects such as weapons, biology and other fields. Figures such as Ruby, Aline and Velnorah participated in research alongside artificial personnel and clone-based workforces capable of performing tasks at a scale unavailable to ordinary laboratories. Violet's desire to minimize corruption and disloyalty also meant that the highest levels of sensitive research remained heavily connected to members of Victor's family and people whose loyalty had already been proven.[1153]
The [[World Core]] and the relationship among planets, their [[World Trees]] and the Energy systems supporting life became increasingly relevant to Imperial expansion. Victor's civilization was no longer planning around isolated cities or even single planets; it needed to understand the mechanisms that allowed entire living worlds to function if those worlds were going to be incorporated, protected or reconstructed on a large scale.[1153]
Meanwhile, Victor's daughters continued forming relationships independent of the identities of their mothers. Girls born from radically different races and Divine lineages increasingly regarded one another simply as sisters of the same Elderblood family. The appearance of twins and additional children only made that network more complicated, but it also demonstrated why Victor considered familial unity one of the strongest foundations available to his Empire. During this period Ariel experienced an extended intimate session with Victor lasting roughly fifteen hundred years of subjective time inside a Time Dome, made possible in part by a Concept of Love left in her soul. Her body changed under the combination of the race transformation and the prolonged contact: breasts and hips grew, skin brightened, and her hair lengthened to her ankles. She was later joined by other wives in a group encounter. Nyx observed naked from the side. The liquids and marks of the session were cleaned by Victor's authority once it ended.[1154][1155]
One of Victor's remaining loose ends involved the reincarnated Soul associated with [[Merlin]]. Through the intervention and reconstruction performed by [[The Universal Tree]], the fundamental structure of the Soul changed so extensively that the resulting existence could no longer meaningfully be treated as the original Merlin simply returned to life. Victor accepted the new being as a daughter and named her [[Melida Charlotte Elderblood]].[1156][1157]
Charlotte immediately displayed extraordinary intelligence and an almost instinctive capacity to comprehend Energy. Her existence became the catalyst for one of Victor's most important realizations. Instead of treating Fire Energy, [[Divine Energy]], Time, Space and the countless other supernatural powers of Creation as entirely unrelated substances, Victor began perceiving them as different characteristics imposed upon a more fundamental medium.[1157][1158]
The principle could be understood as a blank canvas being given different paints. Before an Energy possessed the attribute of Fire, Death, Life, Space or another phenomenon, there existed a more fundamental state upon which those properties could be imposed. Victor connected this principle to the work of [[Primordial Chaos]], whose role in establishing Creation involved producing structure and characteristics from what originally lacked them. Through this understanding, Victor obtained access to Attributeless Energy—also associated with [[Creator's Energy Mastery]]—and gained a new perspective on the common foundation beneath apparently incompatible supernatural systems.[1158]
This breakthrough was more important than simply acquiring another Energy type. Victor had spent much of his life learning to wield an enormous number of different powers. Understanding the substrate beneath those powers offered the possibility of creating the required characteristics himself rather than remaining dependent upon finding and absorbing every specialized form individually.[1158]

##### Preparing for the Wider Universe
Chapters 1106–1123
Victor's growing civilization continued absorbing useful individuals rather than automatically exterminating everyone connected to defeated factions. Gods and former enemies willing to accept the Imperial order could receive new opportunities, while beings such as Yama chose to begin again from a lower position rather than cling to titles that meant little beside the civilization Victor was creating. Submission did not guarantee prestige, but usefulness, loyalty and continued growth could create a place even for people who had once stood outside Victor's faction.[1159]
Victor and [[Scathach]] simultaneously returned to the question of martial advancement. Grandmaster had once appeared close to the summit of martial knowledge, yet neither of them accepted the idea that an art based upon understanding could possess an arbitrary final stage. Their investigation into what existed above Grandmaster continued the lesson Victor had rediscovered earlier: greater power did not replace technique, and the path forward depended upon changing the practitioner's understanding rather than simply accumulating additional Energy. Between sessions Victor pulled Scathach close for a long kiss that lasted minutes and formed a visible bridge of connection when they parted. He then kissed and teased her neck until she moaned. She was already carrying his seed from an earlier encounter. The moment mixed martial discussion with possessiveness and affection; she controlled the resulting desire rather than acting on it immediately.[1160][1161]
Violet continued managing another kind of expansion—the Elderblood family itself. Women who had already developed close relationships with Victor were increasingly brought into the family structure rather than remaining indefinitely in an ambiguous position. Even the [[World Trees]] became more openly possessive of Victor, demonstrating that cosmic age and planetary scale were apparently no protection against the obsessive tendencies common throughout his household.[1162][1163][1164]
Imperial expansion then moved decisively beyond its original worlds. John led a silent sweep of another planet. Stealth troops, some of them three meters tall, cleared the high officers of bases across the globe in seconds and took the useful ones into subspace. An orbital shot of disruptor munitions killed a huge artifact of blue Energy and blacked out the northern sector. That woke nine [[Ahishahu]], dragon-like manifestations of Nature that the local Gods had been using as power sources. The order that followed was to capture them, not to burn the world empty. Victor no longer needed to personally descend upon every world the Empire encountered.[1165]
[[Akasha Elderblood]] was essential to making such expansion manageable. The central intelligence she represented operated alongside enormous numbers of subordinate artificial intelligences and human or supernatural operators, connecting military, scientific and governmental information throughout the Empire. The objective was not simply to conquer planets faster than they could be administered, but to construct a network capable of continuing to function when the Empire eventually spread across galaxies.[1166][1167]
Future reforms consequently dealt with administration, education, racial integration, merit, military organization and the distribution of resources throughout an increasingly diverse population. Victor's Empire was transitioning from a coalition centered upon his family into a state intended to survive sustained interstellar expansion.[1166][1167]
Amid the cosmic preparations, Victor reunited with three of the most important companions from his human life: [[Frederick Winter]], [[Edward Jonathan Elizabeth Lykos|Edward Lykos]] and [[Andrew Walter]]. Their reunion highlighted how radically Victor's path had diverged from those of his friends. Frederick had become powerful by ordinary standards, yet Victor considered his progress embarrassingly inadequate relative to the opportunities and body he possessed. The Emperor's solution was characteristically simple: if his friend had wasted his potential, Victor would personally ensure that the opportunity was no longer wasted.[1168][1169][1170]
The reunion also returned to the question of whether power had changed Victor. Frederick's conclusion was closer to the opposite: power had primarily allowed Victor to become a more complete version of what he had always been. He still answered hostility with hostility, remembered kindness, protected the people he considered his own and became violently intolerant of threats toward them. What had changed was the scale on which those traits could now affect Reality.[1168]
Faith became particularly relevant to Frederick and Andrew. Victor's religion differed from many old mortal religions because the Gods surrounding it demonstrably existed and could visibly respond to their followers. Frederick discovered that placing his Faith in Victor considerably strengthened techniques that depended upon such spiritual connections. Victor in turn Blessed his old companions, assuring them that genuine Faith in him would remain meaningful even if their journeys eventually took them into distant worlds or dangerous regions far from [[Yggdrasil]].[1171]
[[Leona Elizabeth Elderblood Lykos]] subsequently spent time with Victor and his family, while more of the younger Elderblood generation continued appearing and integrating with their sisters.[1172][1173] Despite the sheer number of wives, daughters, races, former enemies, Goddesses and ancient beings involved, the household maintained a surprising degree of harmony because nearly everyone accepted several central rules: the family came first, betrayal was intolerable and rivalry was acceptable only so long as it did not become genuine hostility capable of destroying the whole.[1174][1175]
Violet finally addressed several relationships that had remained unresolved. She gave Kali, [[Albedo Moriarty Elderblood]] and [[Dún Scáith|Dun Scaith]] the opportunity to formally pursue Victor and potentially enter the family. Importantly, Violet's permission was not itself a marriage decree; whether any woman ultimately became Victor's wife still depended upon Victor and the relationship that developed between them. Kali accepted readily, explaining that Victor had helped her advance, allowed her to control Destruction sufficiently to live more normally and was one of the extremely few beings powerful enough to restrain her safely should she ever lose control.[1176]

##### Forbidden Knowledge and the First Step Beyond
Chapters 1124–1134
The closing portion of the volume shifted from preparing the Empire internally to confronting what existed beyond its familiar territory. Even Victor's family continued changing—Hela's circumstances added yet another future child to the already enormous household—but the Emperor increasingly focused upon questions that could not be answered by remaining inside the safe regions of his Sector.[1177]
[[Albedo Moriarty Elderblood]] became one of the people Victor deliberately exposed to that greater reality. Her obsession with knowledge made her exceptionally talented, but Victor understood that reading information and genuinely perceiving the scale of existence were different things. He brought her into environments between galaxies and exposed her to things that ordinary researchers would consider impossible, forcing Albedo to confront how limited the perspective of even an exceptional scientist could remain when all of her assumptions had been formed inside a relatively small region of the Cosmos.[1177][1178]
Victor's lesson was not simply to memorize another collection of forbidden facts. He wanted Albedo to learn how to see Reality without depending entirely upon the interpretations supplied by familiar senses and systems. Even abilities such as Eyes designed to reveal truth still operated through a particular framework. Understanding beings and phenomena that did not obey familiar rules required expanding the observer's perception rather than merely acquiring a larger library.[1178]
The practical reason for such preparation became clearer when the Empire followed evidence of outside interference into the Andromeda Galaxy. There they discovered the [[Skaarith Empire]], a world whose people had been rewritten by a virus that both strengthened them and kept them fighting. Two outside Emperors were using the planet as a war game, and outside spies were still in the population. The World's Tree was almost dead. The core was being drained as a battery, and a World Tree that is not fed back cannot keep a world alive. Velnorah commanded the fleet. Orbital fire wiped the infected population. Dragonoids took samples. She still hunted for what was left of the Tree, because a living Tree, and the biological record in it, was the only road back to the people the planet had been before the experiment.[1179]
Victor continued acting as a teacher throughout these preparations. Rather than hoarding everything he had learned, he helped ancient beings such as Kali and [[Dún Scáith|Dun Scaith]] confront gaps in knowledge they had never previously needed to address. His lessons ranged from conceptual understanding to Runes, creating the unusual situation in which beings vastly older than Victor were now becoming his students because the speed and breadth of his development had carried him into fields they themselves had never mastered.[1180][1181]
The younger Elderblood generation was also maturing socially. [[Nero Elderblood]] and [[Ophis Tepes Elderblood]], once among the children being protected and trained, increasingly acted as elder sisters toward the enormous number of younger girls around them. The family was beginning to develop its own internal generations and hierarchy through experience rather than simply through the identity of each child's mother.[1182]
Victor then encountered The Owner of Limbo, the Primordial of Balance. Their conversation expanded his understanding of the condition of the Universe and the purpose served by Balance. A naturally balanced Cosmos was not supposed to resemble the unstable system Victor had inherited; its Timeline and cosmic processes should proceed according to an ordered cycle until the eventual End. The incomplete state of [[Primordial Chaos]] had left the existing Creation abnormal, while Victor's own rapid development introduced another variable capable of disrupting whatever equilibrium remained.[1183]
Victor did not simply trust the Primordial because the being spoke calmly or possessed knowledge he wanted. Balance's vague answers and apparent expectations regarding Victor made the Emperor suspect that he was being maneuvered toward someone else's objective. If greater cosmic powers were beginning to observe him, entering unknown territory with his genuine body would expose far too much. An enemy capable of tracing Souls or metaphysical connections might discover his family, his [[World Trees]], his Eldritch nature or the deeper structures tied to his existence.[1183][1184]
Victor therefore created a scout specifically designed to contain almost none of those vulnerabilities. The clone was pure Energy in the shape of a younger Victor. It received a greatsword and a lesser copy of the Emperor's armor, with a cape of pure miasma. It did not carry his Eldritch factor, his tie to the World Trees, or [[Junketsu]]. Its memories of wives and daughters were an empty shell. He did not steer it. He only watched through its eyes, and the link was thin enough to cut. The personality was the reckless Victor of earlier years, mixed with the theatrical violence associated with [[Adonis Snow]], so that a capture would teach an enemy about a fighter and not about the family.[1184]
The clone entered foreign territory and soon encountered the Empire of Light. The soldiers were not a race. They were unfinished Gods made of Energy, formless until they needed a body. Commander [[Vik-Ir-loah]] met him. The clone ate heads and Souls for the information in them, coated his sword in violet Energy, and threw their own Light beams back. A martial cut from the greatsword dropped more than five thousand in one swing. Their answer was not a stronger warrior. Pillars that mixed technology and Divinity sealed the space, slowed even Lightning and Reality-bending, and regrew as fast as he broke them. Light healed the commander's flesh and his armor. Ships whose engines were Light closed the perimeter. The restricted copy still won the local exchange. The real Emperor and his wives watched from safety, and what they watched was a civilization that already had counters for speed, Space and Reality.[1185]
The encounter rapidly proved why the wider Universe could not be underestimated. The Empire of Light possessed Divine technology capable of analyzing abilities, deploying enormous numbers of troops, creating suppression fields and developing countermeasures while battle was still occurring. Victor's clone remained superior to ordinary forces because his Grandmaster martial knowledge, Soul abilities and capacity to adapt were things technology could not immediately reproduce, but the enemy continuously escalated the quality of the resources sent against him. The Elderblood observers recognized the uncomfortable implication: most ordinary soldiers, Gods and supernatural races from their own civilization would be annihilated if thrown carelessly into a war against powers operating at this level.[1185][1186]
The clone nevertheless continued learning faster than the enemy expected. He corrupted one of their commanders through the interaction of Darkness, Abyssal Miasma and Soul manipulation, bypassed attempted anti-cloning countermeasures and infiltrated the Light infrastructure of the Solar System. There he discovered a massive source of pure Positive Energy functioning as the heart of the local network. More disturbing than the Energy itself was the method by which the Empire used it: prolonged exposure and integration gradually stripped beings of meaningful free will until they effectively became extensions of the Light and its Emperor.[1187]
The discovery disgusted Victor despite his own controlling personality. His Empire demanded loyalty and imposed his authority absolutely when necessary, but he still wanted his people to possess identities, desires and the ability to think. The Empire of Light instead converted populations into obedient tools whose thoughts and basic actions could be dictated by the system controlling them.[1187]
Before destroying the local power source, the clone copied the information available within the enemy installation and transmitted the captured data back to the real Victor. Velnorah isolated the information inside a separate space rather than recklessly connecting potentially hostile technology to the Imperial network. The mission had therefore already succeeded: Victor now possessed technological, military and ideological intelligence concerning one of the advanced civilizations beyond his familiar domain.[1187]
Once the local system was disabled, the clone stopped prolonging the battle. Using the difference between a genuine Grandmaster and opponents who had relied heavily upon external systems, he annihilated the remaining forces and killed the warrior identified as [[Solus 969|Number 969]]. Only afterward did he learn why the dying opponent remained confident. Far outside the Solar System waited an artificial structure larger than the system itself, equipped with weapons whose firepower made the previous battle appear almost insignificant.[1187]
The distant fortress opened fire. The attack did not merely target Victor's clone or the planet on which the conflict had begun—it erased the entire Solar System. The clone laughed at the absurd scale of the weapon even as his body and everything surrounding him were vaporized. Defending against such an attack was beyond the deliberately restricted clone, but survival had never been the purpose of his creation. The real Victor remained untouched, his family remained hidden and the Empire had obtained exactly what the reconnaissance mission was designed to acquire: knowledge of what awaited them outside their comparatively protected territory.[1187]
Volume 8 consequently ended on a fundamental change in scale. Victor had begun the volume returning home to a new generation of daughters and spent much of it transforming his household, religion and territories into a genuine interstellar civilization. By its conclusion he had unified [[Yggdrasil]], become Overlord of his Sector, developed the [[Dragon Heart]] and Akasha, expanded the Empire beyond its original worlds, discovered a deeper foundation of Energy and created forces capable of fighting on multiple planets without his personal intervention. Yet the destruction of an entire Solar System as collateral damage demonstrated how small those achievements could appear beside the civilizations occupying the greater cosmic stage. The [[Elderblood Empire]] was no longer preparing merely to dominate its home Sector. It was preparing to meet powers whose rulers and technologies operated on a scale where star systems could be sacrificed as weapons—and the Emperor of Light was only the first such power Victor had encountered.[1187]

#### Volume 9: Those Who Rule Reality
Chapters 1135–1207

##### Those Who Rule Reality and the Coming War
Chapters 1135–1138
Following the destruction of the younger clone he had sent beyond his familiar territories, Victor Elderblood received his first undeniable proof of how far civilizations existing in the higher regions of the greater Cosmos stood above the old Pantheons of Earth. The Empire of Light had not merely defeated the clone; its military infrastructure possessed enough firepower to erase the entire Solar System in which the confrontation occurred. Victor had deliberately severed the clone from the deeper metaphysical connections leading back to his original body and family, ensuring that destroying it would not give the enemy a path toward the [[Elderblood Empire]]. The mission therefore remained a strategic success despite the clone's death: Victor obtained direct military and ideological information from an Upper-Sector civilization while exposing almost nothing of his true position.[1188] More importantly, he learned that the Being known as <Light> was not unique. Other rulers or supreme figures associated with powers such as <Darkness>, <Emperor> and <Law> existed within the larger cosmic hierarchy, and Victor immediately rejected the assumption that permanent peace between himself and such Beings could be guaranteed. He would never willingly subordinate himself to another ruler, while sufficiently perceptive powers would eventually recognize the rapidly developing Dragon Emperor either as something to control, something to exploit or a threat that had to disappear. The confrontation with Light therefore transformed the Upper Sectors from an unknown frontier into an inevitable future battlefield.[1188]
Rather than immediately tearing through the barrier separating his Sector from the higher regions, Victor chose to consolidate everything behind him first. His Cosmic Consciousness spread through the Mid-Level Sector until it reached the enclosing barrier, while the unrestricted scale of his body had grown beyond ordinary galaxies. His existence had become so metaphysically "heavy" compared with the surrounding Reality that Victor believed he could force the Sector itself to expand merely by fully imposing himself upon it.[1189] Instead of wasting power increasing the region's size simply for his own comfort, Victor contacted the [[World Trees]] spread throughout the Sector. Millions responded. Their locations, combined with his own perception, allowed him to construct a strategic map of the galaxies and systems belonging to the region, which he transferred to [[Akasha Elderblood]] for future administration, military logistics, colonization and infrastructure planning. The World Trees became natural anchors for an enormous network connecting Imperial worlds, while planets were increasingly classified according to specific purposes such as population, agriculture, mining, automated industry, research or military use. Victor could personally replace the functions of a World Tree when necessary by supplying enough Energy and Life-related influence to sustain additional worlds, but he preferred creating systems capable of functioning without his constant supervision.[1189]
The Empire's understanding of astronomical engineering expanded alongside its territory. Stars, black holes and other large-scale celestial structures were no longer automatically regarded as immutable features of nature; Victor and his researchers could contemplate relocating them, reinforcing Galactic structures and eventually constructing artificial equivalents as components of Imperial architecture. The allied Hindu and Biblical Pantheons were permitted access to Elderblood resources so that they could develop alongside the Empire. Victor genuinely wanted his allies stronger before the coming war, but he also understood the political consequence: the more their civilizations relied upon Elderblood infrastructure, knowledge and resources, the more difficult it would become for them to betray him later. He could have annexed the remaining Pantheons outright, but saw little value in accepting direct responsibility for populations that could instead remain useful allies beneath the larger Imperial sphere.[1189]
With the foundations prepared, Victor initiated the most extreme developmental undertaking in Imperial history. Standing beside a massive black hole and casually exercising control over the surrounding galaxy, he reflected upon the distance between the sick Human he had once been and the Being now capable of treating astronomical structures as objects beneath his authority.[1190] Victor then ordered a temporal ritual intended to grant the Empire approximately 200,000 years of internal development while roughly one external year passed. Natalia, as the Dragon Goddess of Time, controlled the temporal component, while Victor became the principal Energy source and stabilizing anchor. [[Jeanne Elderblood]] and the other Empresses supported the structure, and Victor deliberately prevented his daughters from shouldering the main burden, deciding that the older generation would sustain the dangerous process while the second generation used the centuries and millennia it created to grow. The military would simultaneously be reorganized into specialized Legions and the allied Pantheons integrated into the command structure intended for the future Upper-Sector war.[1190]
Victor's objective had already grown beyond merely defeating Light. He increasingly viewed the vacant supreme position over their Reality as an unresolved structural problem. <Positivity> and <Negativity> represented divided foundations from which complete [[Chaos]] could theoretically emerge, while the supreme cosmic position once associated with that greater whole remained unoccupied. Victor had no intention of surviving beneath another Being who eventually claimed it. His preparations were therefore aimed not only at defending his Empire but at the much larger struggle implied by the Throne of the Universe. Before activating the ritual fully, Victor addressed his people and acknowledged that his path would drag them into wars of a scale most had never imagined. He nevertheless promised that those who followed him would not simply disappear if they died; so long as their Souls remained recoverable, Victor intended to preserve them and give them another opportunity through the afterlife and reincarnation systems being built beneath his authority. Because Victor's Soul and words had acquired genuine metaphysical power, this promise carried far more weight than ordinary political rhetoric.[1190]
The ritual succeeded, but its cost immediately exceeded Victor's original expectations. Accelerating a Galactic civilization did not simply mean accelerating conscious thought: planets continued rotating, stars continued evolving, ecosystems developed, populations reproduced, industries consumed resources and every supernatural and physical process inside the affected region had to remain synchronized beneath the altered flow of Time. After only approximately seven weeks, Victor experienced something that would once have seemed nearly impossible—signs that he could theoretically become tired.[1191] The World Tree network, his [[Dragon Heart]], his Eldritch existence and the Energy supplied by his family kept the process stable, but efficiency became increasingly important. Jeanne gradually assumed a larger share of the energetic burden, Natalia maintained the temporal structure and Victor's wives rotated between supporting the ritual and descending through avatars to supervise Imperial civilization personally.
The accelerated era also created an immediate problem surrounding death. Hundreds of billions and eventually far greater populations could not simply enter afterlife systems originally designed for much smaller civilizations. [[Hela Elderblood]] and the other women associated with death, Souls and afterlives began restructuring the entire Imperial process: Hell remained available for sinners, Demons and Souls suited to it, while additional regions were created for Soul evaluation, worthy dead, temporary rest and reincarnation. Creating dimensions for these purposes was comparatively simple; properly controlling the flow and ownership of Souls was considerably harder, causing Victor to take responsibility for the deepest parts of the system because his Authority over Souls exceeded that of the surrounding Gods.[1191] At the same time, [[Aphrodite]] and the Goddesses connected to Life, Fertility, Motherhood, Marriage and similar Concepts increased birth rates and general health throughout Imperial territory, beginning the enormous demographic expansion necessary for a civilization expected eventually to populate galaxies.

##### Two Hundred Thousand Years of Imperial Development
Chapters 1139–1144
The first tens of thousands of accelerated years transformed the [[Elderblood Empire]] from an interstellar civilization still recognizably descended from Earth and [[Nightingale]] into something fundamentally different. Victor and his Empresses did not merely activate the ritual and wait outside; avatars of the ruling family appeared repeatedly during major historical milestones, including the first warrior to pass the 500th floor of Babylon's Tower of Challenges and the enormous demographic expansion produced through Divine fertility blessings.[1192] Imperial medicine, genetics, Velnorah's biotechnology and Divine intervention removed many of the bloodline problems that had once made supernatural hybridization dangerous. Humans, Vampires, [[Werewolves]], Spirits and numerous compatible races increasingly produced healthy descendants, and stable hybrid populations became ordinary components of Imperial society. Transportation changed just as dramatically. Teleportation networks and Space-Time technology connected inhabited worlds rapidly enough that astronomical distance increasingly became a logistical inconvenience rather than the defining barrier it had been during the Old World era.
The military was reorganized into a complete system of specialized Legions rather than forcing every institution to perform the same role. The Third Legion, [[The Black Hand of the Emperor]], commanded by [[Kaguya Elderblood Blank]] with Nyx Elderblood capable of acting in her place, became responsible for intelligence, infiltration, espionage, counterintelligence and psychological warfare. The Fourth Legion, [[Stellar Arsenal]], gathered the Empire's most dangerous scientific, magical and technological research beneath figures such as [[Ruby Elderblood Scarlett]], [[Velnorah Xyphora Elderblood Thaloria II]] and [[Aline Elderblood Valefar]], with its mandate explicitly extending toward weapons capable of remaining relevant against Solar-System-scale and greater enemies. [[The Imperial Guard]] became the Fifth Legion, commanded primarily by [[Nero Elderblood]] and [[Ophis Tepes Elderblood]] with [[Rose Adrasteia Elderblood]] able to substitute, while the Sixth Legion, [[The Silent Judgment]], under Jeanne and with Leona capable of assuming command, operated as the visible hand of Imperial law against major rebellion, corruption and internal threats.[1192] By Imperial Year 1,000 the structure had expanded further: the First Legion, the Spartans, became the Empire's principal offensive spearhead, while the Second Legion, [[Order of the Iron Veil]], was organized around planetary defense, fortifications and territorial protection. A deliberately concealed Seventh Legion, the [[Children of the Abyss]], completed the seven-Legion framework as a force reserved for threats of a more abnormal or existential nature.[1193]
Death itself became integrated into Imperial administration.
