##### Fun Calculation: How Long Has Victor Spent in Bed?
Conservative quantified total: approximately 6,000+ subjective years. This uses only intervals whose intimate duration is directly quantified or sufficiently explicit: roughly one year during the post-Hell harem reunion (Chs. 693–696 / 730), more than five months in Chapter 889, approximately 2,000 years across the Ariel/Nyx/full-harem block in Chapter 1102, 2,000 years with Violet and Jeanne in Chapter 1105, almost 2,000 years with Hela by Chapter 1124, and four months with Violet in Chapter 1156. Because Hela's period is described as "almost" 2,000 years, this should be treated as a rounded minimum rather than an exact stopwatch total.[40][41][47][57][58][60][20]
Broader estimate: approximately 7,000+ subjective years. Chapter 1162 adds an intended extension of roughly 1,000 years once [[Scathach]] joins Anna, Pepper, Ruby, Siena and Lacus. The narration cuts away before giving an exact completed duration, so this millennium belongs in the broader estimate rather than the conservative minimum.[28]
The real total is unquestionably higher. Neither figure attempts to add the countless unquantified encounters occurring between battles, training and government work; the various dedicated R-18 chapters with no stated duration; the first-intimacy events only confirmed retrospectively; or every sexual encounter during the approximately 2,000-year family-development period surrounding Chapter 986. Chapter 986 clearly establishes repeated bedroom activity, pregnancies and family growth, but counting that entire interval as sex would be inaccurate because Victor and the family were simultaneously training, ruling, researching, raising children and developing the Empire.[53]
Reading the classificationsDedicated R-18 means the chapter deliberately centers an intimate encounter. Direct / Non-Dedicated means intercourse or consummation is canon but is not the chapter's primary extended focus. Fetish Disclosure means a chapter discusses previous bedroom behavior or fantasies without necessarily containing a new sexual encounter. Retrospective means a later chapter explicitly confirms an off-screen event. Time Skip / Time Sphere means the novel gives a subjective duration while skipping most of the repeated sexual activity.

#### Notes
- Despite commonly being described as Victor's harem, the women themselves increasingly function as a single enormous family. By the later story, Victor explicitly prohibits political factions from forming among his wives. Smaller friendships and social circles naturally exist, but they are not permitted to become competing courts struggling for influence over the Emperor.[63]
- [[Violet Elderblood Snow]] is Victor's First Wife and eventually becomes the Dragon Empress. She therefore possesses a unique coordinating position within the household, but the numerical order used by this page is not the family's formal hierarchy and does not measure Victor's affection for any wife.
- The principal registry currently contains 58 confirmed wives. The four daughter-wife entries associated with the Extra chapters are deliberately separated from that figure because they belong to later/future continuity rather than the same chronological point as the main registry.
- There is no single universal form of marriage within Victor's family. His earliest wives were connected to him through the Vampire marriage system, while later relationships include [[Soul Marriage]], direct family acceptance, Divine relationships, Draconic transformations and bonds that are only explicitly described as marriages after significant periods have already passed. A conventional wedding ceremony is therefore not required for a character to be canonically recognized as Victor's wife.
- Soul Marriage represents a substantially deeper bond than an ordinary political or legal marriage. It connects the participants at the level of their Souls and becomes increasingly important as Victor and many of his wives ascend into Divine, Draconic and Conceptual states.
- Victor's family does not experience time in the same way as ordinary Humans. Space-Time abilities and accelerated dimensions allow Victor and his wives to spend months, centuries or even millennia together while comparatively little time passes elsewhere. Consequently, the chronological distance between two chapters can dramatically understate how long a relationship has developed from the characters' perspective.
- The later size of the harem is closely connected to Victor's increasingly non-Human lifespan. Once Victor and his wives become beings capable of living indefinitely and manipulating time, relationships can develop over thousands of subjective years without the limitations that would exist in a Human lifetime.
- Victor does not normally treat marriage as a purely political transaction. Political advantages frequently accompany his relationships, but women who enter the family are expected to become part of the household itself rather than remaining distant consorts. This principle becomes increasingly important as the Elderblood household develops from a collection of lovers and allied families into an Imperial dynasty.
- Victor's family structure is unusually stable for a harem of its size because its members are united by direct personal attachment to Victor and increasingly strong familial attachment to one another. Rivalry, jealousy and possessiveness remain common personality traits, but serious internal disputes are treated as family problems rather than struggles for succession or political control.
- Victor continues making individual time for his wives even after becoming the ruler of an enormous Empire. The later narrative repeatedly emphasizes that his ability to manipulate time allows him to avoid treating newer wives as disposable political additions; courtship can take years from the woman's perspective even when Victor could theoretically accelerate the process immediately. [[Tyche]] is a particularly clear example, as Victor deliberately allows their relationship to develop naturally rather than immediately consummating the marriage.[64]
- Victor's own underlying philosophy toward his wives is summarized by one of the aspects of his subconscious in Chapter 996: family comes first, and the same mixture of support, protection and possessiveness that he had already shown toward his wives becomes the model he later applies to his children.[65]
- The harem also plays an increasingly important role in governing the Empire. Victor does not personally micromanage every institution; many of his wives independently command military forces, intelligence networks, scientific divisions, religious institutions, territories or other portions of the Imperial administration. Their status as wives therefore develops alongside substantial political and military authority.
- [[Yggdrasil]], [[Qliphoth]], Aurora, Aria, [[Diana]], Diane and many other [[World Trees]] possess lover-like or spouse-like Soul bonds with Victor, but they are kept outside the ordinary wife count because the story does not consistently apply the same marital terminology to every World Tree bonded to his Soul.[1][2]
- Likewise, being openly attracted to Victor does not make a woman a wife. The article therefore distinguishes confirmed wives from women who love him, desire him, are being courted, have been proposed as possible additions or simply possess unresolved romantic potential. [[Yuki Snow]] and Evie Moriarty are notable late-story examples of this distinction.
- [[Hilda Snow Elderblood]] is explicitly recognized as one of Victor's wives by Chapter 1096 despite earlier ambiguity surrounding her position. Tyche remains a prospective wife through Chapter 1170, enters a physical relationship with Victor in Chapter 1171 and is later unambiguously part of the family as both his wife and the mother of [[Moira Eutychia Elderblood]]. These later confirmations supersede provisional descriptions made before those relationships were completed.
- Not every wife's first sexual encounter receives an R-18 chapter. Some encounters are depicted directly, others fade to black, and many are only revealed afterward through conversation, pregnancy, marriage status or references to events occurring during a time skip. The First Intimacy field therefore records the earliest identifiable consummation or confirmation rather than promising an explicit scene.
- The post-Hell reunion provides the clearest early example of this compressed chronology. After approximately seven hundred years separated from most of his family, Victor spends roughly one subjective year reconnecting with his then-current wives, allowing numerous relationships that had previously remained unresolved to progress during the same period.[40][41][42]
- Later Space-Time periods make this effect considerably more extreme. Victor spends approximately two thousand years across the Ariel/Nyx/full-harem period, another two thousand years with Violet and Jeanne, and almost two thousand years with Hela. The exact amount of Victor's life spent specifically in sexual activity cannot be calculated because most ordinary encounters are never given durations, but the directly quantified periods alone amount to more than six thousand subjective years.[57][58][60]
- Sexual preferences within the harem differ substantially between wives rather than representing one universal dynamic. Some wives strongly prefer private one-on-one intimacy, others enjoy group encounters, role-play, BDSM, domination contests, punishment, bondage or other specific practices. The Intimacy & Preferences Index records only preferences directly described or demonstrated by the novel and distinguishes a confirmed practiced act from a recurring fetish whenever the evidence allows.
- Motherhood substantially changes the later social dynamic of the harem. By the late Imperial era, the wives are not merely Victor's partners but mothers within an enormous shared dynasty whose daughters commonly refer to Victor's other wives as their mothers as well. This produces a family structure far broader than conventional biological parentage.
- The Elderblood household ultimately grows beyond the original meaning of a conventional harem. After thousands of subjective years, its wives, children, Soul-bonded partners and associated branches operate as the core of an Imperial family whose relationships overlap with the government, military, scientific institutions and supernatural structure of Victor's civilization.

Victor Elderblood's Martial Arts documents Victor Elderblood's development specifically as a martial artist: the foundations taught to him by [[Scathach Elderblood Scarlett]], his progression through recognized martial ranks, his study of numerous weapon and unarmed systems, the development of an adaptive method capable of accommodating radically different forms of combat, his eventual creation of original martial arts and his attainment of Grandmastery through the Greatsword. The subject is separate from Victor's general increase in supernatural power. His raw strength, racial evolutions and supernatural abilities are documented respectively on Victor Elderblood/Progress, Victor Elderblood/Growth and Victor Elderblood/Abilities; they are relevant here only where they directly change the body, principles or technical systems through which Victor practices martial arts.
Victor began his supernatural life with exceptional instincts and physical potential but virtually no serious formal combat education. [[Scathach]] rebuilt him from that point upward, first correcting his fundamental movement and weapon handling and then giving him a sufficiently broad martial framework that completely foreign fighting systems could later be understood through the same underlying principles.[1][2][3][4] Victor eventually carried that foundation far beyond its original purpose. He studied techniques belonging to Humans and supernatural races, learned to extract useful principles without being constrained by the body for which a technique had originally been designed, became capable of teaching Scathach's own principles, created techniques and foundational systems of his own, formalized the [[Seven Arts of the Blood Dragon Primogenitor]] and finally returned to the Greatsword—the first weapon he had consciously chosen—to obtain the Enlightenment required for Grandmastery.[5][6][7][8][9]

#### Martial Mastery Progression
Main article: Martial Art Mastery
Martial proficiency runs from Apprentice to Grandmaster. In that range, only Master and Grandmaster are the ranks that matter. Few beings reach Master. Fewer reach Grandmaster, and Gods do not reach it easily. Victor knows two Grandmasters, [[Scathach Elderblood Scarlett]] and [[Rose Adrasteia Elderblood]], and the beings in that rank can be counted on both hands.[17]
The ranks named in his training are Apprentice, Expert, Master and Grandmaster. Expert sits one step under Master. Haruna, a Master of Katana Arts, reads his Expert Greatsword and Odachi as one level below her own rank. Grandmaster is not another year of Mastery. It requires a personal Enlightenment. [[Vlad III Tepes|Vlad Tepes]] is a Master, and he never felt that Enlightenment no matter how long he trained. The distance between the two ranks is heaven and earth. [[Scathach]] is a Master of pretty much every martial art and a Grandmaster of the spear. Rose gave her life to the sword, so her level in that one art may stand higher than Scathach's. Grandmaster arts begin to put a Concept on the weapon. [[Aphrodite]] is the one who says so. Rose's blade cannot be seen. Describing Enlightenment would damage the listener. The feeling is different for each being, and hunting for someone else's feeling sends the training the wrong way.[12][18][17]
He is not walked through every lower grade. The table keeps the ranks he states separate from the stretches of training that describe his path.

#### I. The Beginning — Scathach's Student
Victor's serious martial development began when [[Scathach Elderblood Scarlett]] took responsibility for his training. Before that point, Vampirism had given him an enormous physical advantage over ordinary Humans and many weaker supernatural opponents, but it had not given him the fundamentals expected of a genuine martial artist. [[Scathach]] deliberately refused to let his regeneration, strength or inherited abilities disguise those deficiencies. Her earliest instruction was severe even by supernatural standards: Victor was repeatedly wounded, impaled and pushed through levels of pain that would have incapacitated an ordinary fighter so that he would learn to remain aware of the battlefield while injured rather than mentally collapsing the moment his body was damaged.[1]
Once his ability to function under injury had been established, Scathach began correcting the actual mechanics of his combat. Movement that wasted distance, excessive force, poor posture, predictable attacks, inefficient Energy use, weak defensive habits and uncontrolled weapon handling were treated as flaws regardless of whether Victor's raw power was great enough to overwhelm the immediate opponent. This produced the principle that remained underneath nearly every later stage of his martial development: supernatural power is something technique should control and enhance, not something that should replace technique whenever the user is strong enough to ignore their mistakes.[2]
I
Power should enhance technique.Power should not replace technique.

##### Choosing the Greatsword
When formal weapon training began, Victor showed particular interest in the [[Spears|Spear]] and Greatsword, but ultimately selected the Greatsword, a weapon he had admired since childhood.[2] At the time, this was simply the first major weapon around which [[Scathach]] would build his training; neither Victor nor anyone around him yet knew that the choice would eventually define the deepest part of his martial identity. Victor later became skilled with many weapons, and the Odachi in particular developed into one of his major alternatives through [[Junketsu]], but the Greatsword remained tied to the beginning of his disciplined martial life. Millennia of accumulated experience did not erase that connection. When Victor finally required the personal Enlightenment necessary to become a Grandmaster, it was the Greatsword—not his Odachi, fists, supernatural powers or even the Seven Arts—that provided the path forward.[9]
↑ Return to Martial Archive

#### II. Building the Foundation
Main article: [[Scathach’s Foundational Martial Art]]
[[Scathach]]'s system was not built around memorizing a single sequence of attacks. Its purpose was to teach the components from which a complete fighter could construct movement. Her daughters had originally been trained through different specializations—Pepper in Strength, Siena in Power, Lacus in Speed and Ruby in Defense—while the fifth component, Control, represented the point at which the previous principles could be combined and applied efficiently as one martial system.[3][4][20] Victor's unusual development allowed him to learn the fundamentals of all of them within roughly six months, although his tendency to use excessive force continued to demonstrate that understanding a principle and perfectly applying it in every situation were not yet the same thing.[3][4]
Principle
Martial Function
Strength
Efficient generation, transfer and employment of physical force rather than simply striking with everything the body can produce.
Power
Incorporation and regulation of supernatural abilities so that the user's powers become part of their martial movement instead of independent attacks attached afterward.
Speed
Footwork, acceleration, breathing and the removal of movement that delays the practitioner without contributing to the intended action.
Defense
Defensive positioning and the use of physical or supernatural characteristics to avoid, redirect, endure or neutralize attacks while preserving the practitioner's ability to counter.
Control
The integration and regulation of the previous principles, allowing strength, speed, defense and supernatural power to be used with the amount and timing appropriate to the situation.
The long-term importance of this system was greater than the five techniques themselves. It gave Victor a common martial language. When he later encountered a Werewolf technique, a Tengu art, an unfamiliar weapon or the fighting habits of another supernatural race, he did not need to abandon everything he already knew and begin as an unrelated practitioner. He could examine how the foreign system generated force, moved its body, controlled distance or employed its unique physiology and compare those mechanics with the foundation already established by Scathach.

##### From Student to Teacher
Victor's instruction of Pepper in Chapters 421–422 demonstrates how far this understanding had matured. He recognized that [[Scathach]] had not given each daughter an isolated style merely because their talents differed; their specializations were also pieces of a larger training method intended eventually to lead back toward Control. Victor could therefore explain the relationship among their techniques, identify Pepper's immediate deficiencies and reproduce principles Scathach had originally taught to other daughters, including the footwork associated with Lacus and defensive applications associated with Ruby.[6][20] This is one of the earliest clear points where Victor stops behaving only as a talented student. Teaching forced him to articulate why movements worked, diagnose what another practitioner lacked and adapt the lesson to that person rather than merely reproducing what Scathach had once done to him.
Student→Practitioner→Teacher of the Principle
↑ Return to Martial Archive

#### III. The Search for a Universal Fighting Style
He did not want a warrior who died the moment the preferred weapon was gone. He wanted to be a master at everything. [[Scathach]] understood that goal when she watched him change weapons in the middle of the fight with the Alpha Werewolf. Said simply, that is becoming a [[Ares|God of War]], because only the God of War had dominion over all weapons. She did not have that complete mastery. She still preferred the spear. What he was looking for went past what she had looked for. She thought it absurd, and she liked it.[13] Away from [[Nightingale]] he pushed the same aim further. Through Esther he took martial material from Humans and from species whose bodies were not his: Werewolf fist arts, Tengu Naginata arts, Banshee systems, and books on spears, axes, Western swords, katanas and whips, together with a large quantity of Human martial knowledge. What the books gave him was the basics. The unusual part was what he tried to do with those basics.[5]
Victor refused to treat foreign physiology as an absolute barrier. If a Tengu technique relied upon wings, he considered whether Blood could produce wings capable of reproducing the relevant mechanic; if a Werewolf system relied upon exceptional physical power, Victor compared that requirement with his own strength rather than simply dismissing the technique because he was not a Werewolf. This mentality did not mean every racial technique could be copied literally. Instead, Victor increasingly searched for the principle beneath the original movement: what mechanical or supernatural condition made the technique function, whether he possessed an equivalent method of creating that condition and how it could be reconstructed without damaging the foundation he already possessed.[5]

##### The Failed Fusion
Victor initially attempted the most direct solution—merging [[Scathach]]'s martial art with the many systems he had studied. The attempt failed. Complete martial arts contain their own assumptions regarding stance, balance, rhythm, muscle memory, weapon dimensions and the physiology of the original practitioner; mechanically stacking them together produced contradictions rather than a superior style. Victor's actual breakthrough was therefore not fusion but adaptation. Scathach's art remained the stable foundation, while the useful fundamentals of other systems were translated into a form compatible with it. This allowed Victor to move between weapons without suffering the dramatic loss of efficiency expected when a specialist abandons the discipline around which their instincts were built.[5]
One Foundation↓Many Compatible Principles↓One Adaptive Martial Artist
This distinction is essential to understanding Victor's later versatility. He is not best described as carrying dozens of completely separate schools and consciously selecting one from an internal catalogue. His development increasingly turns those schools into sources of principles that can be expressed through a single evolving martial foundation.
↑ Return to Martial Archive

#### IV. The Adaptive Martial Artist
Fighting him felt like fighting several people through one body. The mannerisms of many fighters were there, and none of them got in the way of the style.[14] The aim was already named. To be a master at everything is to become a [[Ares|God of War]], because only the God of War had dominion over all weapons.[13] If he keeps training and never loses focus, he may come close to a God of War who knows all the martial arts in the world and can use every one of them perfectly, without the disadvantage that breadth usually costs. Ares took thousands of years to perfect the martial arts he had learned, and he wasted a great deal of that time. Victor does not. So long as the focus holds, it is possible.[14]
The process can be understood through four recurring steps. Victor first observes a movement or foreign system and separates its visible form from the mechanic that actually produces the result. He then understands what the technique requires—body structure, timing, force, Energy, positioning or another principle. That principle is translated through the foundation he already possesses and finally personalized until the movement is natural for Victor rather than a weaker imitation of its original user.
Stage
Process
Observe
Examine the opponent, teacher, weapon or foreign martial system closely enough to distinguish the important mechanic from superficial movement.
Understand
Determine why the technique works and what physical or supernatural conditions are actually required to reproduce its result.
Translate
Reconstruct the principle through Victor's own martial foundation, physiology, powers and available weapons instead of copying the original body mechanically.
Personalize
Refine the translated movement until it is natural to Victor and can be used without disrupting the rest of his fighting method.
This adaptability becomes increasingly important as Victor himself changes species. A movement learned as a young Vampire cannot always remain mechanically identical after his body acquires radically different mass, reach, strength, wings, supernatural senses and Reality-affecting properties. Victor therefore treats martial arts as living systems that must continue evolving with the practitioner rather than sacred choreography whose original form must be preserved regardless of what the user becomes.
↑ Return to Martial Archive

He names both the Greatsword and the Odachi as Expert Level, and he says he is not a Master yet.[12] There is no formal gap between the two weapons then. [[Junketsu]] made the Odachi convenient, and he accumulated tremendous practical experience with it. The Enlightenment comes through the Greatsword, the weapon of his first formal training under [[Scathach]].[9]

#### VI. Mastery
His confrontation with [[Adam William Lykos]] is the practical shape of a mature martial Master. At the start, his stance is mistaken for Bajiquan. He identifies it as [[Scathach]]'s style modified to suit his own needs.[10] He is no longer reproducing her art exactly as it was taught, and the foundation is still recognizable under the changes.
Once the fight accelerates, Tasha counts more than five martial styles in a very short period. He changes stance and range without the instincts of the previous system getting in the way. Capoeira is named when he drops low and attacks through dance-like kicks. He later takes a rear naked choke recognized as Jiu-Jitsu. At another point he adopts a stance that looks like Boxing. The art he then uses is not Boxing. It is another, deadlier system.[11] He can change the principles governing his movement without the change itself degrading the performance.
The fight ends with Alucard Original Style: Inner Destruction. Rather than depending upon a single enormous external impact, he lands several precisely concentrated attacks into the same location, combining internal-destruction principles with his knowledge of vulnerable points in a living body.[11] He calls himself a Close Combat Master, and the technique carries his own name. Enlightenment, the thing that separates that Mastery from Grandmastery, is still ahead of him.[18]
Master of Close Combat+Master-Level General Martial Artist+Expert or Greater in Multiple Weapons+Adaptive Multi-Style Foundation
↑ Return to Martial Archive

#### VII. Developing a Personal Martial Identity
The largest difference between Victor's early and later development is not simply an increase in skill. He gradually changes from someone who learns and adapts systems created by other people into someone capable of designing martial systems from first principles.

##### Inner Destruction
Alucard Original Style: Inner Destruction is one of the earliest techniques whose name openly marks that change.[11] Victor's attack against Adam combines several rapid precision impacts, knowledge of internal destruction and vulnerable points of the body into a technique constructed around Victor's own understanding. Its relevance to his martial history is therefore greater than the damage it inflicts. By formally calling the technique an Alucard Original Style, Victor is acknowledging that adaptation has advanced far enough to produce techniques whose identity is his rather than [[Scathach]]'s, a Human school's or another species'.

##### Dragon-Tailored Martial Foundation
Victor's later evolution into a Blood Dragon created the same problem on a much larger scale. The body through which he practiced martial arts no longer possessed the same assumptions as the Vampire body with which he began training. After [[Scathach]]'s own Dragon transformation, he gives her an unfinished martial framework designed specifically for Dragons using humanoid forms, because simply giving a Dragon Human or Vampire techniques without modification would ignore the nature of its new body.[7]
The system was not yet presented as a completed martial art. It was an idea and foundation intended to teach Dragons how to use the advantages of their physiology coherently rather than simply adding greater strength to old movements. Scathach could recognize Victor's previous martial influences within it, but those principles had already been restructured around a different kind of existence.[7] This represents one of Victor's clearest transitions from student to system designer: he had become capable of doing for another developing martial artist what Scathach had once done for him—constructing the foundation upon which that person's own technique could later grow.
Victor's progression eventually reached the point where he no longer merely learned foundations; he could create them.
↑ Return to Martial Archive

#### VIII. The Seven Arts — Victor as a Martial Art Creator
Main article: [[Seven Arts of the Blood Dragon Primogenitor]]
Victor's most complete original martial system is the Seven Arts of the Blood Dragon Primogenitor.[8][19] By this stage he possessed centuries of practical warfare, [[Scathach]]'s foundational teachings, Human and supernatural martial knowledge, experience with numerous weapons, the memories of consumed combatants and the fundamentally different physiology of a Blood Dragon. Rather than allowing those elements to remain an unstructured collection, Victor used his accumulated experience to create an advanced system built specifically around the characteristics available to his race. The Seven Arts integrate physical movement with increasingly sophisticated control over Energy, gravity, Reality and eventually the Soul, allowing the martial art to be expressed through the body or through weapons rather than existing as a single fixed weapon school.[8][19]
He was thinking past the person using the art. Scathach and the other Masters recognized that the system had prerequisites dangerous enough that reproducing the movements was not enough. The practitioner needed the foundation, and the Energy, Reality and Soul control. He realized his original first level was too advanced to be the entry, and he began a Level 0 to teach Dragons how to move their bodies and control Reality well enough for the later stages.[19] Inventing a powerful personal technique and building a system other people can be taught are not the same work. He had to set the order, the prerequisites, and the safety of practitioners who did not already have his instincts.
Earlier Victor
Seven Arts-Era Victor
Learns Scathach's system
Creates an independent progressive system built upon everything he has learned
Studies foreign martial arts
Determines which principles can coexist inside a coherent curriculum
Adapts techniques for himself
Creates preparatory stages so that other practitioners can acquire the prerequisites safely
Uses supernatural abilities alongside martial arts
Treats Energy, gravity, Reality and Soul control as mechanics integrated directly into martial progression
Corrects his own movement
Diagnoses flaws in the structure of his own martial art and redesigns that structure instead of defending it simply because he created it
The Seven Arts therefore represent the culmination of one part of Victor's development: the former student of Scathach had become capable of creating an extremely advanced martial system of his own. Ironically, the very complexity of that achievement also helped expose what he still lacked. Creating an art capable of combining so many advanced principles did not itself make Victor a Grandmaster. His next breakthrough required movement in the opposite direction—away from adding more systems and back toward the most basic foundation of his martial life.
↑ Return to Martial Archive

#### IX. The Barrier to Grandmastery
Grandmastery is not the next promotion after enough years as a Master. The difference is Enlightenment. Vlad never reached it, despite his age and his training, because that realization never came. A person can be a Master in all martial arts and still not be a Grandmaster, and the two ranks are as far apart as heaven and earth. [[Scathach]]'s breadth did not promote every art she knew. She is a Grandmaster of the spear. Rose is the other road: the sword, until the blade itself carries a Concept and cannot be seen.[18][17]
This distinction created a particular problem for Victor. By the time of the Seven Arts he possessed an extraordinary quantity of knowledge, tremendous combat experience, multiple weapon disciplines, a Master-level adaptive foundation and the ability to create martial arts sophisticated enough to challenge other elite practitioners. None of those achievements answered the actual question required for Grandmastery. More years could refine what he already possessed, but simply accumulating another weapon, another supernatural system or another thousand techniques would only increase the size of the structure. The missing element was an understanding of the martial path beneath that structure.
What remains when every borrowed technique, accumulated weapon and supernatural advantage is stripped away?
↑ Return to Martial Archive

#### X. Enlightenment — Return to the Beginning
The breakthrough comes in the training that follows the Seven Arts. The arts did not put him in the Grandmaster realm. He meets a barrier he cannot remove by increasing his power. His internal perception represented that limitation as an enormous damaged gate. Different manifestations of Victor's own existence arrived at essentially the same conclusion: the existence of a limitation was not a sufficient reason to accept it, but destroying the limitation still required understanding what was actually preventing his progress.[22][23][9]
The answer appeared when the different versions of Victor created Greatswords and assumed a posture he recognized immediately: the basic Greatsword stance [[Scathach]] had taught him at the beginning of his martial education.[9] Victor had spent centuries looking outward—learning new weapons, absorbing more combat experience, acquiring new bodies, developing supernatural systems and building increasingly complicated techniques. The realization was that none of those achievements invalidated the foundation supporting them. A structure could not continue rising indefinitely while its pillars remained less refined than everything placed above them. Victor therefore stopped searching for another advanced answer and returned to the origin he had assumed he had already surpassed.
Victor Before Enlightenment
Enlightenment

More knowledge was no longer sufficient to produce the required breakthrough
Possessed numerous fighting styles and weapon systems
Those systems required a clearly understood personal foundation beneath them
Created increasingly complicated martial techniques
Complexity could conceal imperfections that remained inside the most basic movement
Had mastered broad forms of combat
Mastery of many things was different from reaching the deepest understanding of one personal path
Constantly searched outward for the next improvement
Returned to the Greatsword and the first stance from which his formal martial life had begun
With that realization Victor broke through the barrier and entered the Grandmaster realm through Greatswordsmanship.[9]
GRANDMASTERGREATSWORD
The significance of the breakthrough is not that Victor abandoned everything he had learned. The Seven Arts, foreign systems, unarmed techniques and weapon knowledge all remained part of him. What changed was the hierarchy between them. Victor finally possessed a personal martial center strong enough that everything else could be measured, corrected and rebuilt around it rather than endlessly accumulating knowledge without perfecting the structure underneath.
↑ Return to Martial Archive

#### Grandmaster Greatswordsmanship
Grandmastery immediately changes the way Victor understands movement. Rather than receiving an entirely foreign set of techniques, he begins perceiving imperfections inside actions he had already performed for centuries. Stance, breathing, footwork, positioning, posture, weight transfer, alignment, timing and the relationship between one movement and the next are refined according to his current body.[9] The important distinction is that this process is no longer simple imitation. [[Scathach]] taught Victor techniques through the proportions, instincts and experience of Scathach; Grandmaster understanding allows Victor to identify where those inherited mechanics still contain assumptions belonging to his teacher and alter them until the movement is correct specifically for Victor Elderblood.
The same habit he had used on foreign arts is finally turned on the oldest part of his own foundation. The movements become so completely internalized that martial execution approaches instinct: instead of consciously remembering a stance and forcing the body into it, the body naturally expresses the refined action appropriate to the situation.[9]

##### Concept, Precision and Efficiency
The gap between Master and Grandmaster is heaven and earth. Grandmaster arts begin to apply a Concept through the weapon. That is why Rose's sword and [[Scathach]]'s spear do what ordinary technical mastery does not, and why Rose's blade cannot be seen.[18] His first act after the breakthrough is a Greatsword slash, not a Seven Arts combination. The cut opens a rupture through his Inner Cosmos and continues past that structure. He recognizes the result as swordsmanship. The strength of the technique is still the being who uses it. The rank lets his existence come out through a movement that is no longer wasting itself.[9]
VII
Grandmastery did not replace Victor's existing power.It removed imperfections that prevented that power from being expressed through completely refined martial movement.
Rose congratulates him on his first steps into the realm.[9] Entry is not the peak of the rank. Scathach's answer is that the level has been reached and now has to be taken to the top.
↑ Return to Martial Archive

#### XI. Martial Development After Grandmastery
Grandmaster is a threshold, not the end of the art. After Rose and [[Scathach]] became Dragons, both began to move again. A Grandmaster progresses further only after a higher state of existence. Rose's Noble Vampire body had been limiting the sword. Once she was a Dragon, the art advanced quickly.[15] Rose later stands on the threshold of surpassing Grandmaster and of an entirely new realm of martial arts, with Scathach in the same place. Rose is ahead, because she gave all of her time to the sword. For someone at that peak, a simple cut can become something that eviscerates mountains. The Dragon body is why. As a Noble Vampire, even after several centuries, her body had not been strong enough to become a weapon the way a Dragon's body can. Scathach's strongest technique evolves for the same reason.[24]

##### Higher-Level Techniques
Victor and [[Scathach]] keep working past the rank they can already see.[25][16] While they work with Attributeless Energy, he suggests calling the method a Grandmaster tier of energy control, on the model of martial arts. Scathach names it a Higher Level Technique, one level above their Grandmaster martial arts and above the martial art he created. He agrees.
He then divides that energy technique the way martial arts are divided. A Beginner is only learning the energy, and even that start requires almost perfect control of one's own powers. Proficient is the grade that can use attributeless energy to strengthen attacks, and it is reached only after the whole Beginner grade under a suitable master. Master, his own grade, requires a [[Primordial Chaos]], someone who creates an entire universe, or the use has consequences. Those three grades belong to the energy method. His highest named martial rank remains Grandmaster Greatswordsmanship.

#### Evolution of Victor's Martial Philosophy
Victor's martial philosophy changes repeatedly as his understanding grows, but each later stage retains lessons from the stages before it rather than replacing them completely.

##### Power, Discipline and Foundation
The earliest Victor naturally relied upon the physical advantages of Vampirism. [[Scathach]]'s training deliberately attacked that dependency by treating inefficient technique as a flaw even when Victor possessed enough strength to win anyway. The result was his first mature martial principle: power without control creates waste. Strength, speed, regeneration and supernatural abilities became more useful when supported by disciplined movement, and the five components of Scathach's foundational system gave Victor a language through which he could evaluate every later art.[2][3][4]

##### Breadth Without Fragmentation
He did not want mastery of one weapon to make every other weapon a liability. To be a master at everything is to become a [[Ares|God of War]], because only the God of War had dominion over all weapons, and even [[Scathach]] still preferred the spear.[13] Learning many complete schools still produced incompatible instincts. The failed fusion gave the workable answer: one foundation, and the useful principles of the other arts translated into it.[5] Fighting him then felt like fighting several martial artists in one body, and against Adam he could change close-combat methods without stopping to switch styles.[14][10][11] The art in use became subordinate to what the fight required.

##### From Practitioner to Creator
Mastery eventually made Victor responsible for more than his own movements. Teaching Pepper required him to understand [[Scathach]]'s system well enough to explain its internal design; creating a Dragon foundation required him to account for bodies fundamentally different from the ones for which he had originally trained; Inner Destruction demonstrated the creation of a personal technique; and the Seven Arts required him to construct an entire progression with prerequisites, stages and safety considerations.[6][20][11][7][19] Victor's martial questions therefore expanded from "How should I perform this?" to "Why does this work, who can perform it, what must they learn first and how should the system itself be structured?"

##### Grandmastery — Complexity Returns to Simplicity
Victor's Enlightenment completes this philosophical arc by revealing the weakness hidden inside endless accumulation. Complexity was not a mistake—the knowledge accumulated throughout his life remained invaluable—but advanced systems could not compensate indefinitely for imperfections in the foundation beneath them. The creator of the Seven Arts ultimately reached Grandmaster not by adding an eighth art, another weapon or another supernatural mechanism, but by returning to the first Greatsword stance he had learned and understanding it at a level his previous self could not.[9] Grandmastery consequently does not reject Victor's versatility. It gives that versatility a perfected center.
Power→Technique→Breadth→Adaptation→Mastery→Creation→Simplicity→Grandmastery
↑ Return to Martial Archive

He learns martial principles very quickly. Rapid learning and finished mastery are not the same thing. His early progress under [[Scathach]] was abnormal even by Vampire standards.[3][4]
Foundation
The breadth of Victor's later martial knowledge remains possible because Scathach first gave him a stable set of fundamentals against which unfamiliar movement can be compared.
Adaptability
Victor can study systems built for different races or weapons, isolate useful mechanics and reconstruct those mechanics through his own physiology rather than requiring literal biological equivalence.[5]

Changing weapons, ranges or fighting systems produces far less loss of efficiency than would normally be expected from a broadly trained martial artist.[5][11]
Combat Analysis
Victor studies opponents for principles rather than only weaknesses, turning actual combat into another source of technical information and refinement.
Personalization
Victor increasingly alters inherited movements according to his own proportions, powers and instincts. Grandmastery applies this process even to the foundational Greatsword movements he originally learned from Scathach.[10][9]
Precision
His development moves steadily away from solving every problem through maximum output and toward applying the amount of force, timing and placement actually required.
Efficiency
Control is a recurring theme from Scathach's fifth foundational principle through Victor's later martial creations and Grandmaster breakthrough. Removing wasted movement, Energy and unnecessary complexity remains central to his development.[4][9]
Teaching
Victor becomes capable of identifying weaknesses in other martial artists, reproducing principles they were never personally taught and constructing training frameworks around their needs.[6][20][7]

Develops original named techniques, an unfinished Dragon foundation and eventually a complete progressive martial system.[11][7][8][19]
Self-Correction
Victor does not treat his own creations as untouchable. The immediate creation of a Seven Arts Level 0 after recognizing that his intended entry stage was unreasonable is a direct example.[19]
Continuous Development
Grandmastery changes the quality of the training and does not end it. Rose and Scathach keep progressing after the rank, and a Higher Level Technique is classified above their Grandmaster martial arts.[15][16]

Major Weapons: Greatsword and Odachi, with broad secondary weapon knowledge.
Creator Status: Creator of original techniques, an unfinished Dragon-tailored foundational martial system and the [[Seven Arts of the Blood Dragon Primogenitor]].
Grandmaster Development: The breakthrough is his first steps into the realm. The rank continues after that.
Above-Grandmaster Development: Rose and [[Scathach]] reach the threshold of a further realm. A Higher Level Technique sits one level above their Grandmaster martial arts. No separate traditional rank above Grandmaster has been given to him.
Victor's current martial identity is therefore more accurately described as a Greatsword Grandmaster supported by an exceptionally broad Master-level martial foundation than as a character who has simply "mastered every martial art". His greatest martial advantage is not the possession of an encyclopedic list of styles by itself, but the method through which he understands and reorganizes them. Foreign techniques are reduced to their useful principles, those principles are tested against the common foundation established by Scathach and the result is rebuilt around Victor's current body, powers and instincts.
The progression creates a deliberate symmetry within Victor's martial life. Scathach originally took a newborn Vampire with tremendous power but little technical discipline and taught him how to stand, move, control his strength and properly wield a Greatsword. Victor eventually became capable of teaching those same principles, adapting them to other species, creating original techniques and designing complete martial systems. Yet the breakthrough that finally carried him beyond Mastery required him to recognize that none of those later achievements made the beginning obsolete. His first step into Grandmastery was ultimately a return to the weapon and fundamentals with which his true martial education had started.[9]
↑ Return to Martial Archive

#### Scope and Clarifications
- This page indexes Victor's martial development rather than his overall power progression. The destructive scale of an attack may illustrate what Victor can express through a technique, but increases in his raw strength, species, Divinity or cosmic power belong primarily on Victor Elderblood/Progress, Victor Elderblood/Growth and Victor Elderblood/Abilities.
- Becoming a Blood Dragon changed the body he fought with. Grandmastery was a separate Enlightenment, through the Greatsword.[9]
- Pepper, Siena, Lacus and Ruby were trained in Strength, Power, Speed and Defense. Control is the point at which those four are combined.[20]
- The foreign books gave him the basics. He adapted those basics through [[Scathach]]'s foundation and could change weapons without the usual loss of efficiency.[5]
- Only the [[Ares|God of War]] had dominion over all weapons. Victor wanted to be a master at everything, and Scathach reads that goal as becoming a God of War. She still preferred the spear. If he never loses focus, he may also come close to a being who knows all the martial arts in the world and can use them perfectly. Ares took thousands of years to perfect the martial arts he had learned.[13][14]
- The opening stance against Adam is mistaken for Bajiquan. He identifies it as Scathach's martial art, modified for his own needs.[10]
- Capoeira and Jiu-Jitsu appear in the fight with Adam. He also takes a stance that looks like Boxing. The art he then uses is not Boxing.[11]
- The Dragon foundation and the Seven Arts are separate. The first is an unfinished foundation for Dragons learning their new bodies. The second is his later progressive martial art.[7][8][19]
- Consumed memories add that being's combat experience. They do not, by themselves, turn every named art that being knew into a rank Victor holds.[8]
- The Enlightenment is Greatsword Grandmastery.[9]
- The first Grandmaster slash opens a rupture through his Inner Cosmos. He recognizes it as swordsmanship. The strength of the technique is the being who uses it.[9]
- A Grandmaster progresses further only after a higher state of existence. Rose and Scathach reach the threshold of a further realm once they are Dragons. That realm is not given another rank-name.[15][24]
- Higher Level Technique is the name of the attributeless-energy method, one level above their Grandmaster martial arts and above the art he created. Beginner, Proficient and Master, in that conversation, are grades of the energy method. His martial rank remains Grandmaster.[16]
↑ Return to Martial Archive

Victor's Sector is the Mid-Level Sector and principal cosmic Reality of Victor Elderblood and the [[Elderblood Empire]]. Its original core contained [[Yggdrasil]], the Milky Way and an enormous material cosmos enclosed by a metaphysical Sector barrier. Sectors are divisions of the greater Universe, but individual Sectors possess sufficiently complete cosmic structures that the story also contextually describes them as a Universe, Cosmos or Reality.[1][2][3]
The Sector is not limited to ordinary three-dimensional astronomical space. Its complete structure includes the material cosmos of galaxies, stars, Solar Systems and planets together with the [[Dimensional Void]], through which Pantheons, Divine Realms, Heavens, Hells and other supernatural dimensions are connected to the same broader Reality. Its [[World Trees]] provide a further biological and metaphysical network linking planets and higher-dimensional structures.
Victor's first full survey of the original Mid-Level Sector fixed its shape. He identified Earth in the Northern Region, three other developed sister-World-Tree civilizations toward the south, east and west, primitive life on other worlds and the metaphysical barriers enclosing the Reality.[4] Victor's Cosmic Consciousness extended throughout the entire Sector until reaching its outer boundary. Millions of World Tree connections responded to him, allowing Victor to construct a strategic map containing all galaxies belonging to the Sector.[5]
Even before the merger, the Sector already extended across countless galaxies. After establishing the World Tree Network through Mars, Victor directly perceived connected planets distributed throughout those countless galaxies, The gap between the farthest of those worlds is past any ordinary measure.[6]
The merger then changed the Sector's physical configuration. Nightingale, Samar and the Magic World were three Lower Sectors already deeply connected to Victor's Empire. By the late Imperial era, the Magic World had been conquered and developed by the Witches and is referred to in the merger sequence simply as Arcane or the Planet of the Witches. This later Arcane designation should not be confused with the original Arcane Realm from which the Witches initially opened the dimensional connection to the Magic World.[7][8][9]
Victor deliberately drew all three Lower Sectors toward his own. His outer barrier expanded as their Galactic contents appeared inside his sphere of influence, after which he personally reorganized the imported galaxies so they would neither collide with the mature Galactic structures of his Mid-Level Sector nor interfere with one another.[10][11]
The merger did not advance the Sector into a higher classification. Ruby explicitly explained that absorbing the smaller Realities did not cause the Mid-Level Sector itself to evolve; the process instead added additional Galactic territory within the enlarged Reality.[9] He rearranged individual galaxies and entire Galactic groups, including moving a spiral galaxy together with billions of stars while preserving its Solar Systems and stellar orbits. He subsequently placed Nightingale and Samar within a protected central Imperial region only a few hundred light-years apart, while the Witch-controlled Magic World—called Arcane during the operation—could be relocated more freely because its planet did not possess the same system-level peculiarities.[11]

#### Cosmological Structure

##### Sector and Greater Universe
Victor's Sector is one division within the greater Universe rather than the entirety of Creation. Sectors are territories distributed throughout the Universe and separated by invisible barriers according to their developmental levels. These protections prevent vastly more advanced civilizations from freely descending into weaker regions and overwhelming civilizations incapable of resisting them.[1]
At the same time, an individual Sector is a complete local cosmos. Universe, Cosmos and Reality are used for what someone can perceive inside one Sector. That usage does not erase the greater Universe made of many Sectors.
Velnorah and the Universal Tree supply the comparison that fixes the hierarchy. Lower Sectors are comparatively small protected cosmic environments; Mid-Level Sectors are considerably larger; and reaching the Higher Sectors is analogous to leaving a protected enclosure and entering an open ocean occupied by ancient and dangerous powers.[9][10]

##### Barrier-Limited Reality
The Sector barrier is a genuine cosmological boundary. Victor's first survey met protections separating his native Reality from neighboring Sector levels, A later expansion of his Cosmic Consciousness again ran until it naturally stopped at the Mid-Level Sector's outer barrier.[4][5]
A report of an "entire Universe" or an "entire cosmos" is the whole of the Reality that person can reach. It is not every Sector in the greater Universe, unless the boundary itself was crossed.
The boundary is not immutable. Victor pulled the three Lower Sectors into his sphere of influence and the barrier of his own Sector expanded enormously as entire galaxies appeared inside the enlarged Reality.[10] [[The Universal Tree]] specifically prevented unrelated neighboring Lower Sectors from being pulled into the merger, showing that the boundaries and relative placement of Sectors can be manipulated under exceptional circumstances.

##### Sector Development
Lower Sectors are young cosmic environments. They hold relatively few galaxies, and many of those galaxies are still early in their development. Set beside them, Victor's Mid-Level Sector is far further along. He treated the smaller Realities as newborns.[10]
[[The Universal Tree]] explains that this development belongs to a greater cycle of cosmic Life and Death. Stars and galaxies possess their own form of Life and eventually die; the energy released through their destruction contributes to the creation and development of new Galactic structures elsewhere. Even the death of a sufficiently immense Galaxy in the Higher Sectors can release enough energy to assist the creation of many smaller galaxies in weaker regions.[10]
This provides a biological and metaphysical component to Sector development beyond ordinary astronomy. Younger Lower-Sector galaxies require time to mature just as inhabited worlds and [[World Trees]] do.

##### Sector Influence and Anchoring
Powerful beings from Higher Sectors can manipulate where developing Sectors eventually emerge. They scatter fragments of their own power into smaller Realities, causing the affected Sector to gradually become aligned with the region selected by the higher power. When the Lower Sector eventually progresses, it therefore emerges near that faction rather than appearing unpredictably elsewhere.[10]
Victor copied this principle. The spheres sent to [[Nightingale]], Samar and the [[Magic]] World contained small fragments of himself. Their purpose was to saturate the three Lower Sectors with Victor's influence until he could draw those Realities toward the edge of his own Sector.[12][10]

##### Countless Galaxies
The count is all galaxies on the strategic map, built through Cosmic Consciousness and millions of World Tree connections.[5] Once he could touch the planets on that network directly, the same field is countless galaxies.[6]
The merger subsequently added the Galactic contents of three Lower Sectors. the smaller Realities contained comparatively few, younger galaxies, while After the merger the field still held countless galaxies surrounding Victor after the merger and shows him arranging individual galaxies and Galactic groups.[10][11]
"Countless" therefore remains the strongest canonical quantity. No exact diameter, radius, volume, number of galaxies, total star count or planet count has been given.
↑ Return to Sector [[Atlas]]

#### Pantheons and the Dimensional Void

##### Dimensional Layer
Pantheons within Victor's Sector are not ordinary planets or neighboring Galactic territories. They exist primarily as Divine dimensions connected through the Void between Dimensions, forming a supernatural layer of the same Sector distinct from conventional material space.
This distinction is directly demonstrated when Victor interacts with Divine territories. The rebuilt [[Olympus]] is treated as a dimension: after the destruction of the former Greek realm, the Akashic System analyzed, restored and expanded the dimensional structure before integrating Victor's newly created world into it.[3] During the annexation of the [[Indian Pantheon|Hindu Pantheon]], Victor approached through the Void between Dimensions before penetrating the Pantheon's defenses.[13]

Pantheons therefore belong to the Sector's complete cosmological structure even when they cannot be plotted as physical locations inside a Galaxy.

##### The Arcane Realm and the Magic World
The original Arcane Realm and the [[Magic]] World are related but should not be treated as the same original location. [[The Arcane Realm]] was the established dimensional homeland of the Witches. its researchers created a portal connecting their Realm to an entirely different inhabited world.[7]
That destination was the Magic World, which Victor initially perceived as an entirely different Universe and which later information identified as another weaker Sector.[7][8] The Witches subsequently became deeply involved with that world and eventually conquered and administered it.
Once the Witches ruled it, that Lower-Sector world is the Planet of the Witches. In the merger itself, Victor and the others call the third target Arcane. Arcane is the Magic World under Witch rule, not the original Arcane Realm from which the portal was first opened.[9][10][11]

##### Gods as Higher Existences
Gods are explicitly described as Higher Existences.[14] Unlike ordinary supernatural species whose abilities primarily operate through physical or energetic mechanisms, Gods possess Divinities associated with Concepts and Divine authority.
Pantheons should consequently not be understood merely as settlements where powerful individuals happen to live. They are dimensions structured around Divine civilization and Conceptual authority. Gods inhabit and rule them, while sufficiently powerful Divine authorities can create, reconstruct, expand or fundamentally alter their environments.

##### Conceptual Maintenance of Pantheons
The relationship between Gods and Pantheon Reality can become structural. A major example appears after [[Kronos]] loses control of [[Olympus]]: with the God governing Time removed, the Pantheon's temporal function becomes stagnant, leaving its Reality locked into the present rather than progressing normally through past, present and future.[15]
This does not mean every God universally maintains all aspects of Reality. Rather, Gods who embody foundational Concepts can directly regulate the functions associated with those Concepts inside the Divine structures under their jurisdiction.
A similar principle is demonstrated during the Empire's large-scale temporal project. [[Violet Elderblood Snow]]'s Divinity of Order is employed to ensure that Reality continues functioning correctly despite enormous distortions being imposed on Time.[16]

##### Earth's Pantheons
[[Yggdrasil]] historically possessed an extraordinary concentration of Divine civilizations. The Seven Great Pantheons included the Greek, Norse, Shinto, Egyptian, Hindu, Biblical and Chinese Pantheons.[17] Numerous smaller Divine territories and supernatural dimensions also existed.
Their presence helps explain why Earth was such an extreme anomaly compared with the three other developed World Tree civilizations observed by Victor. The planet was not merely technologically or biologically advanced; it was surrounded by a dense network of Gods, Pantheons, supernatural races, afterlives and Concept-bearing entities that greatly accelerated its effective developmental level.[18]
↑ Return to Sector [[Atlas]]

#### Geographic Framework

##### Initial Sector Survey
Victor's first broad geographic model came from that first survey. Before examining the entire Sector, he deliberately looked toward the Andromeda Galaxy and detected a planet containing primitive bacteria-like Life despite the apparent absence of a developed World Tree. He then expanded his perception throughout the surrounding Reality until reaching its barriers.[4]
The survey identified four principal developed sister-World-Tree civilizations in different directions. Earth occupied the Northern Region, with another developed World Tree civilization respectively toward the south, east and west.[4]
These cardinal designations describe the original pre-merger geography. They should not automatically be assumed to represent immutable astronomical coordinates once Victor began deliberately relocating galaxies and Galactic groups.

##### Northern Region
The Northern Region contains Earth, later renamed [[Yggdrasil]]. Among the four principal worlds initially examined, Earth was overwhelmingly the most developed. It possessed multiple Pantheons, Gods, Vampires, [[Werewolves]], Witches, Angels, Demons, Yokai, Progenitors and other extraordinary species or individuals.[4][18]
Victor concluded that Earth's abnormal development was effectively pushing the developmental classification of the wider Sector upward.

##### Southern Region
The Southern civilization consisted of grey-skinned humanoids organized as a hive-like society. Their reproduction involved cocoon-like structures, their society remained technologically primitive and Victor detected no Gods among them during the initial observation.[18]
This civilization should not automatically be identified with the [[Skaarith Empire]]. The later Skaarith civilization is specifically encountered in the southern region of the Andromeda Galaxy, which is a Galactic directional description rather than a confirmed identification with the Sector-wide Southern Region.[19]

##### Eastern Region
The Eastern civilization consisted of humanoid species descended from predator-like lifeforms, possessing scale-like skin and unusually long lifespans. Unlike the Southern and Western societies, they had already reached the space age and possessed powerful Gods. The strongest Divine presence detected by Victor was approximately comparable to a First-Generation Primordial God.[18]

##### Western Region
The Western civilization consisted of pale flying humanoids possessing enhanced regeneration, claws, teeth and black sclera. They were more socially developed than the Southern civilization but had not yet reached the Eastern civilization's space-faring technological level.[18]

##### Post-Merger Galactic Reorganization
The original cardinal framework ceased to represent the complete geography of Victor's Sector after the merger. When the galaxies had to be moved, Victor assumed his unrestricted Draconic form and expanded until his body exceeded the dimensions of a Galaxy. His wings covered entire regions of space while his tail extended among distant stars and systems.[11]
Victor then treated galaxies as movable astronomical structures. He extended one claw toward a spiral galaxy, enveloped it with his power and moved billions of stars simultaneously. Rather than allowing the movement to disrupt the Galaxy gravitationally, he preserved the structure throughout the journey: its Solar Systems remained in their orbits and its stars were not displaced by the relocation.[11]
Once Victor selected an appropriate destination, he released the Galaxy and checked its separation from the surrounding Galactic structures. He subsequently expanded the operation from single galaxies to entire groups of galaxies, directing each group toward different regions so they would remain separated and possess sufficient space for future development.[11]
The younger galaxies originating from the absorbed Lower Sectors received particular attention. Victor considered them underdeveloped compared with the mature structures of his Mid-Level Sector and deliberately placed them where they could develop without being endangered by denser Galactic regions.[10][11]

##### Protected Central Imperial Region
Victor gave special treatment to [[Nightingale]], Samar and the [[Magic]] World / Arcane. Nightingale and Samar possessed peculiarities that required them to remain within their existing Solar Systems. Victor therefore moved complete systems instead of extracting their planets individually.[11]
He relocated an inactive Solar System into one of the Empire's central protected regions and placed Nightingale's system there. A few hundred light-years away, he positioned Samar's system.[11]
The Magic World—called Arcane during this late period—could be moved more freely because its planet did not possess the same requirement to remain within its original Solar System. The exact distance between the Magic World and the other two worlds has not been stated.[11]
Victor selected the region specifically for defense. To reach Nightingale, Samar or the Magic World from the outside, an intruder would have to penetrate several Imperial checkpoints before reaching the central territory.[11]

#### World Tree Network
[[World Trees]] form one of the most important biological, metaphysical and infrastructural systems within Victor's Sector. World Trees are associated with living worlds and can connect material planets to higher-dimensional structures such as Pantheons, Paradises, Hells and supernatural Realms.
They are also part of a much larger system connected to the Universal Tree. the Universal Tree represents Life on a universal scale rather than merely biological organisms. His domain encompasses Life from microscopic matter through worlds, stars and immense Galactic structures.[10]
The four developed Trees found in the opening survey were only the initial known examples. As the [[Elderblood Empire]] expanded, the actual population proved vastly larger.

SECTOR SURVEYMillions of Connections→

##### Milky Way Expansion
With the Milky Way mapped, the Milky Way had been practically completely mapped. Imperial forces had gathered approximately 300 World Tree seedlings and identified another three more-developed [[World Trees]].[20] This immediately demonstrated that the four developed Trees from Victor's first survey did not represent the total number of World Trees existing within the Sector.

##### Millions of Sector-Wide Connections
After confronting evidence of the military capabilities possessed by Upper-Sector civilizations, Victor released his Cosmic Consciousness across his native Reality. His awareness reached the Sector's external barrier before stopping. Victor then called to the [[World Trees]] throughout the Sector and received millions of connections.[5]
Using the World Trees together with his Sector-scale awareness, he produced a strategic map containing every Galaxy belonging to his Sector. This network then became the basis for massive Imperial infrastructure, transportation and colonization.

##### Mars and the Unified Network
The World Tree system reached a new level once Mars became its heart. Rather than simply enlarging [[Yggdrasil]] further, Victor reconstructed Mars into a megaplanet intended to become the heart of the Empire. The world was designed to support trillions of inhabitants and was deliberately created without a pre-existing World Tree because the experiment Victor intended would have overloaded an ordinary planetary Tree.[6]
Victor instead used his connection to the [[World Trees]] under him. The Trees emerged through his power in the form of light and planted roots into Mars, including Yggdrasil itself. Their seedlings were connected through a central core, transforming Mars into the primary nexus of a unified World Tree Network.[6]
The effect was enormous. Transportation and communication between connected territories became virtually instantaneous across the wider cosmic domain. Before this system, even the [[Elderblood Empire]]'s advanced technology could require minutes for messages to cross distances separating remote galaxies; after the network was established, those delays were effectively removed.[6]
Victor then directly perceived his connection to planets throughout countless galaxies, confirming both the scale of his World Tree network and the vast Galactic extent of the Reality under his influence.[6]

##### The Universal Network of Life
The merger preparations expand the role of [[World Trees]] beyond Imperial infrastructure. [[The Universal Tree]] describes them as parts of a much larger network through which Life extends across the Universe. Individual World Trees function as localized nodes associated with worlds, while the Universal Tree remains connected to the greater process of Life itself.[12][10]
Victor's control represents only a small fraction of the total population. When he questioned the Universal Tree about the number of World Trees in his possession, the answer was that Victor controlled less than one percent of all World Trees throughout the greater Universe.[12]
This provides important context for the millions of connections previously observed inside Victor's Sector: millions are enormous from an Imperial perspective but remain a fraction of the World Tree network distributed throughout the greater Universe.

##### World Trees and the Younger Merged Galaxies
The merger also clarified why Lower Sectors are allowed to develop independently. Their galaxies are younger and still progressing through cosmic development. After Victor brought [[Nightingale]], Samar and the [[Magic]] World into the expanded Mid-Level Sector, the Universal Tree agreed to watch over the younger imported galaxies because they had been moved into their new environment extremely quickly and had not experienced the natural development time of Victor's original Galactic structures.[10][11]
Victor nevertheless did not rely solely upon the Universal Tree. After reorganizing the galaxies, he decided to assign his own people to monitor the younger regions as well.[11]
↑ Return to Sector [[Atlas]]

#### Major Galaxies

##### Milky Way
The Milky Way is the original Galactic heartland of the [[Elderblood Empire]] and contains [[Yggdrasil]], the Solar System and many of the earliest [[World Trees]] brought into Imperial administration. Once mapped, it had been practically completely mapped.[20]
The Galaxy later became the location of widespread infestations connected to the Hive, which had established itself across multiple Solar Systems. Victor ultimately exterminated the infestation before the Empire's expedition toward the Skaarith civilization.[21][22]

##### Andromeda
The Andromeda Galaxy is the first foreign Galaxy explicitly examined by Victor immediately before his full Sector survey. He observed primitive Life on one of its planets, with no developed World Tree in evidence.[4]
Later Imperial exploration encountered the [[Skaarith Empire]] within Andromeda's southern region. The Skaarith leadership displayed biology and Energy associated with the same hostile Hive influence previously discovered within the Milky Way, indicating interference by forces operating beyond the civilization itself.[19]

##### Sagittarius Dwarf Elliptical Galaxy
By approximately the 170,000th year of the accelerated Imperial era, Elderblood-controlled territory extended into the Sagittarius Dwarf Elliptical Galaxy. One Imperial world there lies approximately 80,000 light-years from [[Yggdrasil]]. That distance is not the radius of the Sector.[23]
This distance measures the location of one confirmed Imperial territory relative to Yggdrasil and should not be treated as the radius or diameter of the Sector.

##### Imported Lower-Sector Galaxies
The Lower Sectors of [[Nightingale]], Samar and the [[Magic]] World contributed additional Galactic structures when they were merged into Victor's Mid-Level Sector.[9][10]
Compared with Victor's mature Mid-Level Reality, those Sectors contained relatively few galaxies and many of those galaxies were still young. Their exact quantities, names and individual sizes have not been stated.[10]
Victor personally rearranged these imported structures after the merger. Individual galaxies were relocated and Galactic groups were separated into safer regions so the younger structures could continue developing without colliding with one another or with more mature Galactic formations.[11]

##### Countless Unnamed Galaxies
Most galaxies within Victor's Sector are unnamed. Every galaxy of the original Mid-Level Sector was on Victor's strategic map, and the World Tree Network already reached planets throughout countless galaxies before the merger.[5][6]
The same work again shows countless galaxies surrounding Victor after the merger and demonstrates that their geographic arrangement is no longer immutable. Victor can deliberately relocate individual galaxies or entire Galactic groups while keeping their internal astronomical systems stable.[11]
↑ Return to Sector [[Atlas]]

#### Civilizations
The Sector contains civilizations at dramatically different developmental stages. The four developed sister-World-Tree societies found beside [[Yggdrasil]] demonstrate that technological advancement, Divine development and social organization can vary substantially even within the same Sector.[18]
After the merger, the current population also includes civilizations that were historically native to separate Lower Sectors.

Incorporated into Victor's expanded Mid-Level Sector. Its planet could be relocated more freely than Nightingale and Samar.[7][8][9][10][11]
By the merger, the Magic World had changed dramatically under Witch administration. Magical blood had spread through its population, Demigods existed among its people and magical technology had become widespread. The world is described as the Planet of the Witches, establishing why the merger chapters subsequently use Arcane when referring to the Lower Sector.[9]
The populations of the three Lower Sectors were already allied with or incorporated politically into the Elderblood system before the physical merger. What changed in the merger was therefore cosmological rather than merely political: the separate Realities themselves were brought inside the same expanded Mid-Level Sector.
↑ Return to Sector [[Atlas]]

#### Elderblood Dominion

##### Formation of the Empire
After Victor unified the major supernatural powers of Earth, the planet was renamed [[Yggdrasil]] and the [[Elderblood Empire]] was formally established.[24]
On the seventh day of the first Imperial year, Victor became recognized as the Overlord of his native Sector.[25]
The title means an Overlord is an individual who completely controls their Sector. It is not itself a separate species, Divine Concept or fixed combat tier. Velnorah once possessed the title in relation to her own Sector, while Victor now holds complete control over his own.[10]
Victor's personal power and his Overlord status should therefore remain conceptually separate. His strength allows him to enforce his control, but the title describes the relationship between the ruler and the Sector rather than granting the ruler a standardized quantity of power.

##### From Planetary Empire to Cosmic Civilization

Victor knew the structure of his original Sector at the Galactic level, but mapping a Galaxy did not automatically mean that every planet inside it possessed a permanent Imperial government or population.[5]
Once galaxies could be moved, another distinction had become necessary: Victor could physically reposition a Galaxy, Solar System or planet as part of Imperial planning regardless of whether every world inside that structure was inhabited.
